q.p: Adapting an Arthur C. Clarke novel, this Peter Hyams-directed sequel follows astronauts probing what doomed the Discovery One near Jupiter — which movie?
q.e: 2010: The Year We Make Contact (or simply 2010) is a 1984 American science fiction film written, produced, shot, and directed by Peter Hyams.

q.p: Based on the true story of the MIT Blackjack Team, this 2008 heist drama starred Jim Sturgess and Kevin Spacey and topped the U.S. box office on release — what film is it?
q.e: 21 (2008 film) is a 2008 American heist drama film directed by Robert Luketic and distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing.

q.p: Sean Penn plays a dying mathematician and Benicio Del Toro a born-again ex-convict in this nonlinear 2003 thriller about the fallout from a hit-and-run — which film?
q.e: 21 Grams is a 2003 American crime thriller film co-produced and directed by Alejandro Gonzlez Irritu and written by Guillermo Arriaga.

q.p: This Fox police drama about youthful undercover officers ran 103 episodes from 1987 to 1991, with its final season airing in first-run syndication — which series?
q.e: 21 Jump Street is an American police procedural drama television series created by Patrick Hasburgh and Stephen J. Cannell for the Fox Broadcasting Company.

q.p: Directed once again by Phil Lord and Christopher Miller, this follow-up to a 2012 cop comedy sends its two leads undercover on a college campus — which movie?
o: Good Luck to You, Leo Grande
q.e: 22 Jump Street is a 2014 American buddy cop action comedy film directed by Phil Lord and Christopher Miller, written by Jonah Hill, Michael Bacall, Oren Uziel and Rodney Rothman and produced by and starring Hill and Channing Tatum.

q.p: This Fox action drama unfolds in real time, each season spanning a single 24-hour stretch punctuated by split screens and a ticking digital clock — what is it?
q.e: 24 (TV series) is an American action drama television series created by Joel Surnow and Robert Cochran for Fox.

q.p: Directed by Anne Fletcher and starring Katherine Heigl, this 2008 romantic comedy follows a perpetual bridesmaid whose sister steals the spotlight — which film?
q.e: 27 Dresses is a 2008 American romantic comedy film directed by Anne Fletcher and written by Aline Brosh McKenna.

q.p: Set six months after a Rage Virus outbreak, this 2007 horror sequel follows US-led NATO forces trying to establish a safe zone in a devastated London — what is the film's title?
q.e: 28 Weeks Later is a 2007 post-apocalyptic action horror film directed by Juan Carlos Fresnadillo, who co-wrote it with Rowan Joff, Enrique Lpez Lavigne, and Jess Olmo.

q.p: This 2013 German drama film dramatizes the true story of a 10-year-old girl held captive by her kidnapper for eight years — what is it?
q.e: 3096 Days is a 2013 German drama film directed by Sherry Hormann.

q.p: Created by Tina Fey and drawn from her years as head writer at SNL, this satirical sitcom is named for the Manhattan address where NBC's studios sit — which show is it?
q.e: 30 Rock is an American satirical surrealist sitcom television series created by Tina Fey that originally aired on NBC from October 11, 2006, to January 31, 2013.

q.p: This 2020 Polish erotic thriller about a Warsaw woman held captive by a Sicilian man earned a rare 0% on Rotten Tomatoes before becoming a Netflix sensation — what is it?
o: Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani

q.p: Chadwick Boseman starred as Jackie Robinson in this 2013 biopic, its title taken from a jersey number retired across all of Major League Baseball in 1997 — which movie?
q.e: 42 (film) is a 2013 American biographical sports drama film produced by Legendary Pictures and distributed by Warner Bros.

q.p: Kida Khodr Ramadan stars as a Berlin drug-cartel boss trying to go straight in this German drama that premiered on TNT Serie in 2017 — which show?
q.e: 4 Blocks is a German drama series. The first season premiered on German pay television channel TNT Serie on May 8, 2017.

q.p: This 2009 romantic dramedy tells its story of a breakup entirely out of chronological order, starring Joseph Gordon-Levitt and Zooey Deschanel — what is it?
q.e: 500 Days of Summer is a 2009 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Marc Webb in his feature directorial debut, written by Scott Neustadter and Michael H. Weber.

q.p: A marine veterinarian keeps wooing the same amnesiac art teacher from scratch every morning in this 2004 Adam Sandler-Drew Barrymore rom-com — what film is it?
q.e: 50 First Dates is a 2004 American romantic comedy film directed by Peter Segal and starring Adam Sandler and Drew Barrymore, with Rob Schneider, Sean Astin, Lusia Strus, Blake Clark, and Dan Aykroyd in supporting roles.

q.p: Based on the short story 'Fallen Angel' by E. C. Tubb, this 2023 science-fiction thriller pairs Josh Hutcherson with Morgan Freeman. What is this film called?
q.e: 57 Seconds is a 2023 American science fiction thriller film directed by Rusty Cundieff, written by Cundieff and Macon Blair, and starring Josh Hutcherson and Morgan Freeman.

q.p: Adam Driver plays an ancient astronaut who crash-lands on a hostile planet — which turns out to be prehistoric Earth — in this 2023 sci-fi film produced by Sam Raimi. What is it?

q.p: In this 2019 Michael Bay action film, a group who fake their own deaths form a vigilante team to overthrow a ruthless dictator — what film is it?
q.e: 6 Underground (film) is a 2019 American action film directed by Michael Bay and written by Paul Wernick and Rhett Reese.

q.p: Marking Eminem's feature film debut, this 2002 hip-hop drama follows a Detroit rapper trying to break into a genre dominated by Black artists — name the film?
q.e: 8 Mile (film) is a 2002 American hip-hop biographical drama film produced and directed by Curtis Hanson from a script written by Scott Silver.

q.p: A Fox spin-off of a first-responder drama, this Ryan Murphy series ran from 2020 to 2025 and wrapped up its fifth and final season in early 2025 — which show?
q.e: 9-1-1: Lone Star is an American procedural drama television series that aired on Fox from January 19, 2020, to February 3, 2025.

q.p: Born in 1988, this British presenter fronted Channel 4's Married at First Sight: Afters in 2021 and now co-hosts ITV2's Big Brother alongside Will Best — who is she?

q.p: Directed by Marielle Heller, this 2019 drama stars Matthew Rhys as a journalist profiling TV icon Fred Rogers for Esquire — which film?
o: A Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood

q.e: A Clockwork Orange (film) is a 1971 dystopian crime film written, produced, and directed by Stanley Kubrick.

q.p: Adapted from a play called The Talking Cure, this David Cronenberg film stars Viggo Mortensen as Sigmund Freud opposite Michael Fassbender's Carl Jung — which 2011 film?

q.p: Aaron Sorkin adapted his own 1989 play into this Rob Reiner legal drama about the court-martial of two Marines, starring Tom Cruise and Jack Nicholson — which film?

q.p: This 1988 British comedy earned a $188 million worldwide gross and was later ranked the 39th-greatest British film of the 20th century by the BFI — which movie?
q.e: A Fish Called Wanda is a 1988 heist comedy film directed by Charles Crichton and written by John Cleese from a story conceived by Cleese and Crichton.

q.p: Set during Korea's Goryeo Dynasty and loosely inspired by a 14th-century king's reign, this controversial 2008 erotic thriller sold nearly 3.8 million tickets — which film?
q.e: A Frozen Flower is a 2008 South Korean historical erotic thriller film.

q.p: Despite becoming a box-office bomb, this Ridley Scott-directed film about a broker inheriting a French vineyard was nominated for a Critics' Choice Award — which movie?
q.e: A Good Year is a 2006 romantic comedy-drama film directed and produced by Ridley Scott, based on the 2004 novel by Peter Mayle.

q.p: In this Cronenberg thriller, a diner owner becomes an unlikely local hero after foiling a robbery, forcing him to confront enemies from his past. What film is it?
q.e: A History of Violence is a 2005 action thriller film directed by David Cronenberg and written by Josh Olson.

q.p: Starring Choi Woo-shik as a man on the run after accidentally offing a serial murderer, this 2024 Korean dark comedy thriller premiered on Netflix — which series?
q.e: A Killer Paradox (stylized with a red O or ieung) is a 2024 South Korean crime thriller dark comedy television series written by Kim Da-min, directed by Lee Chang-hee, and starring Choi Woo-shik, Son Suk-ku, and Lee Hee-joon.

q.p: Tom Hanks and his real-life son co-star in this 2022 dramedy about a grumpy widower drawn into his neighbors' lives, a remake of a Swedish film — name it?
q.e: A Man Called Otto is a 2022 American comedy-drama film directed by Marc Forster from a screenplay by David Magee.

q.p: Based on a 2012 Swedish bestseller, this 2015 comedy-drama was nominated for Best Foreign Language Film and Best Makeup at the Oscars — what film is it?
q.e: A Man Called Ove (film) is a 2015 Swedish comedy-drama film written and directed by Hannes Holm and based on the 2012 novel of the same name by Fredrik Backman.

q.p: Created by DJ Nash for ABC, this ensemble family drama starring David Giuntoli and Grace Park ran for five seasons and 87 episodes from 2018 to 2023 — what show is it?
q.e: A Million Little Things is an American family drama television series created by DJ Nash for ABC.

q.p: Michael Peña plays a Mexican-American astronaut in this 2023 biographical drama based on the real-life figure's memoir "Reaching for the Stars" — which film?
q.e: A Million Miles Away (film) is a 2023 American biographical drama film detailing the life of José M. Hernández, a Mexican-American astronaut, who is played by Michael Peña.

q.p: In this 2018 post-apocalyptic horror film, a family struggles to stay silent against extraterrestrials with an acute sense of hearing — which movie?

q.p: Emily Blunt's family returns to face the blind, sound-hunting aliens in this 2020 Krasinski-directed sequel, joined by Cillian Murphy. Which film is it?
q.e: A Quiet Place Part II is a 2020 American post-apocalyptic horror film written, directed, and co-produced by John Krasinski.

q.p: Set in 1967 and directed by the Coen brothers, this Oscar-nominated dark comedy follows a Minnesota professor whose life unravels as he questions his faith — which film?

q.p: Based on a real German journalist's efforts to expose a 1980 crackdown in Gwangju, this South Korean drama stars Song Kang-ho as the ordinary cabbie who helped him — which film?

q.p: Based on a John Grisham novel, this 1996 legal drama marked Octavia Spencer's film debut and was the second of two Grisham adaptations directed by the same filmmaker — what is it?

q.e: A Time to Kill (1996 film) is a 1996 American legal drama film based on John Grisham's 1989 novel of the same name.

q.p: Starring Keanu Reeves in a US-Mexico co-production, this 1995 romance was an English remake of a 1942 Italian film and grossed $91 million despite mixed reviews — which movie?
q.e: A Walk in the Clouds is a 1995 period romantic drama film directed by Alfonso Arau and starring Keanu Reeves, Aitana Snchez-Gijn, Giancarlo Giannini, Anglica Aragn, Evangelina Elizondo, Debra Messing and Anthony Quinn.

q.p: Dubbed 'Mr. Perfectionist,' this Indian actor first appeared on screen as a child in his uncle Nasir Hussain's films and later won four National Film Awards — who is he?

q.p: Starring Park Bo-young and Ahn Hyo-seop, this 2019 South Korean drama aired on tvN's Monday-Tuesday primetime slot — which series?

q.p: This visual-novel adventure game franchise from Capcom, styled after courtroom legal dramas, began in 2001 with a title starring a rookie defense lawyer — name the franchise?

q.p: Born in 1985, this Australian actor played August Walker on the series UnREAL and Brad on the Netflix series Sex/Life — who is he?

q.p: Best known as Eric Delko on a Miami-set crime drama, this actor now portrays Agent Luke Alvez on Criminal Minds — who is he?

q.p: Born in 1991, this actress played Colleen Lunsford in Little Sister and Sasha Bingham on Californication — who is she?

q.p: This British actor won a BAFTA TV Award for Best Actor for the 2016 drama Murdered by My Father, and later earned an Emmy for his role in the series Sweet Tooth — who is he?

q.e: Aditi Rao Hydari (born 28 October 1978) is an Indian actress who appears in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam films.

q.e: Aditi Shankar (born 6 July 1997) is an Indian actress and singer known for her work majorly in Tamil cinema.

q.p: Now chairman of Yash Raj Films and India's top-grossing producer ever, he was once denied a spot at the National School of Drama because of his stammer — who is he?
q.e: Aditya Chopra (born 21 May 1971) is an Indian film director, producer, and studio executive who works in Hindi Cinema.

q.p: A former lyricist turned filmmaker, he won the National Film Award for Best Direction with his debut about a 2016 surgical strike — who is this Hindi-cinema director?
q.e: Aditya Dhar (born 12 March 1983) is an Indian film director, screenwriter and producer who works in Hindi cinema.

q.e: Aditya Singh Rajput (19 August 1990 - 22 May 2023) was an Indian television actor, who did various TV commercials and roles in Hindi television shows and Bollywood films.

q.p: This American actress played Dorothy Gale in a dark Oz adaptation, Anathema Device in Good Omens, and Bix Caleen in the Star Wars series Andor — who is she?

q.p: This American actress had film turns in Red Dawn, G.I. Joe: Retaliation, and John Wick, but is best known for TV roles on Friday Night Lights and The Orville; who is she?

q.p: This French actress became the youngest ever winner of the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 2013, sharing the honor with her co-star for a coming-of-age romance — who is she?

q.p: Produced for an Iranian broadcaster and created by Saeed Soltani, this drama is set in the early years of the Pahlavi era — which show?
q.e: After the Rain (TV series) is an Iranian television series produced for IRIB TV3 created by Saeed Soltani.

q.p: Starring Lee Bo-young and Son Na-eun, this 2023 JTBC drama became one of the highest-rated shows in cable television history — what's it called?

q.p: This Russian-Israeli actress won the Golden Eagle Award in 2019 for her leading role as Nadya Lapshina in the romantic drama 'Ice' — who is she?

q.e: Ahn Bo-hyun (born May 16, 1988) is a South Korean actor, model, and television personality.

q.e: Škoda Auto: Czech Republic. The operating profit was €1.6 billion in 2017, an increase of 34.6% over the previous year.

q.p: In which country is Post-Soviet states?
q.e: Post-Soviet states: Estonia. Prior to their independence, they existed as Union Republics, which were the top-level constituents of the Soviet Union.

q.p: In which country is Special wards of Tokyo?
q.e: Special wards of Tokyo: Japan. The 23 special wards (特別区, tokubetsu-ku) of Tokyo are a unique form of municipality under Japan's 1947 Local Autonomy Law.

q.p: In which country is Blue (English group) based?
q.e: Blue (English group): United Kingdom. Blue are an English boy band consisting of members Simon Webbe, Duncan James, Antony Costa, and Lee Ryan.

q.p: In which country is Bhimbetka rock shelters?
q.e: Bhimbetka rock shelters: India. The Bhimbetka rock shelters are an archaeological site in central India that spans the Paleolithic and Mesolithic periods, as well as the historic period.

q.p: In which country is Revolution of April 19, 1810?
q.e: Revolution of April 19, 1810: Venezuela. It is conventionally noted as the beginning of the country's struggle for independence.

q.p: In which country are the South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands?
q.e: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands: United Kingdom. South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands (SGSSI) is a British Overseas Territory in the southern Atlantic Ocean.

q.p: In which country is Cortina d'Ampezzo?
q.e: Cortina d'Ampezzo: Italy. It is part of the linguistic and cultural region of Ladinia.

q.p: In which country is Mausoleum at Halicarnassus?
q.e: Mausoleum at Halicarnassus: Turkey. The structure was designed by the Greek architects Satyros of Paros and Pythius of Priene.

q.p: In which country is 51st state?
q.e: 51st state: United States. "51st state" is a phrase used in the United States to refer to the idea of adding an additional state to the current 50-state nation.

q.p: In which country are the Saipan, Northern Mariana Islands?
q.e: Saipan, Northern Mariana Islands: United States. Saipan is the largest island and capital of the Northern Mariana Islands, an unincorporated territory of the United States in the western Pacific Ocean.

q.p: In which country is Nordic countries?
q.e: Nordic countries: Sweden. The Nordic countries have much in common in their way of life, history, religion and social and economic model.

q.p: In which country is Łódź Voivodeship?
q.e: Łódź Voivodeship: Poland. Łódź Voivodeship (Polish: województwo łódzkie [vɔjɛˈvut͡stfɔ ˈwut͡skʲɛ]) is a voivodeship (province) of Poland.

q.p: In which country is Iron pillar of Delhi?
q.e: Iron pillar of Delhi: India. The metals used in its construction have a rust-resistant composition.

q.p: In which country is Delhi–Mumbai Expressway?
q.e: Delhi–Mumbai Expressway: India. Delhi–Mumbai Expressway connects the Sohna Elevated Corridor, Gurugram to the Jawaharlal Nehru Port in Navi Mumbai via Dausa, Kota, Ratlam, Vadodara and Surat.

q.p: In which country is Felipe Ángeles International Airport based?
q.e: Felipe Ángeles International Airport: Mexico. Apart from civilian operations, the airport accommodates the Mexican Air Force, general aviation, and charter flight services.

q.p: In which country was Łódź?
q.e: Łódź: Poland. Łódź is a city in central Poland and a former industrial centre.

q.p: In which country is Mount Edziza volcanic complex?
q.e: Mount Edziza volcanic complex: Canada. The Mount Edziza volcanic complex ( əd-ZY-zə; abbreviated MEVC) is a group of volcanoes and associated lava flows in northwestern British Columbia, Canada.

q.p: In which country is Huey Lewis and the News based?
q.e: Huey Lewis and the News: United States. Huey Lewis and the News (formerly known as Huey Lewis & The American Express) are an American rock band based in San Francisco, California.

q.p: In which country is Pull&Bear based?
q.e: Pull&Bear: Spain. Pull&Bear is a Spanish clothing and accessories retailer based in Narón, A Coruña, Spain, founded in 1991.

q.p: In which country is Merdeka 118?
q.e: Merdeka 118: Malaysia. Merdeka 118, formerly known as Menara Warisan Merdeka, KL 118, and PNB 118, is a 118-story megatall skyscraper in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

q.p: In which country is Badarian culture?
q.e: Badarian culture: Egypt. The Badarian culture provides the earliest direct evidence of agriculture in Upper Egypt during the Predynastic Era.

q.p: In which country is Carnac stones?
q.e: Carnac stones: France. The stones were erected at some stage during the Neolithic period, probably around 3300 BC, but some may date to as early as 4500 BC.

q.p: In which country is Glass Beach (Fort Bragg, California)?
q.e: Glass Beach (Fort Bragg, California): United States.

q.p: In which country is İşbank based?
q.e: İşbank: Turkey. İşbank, officially Türkiye İş Bankası, is a commercial bank in Turkey.

q.p: Which of these is an official language of Gabon?
q.e: Gabon: French. It has an area of 270,000 square kilometres (100,000 sq mi) and a population of 2.3 million people.

q.p: Which of these is an official language of São Tomé and Príncipe?
q.e: São Tomé and Príncipe: Portuguese. The islands were uninhabited until Portuguese explorers João de Santarém and Pedro Escobar became the first to discover them on 21 December 1470.

q.p: Which of these is an official language of the Seychelles?
q.e: Seychelles: French. Its capital and largest city, Victoria, is 1,500 kilometres (800 nautical miles) east of mainland Africa.

q.p: Which of these is an official language of Georgetown, Guyana?
q.e: Georgetown, Guyana: English. It is situated in Demerara-Mahaica, region 4, on the Atlantic Ocean coast, at the mouth of the Demerara River.

q.p: Which of these was an official language of the Holy Roman Empire?
q.e: Holy Roman Empire: Latin. It developed in the Early Middle Ages (beginning in either 800 or 962), and lasted for a millennium until its dissolution in 1806 during the Napoleonic Wars.

q.p: Which of these is an official language of the Heard Island and McDonald Islands?
q.e: Heard Island and McDonald Islands: English. The Territory of Heard Island and McDonald Islands is an Australian external territory in the southern Indian Ocean.

q.p: Which of these was an official language of Circassia?
q.e: Circassia: Circassian. Circassia ( sir-KASH-ə), also known as Zichia, was a country and a historical region in Eastern Europe.

q.p: Which of these is an official language of Alsace–Lorraine?
q.e: Alsace–Lorraine: German. It was established in 1871 by the German Empire after it had occupied the region during the Franco-Prussian War.

q.p: Which of these is an official language of Republic of Crimea (Russia)?
q.e: Republic of Crimea (Russia): Russian. The Republic of Crimea is a republic of Russia, comprising most of the Crimean Peninsula, but excluding Sevastopol.

q.p: Which of these was an official language of United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland?
q.e: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland: English. The 19th century was an era of Industrial Revolution, and growth of trade and finance, in which Britain largely dominated the world economy.

q.p: Which of these is an official language of the South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands?
q.e: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands: English. South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands (SGSSI) is a British Overseas Territory in the southern Atlantic Ocean.

q.p: Which of these is an official language of Cyprus (island)?
q.e: Cyprus (island): Greek. Cyprus is an island in the Eastern Basin of the Mediterranean Sea.

q.p: Which of these is an official language of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines?
q.e: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: English. Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, sometimes known simply as Saint Vincent, is an archipelagic country in the eastern Caribbean.

q.p: Which of these was an official language of Beiyang government?
q.e: Beiyang government: Mandarin. It was dominated by Yuan Shikai and the other generals of his Beiyang Army, hence the name.

q.p: Which of these is an official language of Qing dynasty?
q.e: Qing dynasty: Manchu. The last imperial dynasty in Chinese history, the Qing dynasty was preceded by the Ming dynasty and succeeded by the Republic of China.

q.p: Which of these was an official language of French protectorate in Morocco?
q.e: French protectorate in Morocco: Moroccan Arabic. The protectorate lasted until after World War II with the dissolution of the Treaty of Fez on 2 March 1956, with the Franco-Moroccan Joint Declaration.

q.p: Who is credited with discovering Sierra Leone?
q.e: Sierra Leone: Pedro de Sintra. Sierra Leone, officially the Republic of Sierra Leone, is a country on the west coast of West Africa.

q.p: Who is credited with discovering Far side of the Moon?
q.e: Far side of the Moon: Luna 3. The far side has sometimes been called the "dark side of the Moon", where "dark" means "unseen" instead of "unilluminated".

q.p: Of which country is Libreville the capital?
q.e: Libreville is the capital of Gabon. It has an area of 270,000 square kilometres (100,000 sq mi) and a population of 2.3 million people.

q.p: Of which country is Frankfurt am Main the capital?
q.e: Frankfurt am Main is the capital of East Francia.

q.p: Of which country is Washington, D.C. the capital?
q.e: Washington, D.C. is the capital of United States. The United States of America (USA), also known as the United States (U.S.) or America, is a country primarily located in North America.

q.p: Of which country is Malagasy an official language?
q.e: Malagasy is an official language of Madagascar. Its capital and largest city is Antananarivo.

q.p: Which country uses the dalasi as its official currency?
q.e: The dalasi is the official currency of The Gambia. The Gambia, officially the Republic of The Gambia, is a country in West Africa.

q.p: Which country uses the loti as its official currency?
q.e: The loti is the official currency of Lesotho. Lesotho (lih-SOO-too; Sotho pronunciation: [lɪˈsʊːtʰʊ]), officially the Kingdom of Lesotho, is a landlocked country in Southern Africa.

q.p: Which country uses the ariary as its official currency?
q.e: The ariary is the official currency of Madagascar. Its capital and largest city is Antananarivo.

q.p: Which country uses the Mauritian rupee as its official currency?
q.e: The Mauritian rupee is the official currency of Mauritius. It includes the main island (also called Mauritius), as well as Rodrigues, Agaléga, and St.

q.p: Which country uses the Moroccan dirham as its official currency?
q.e: The Moroccan dirham is the official currency of Morocco. Morocco, officially the Kingdom of Morocco, is a country in the Maghreb region of North Africa.

q.p: Which country uses the Mozambican metical as its official currency?
q.e: The Mozambican metical is the official currency of Mozambique. The sovereign state is separated from the Comoros, Mayotte, and Madagascar through the Mozambique Channel to the east.

q.p: Which country uses the naira as its official currency?
q.e: The naira is the official currency of Nigeria. It covers an area of 923,769 square kilometres (356,669 mi2).

q.p: Which country uses the Somali shilling as its official currency?
q.e: The Somali shilling is the official currency of Somalia. Somalia, officially the Federal Republic of Somalia, is the easternmost country in continental Africa.

q.p: Which country uses the lilangeni as its official currency?
q.e: The lilangeni is the official currency of Eswatini. It is bordered by South Africa on all sides except the east, where it shares a border with Mozambique.

q.p: Which country uses the bir as its official currency?
q.e: The bir is the official currency of Ethiopia. Ethiopia, officially the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (FDRE), is a landlocked country located in the Horn of Africa region of East Africa.

q.p: Which country uses the ducat as its official currency?
q.e: The ducat is the official currency of Holy Roman Empire. It developed in the Early Middle Ages (beginning in either 800 or 962), and lasted for a millennium until its dissolution in 1806 during the Napoleonic Wars.

q.p: Which country uses the thaler as its official currency?
q.e: The thaler is the official currency of Austrian Empire. It remained part of the Holy Roman Empire until the latter's dissolution in 1806.

q.p: Which country uses the renminbi as its official currency?
q.e: The renminbi is the official currency of China. China, officially the People's Republic of China (PRC), is a country in East Asia.

q.p: Which country uses the florin as its official currency?
q.e: The florin is the official currency of Republic of Florence. The Florentines formed a commune in Rabodo's (Matilda's successor) successors' place.

q.p: Which country uses the solidus as its official currency?
q.e: The solidus is the official currency of East Francia.

q.p: Which country uses the Canadian dollar as its official currency?
q.e: The Canadian dollar is the official currency of Canada. Its border with the United States is the longest international land border.

q.p: Which country uses the yen as its official currency?
q.e: The yen is the official currency of Japan. The Japanese archipelago consists of four major islands alongside 14,121 smaller islands.

q.p: Which country uses the Italian lira as its official currency?
q.e: The Italian lira is the official currency of Kingdom of Italy. The kingdom was established through the unification of several states over a decades-long process, called the Risorgimento.

q.p: Which country uses the piastre as its official currency?
q.e: The piastre is the official currency of Gran Colombia. International recognition of the legitimacy of the Gran Colombian state ran afoul of European opposition to the independence of states in the Americas.

q.p: Which country uses the Norwegian krone as its official currency?
q.e: The Norwegian krone is the official currency of Norway. Norway has a population of approximately 5.6 million, and a total area of 385,207 square kilometres (148,729 sq mi).

q.p: Which country uses the hryvnia as its official currency?
q.e: The hryvnia is the official currency of Ukraine. It is the second-largest country in Europe after Russia, which borders it to the east and northeast.

q.p: Which country uses the Slovak koruna as its official currency?
q.e: The Slovak koruna is the official currency of Slovakia. Slovakia, officially the Slovak Republic, is a landlocked country in Central Europe.

q.p: Which country uses the Polish rubel as its official currency?
q.e: The Polish rubel is the official currency of Congress Poland. It was established when the French ceded a part of Polish territory to the Russian Empire following France's defeat in the Napoleonic Wars.

q.p: Which country uses the convertible mark as its official currency?
q.e: The convertible mark is the official currency of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Bosnia and Herzegovina, often referred to as Bosnia-Herzegovina or simply Bosnia, is a country in Southeast Europe.

q.p: Which country uses the rupiah as its official currency?
q.e: The rupiah is the official currency of Indonesia. Indonesia, officially the Republic of Indonesia, is a country in Southeast Asia and Oceania, between the Indian and Pacific oceans.

q.p: Which country uses the Caribbean guilder as its official currency?
q.e: The Caribbean guilder is the official currency of Curaçao. Curaçao, officially the Country of Curaçao, is a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

q.p: Which country uses the rand as its official currency?
q.e: The rand is the official currency of South Africa. South Africa, officially the Republic of South Africa (RSA), is the southernmost country in Africa.

q.p: Which country uses the Uzbek som as its official currency?
q.e: The Uzbek som is the official currency of Uzbekistan. Uzbekistan, officially the Republic of Uzbekistan, is a doubly landlocked country located in Central Asia.

q.p: Which country uses the Irish pound as its official currency?
q.e: The Irish pound is the official currency of Republic of Ireland. Ireland (Irish: Éire [ˈeːɾʲə]), also known as the Republic of Ireland (Poblacht na hÉireann), is a country in Northwestern Europe.

q.p: Which country uses the forint as its official currency?
q.e: The forint is the official currency of Hungary. Hungary lies within the Danube River's drainage basin, and is dominated by great lowland plains.

q.p: Which country uses the Austro-Hungarian gulden as its official currency?
q.e: The Austro-Hungarian gulden is the official currency of Austria-Hungary. It was dissolved shortly after Hungary terminated the union with Austria in 1918 at the end of World War I.

q.p: Which country uses the Swedish krona as its official currency?
q.e: The Swedish krona is the official currency of Sweden. Sweden, formally the Kingdom of Sweden, is a Nordic country located on the Scandinavian Peninsula in Northern Europe.

q.p: Which country uses the gold rouble as its official currency?
q.e: The gold rouble is the official currency of Russian Empire. It also colonized Alaska between 1799 and 1867.

q.p: Which country uses the złoty as its official currency?
q.e: The złoty is the official currency of Poland. Poland, officially the Republic of Poland, is a country in Central Europe.

q.p: Which country uses the peso moneda nacional as its official currency?
q.e: The peso moneda nacional is the official currency of Argentina. Argentina, officially the Argentine Republic, is a country in the southern cone of South America.

q.p: Which country uses the Nuevo sol as its official currency?
q.e: The Nuevo sol is the official currency of Peru. Peru, officially the Republic of Peru, is a country in western South America.

q.p: Which country uses the riel as its official currency?
q.e: The riel is the official currency of Cambodia. Cambodia, officially the Kingdom of Cambodia, is a country in Mainland Southeast Asia.

q.p: Which country uses the kina as its official currency?
q.e: The kina is the official currency of Papua New Guinea. It has a land border with Indonesia to the west and maritime borders with Australia to the south and the Solomon Islands to the east.

q.p: Which country uses the French livre as its official currency?
q.e: The French livre is the official currency of Kingdom of France. The Kingdom of France is the historiographical name or umbrella term given to various political entities of France in the medieval and early modern period.

q.p: Which country uses the bolívar as its official currency?
q.e: The bolívar is the official currency of Venezuela. It comprises an area of 912,050 km2 (352,140 sq mi), with a population estimated at 31.8 million in 2025.

q.p: Which country uses the quetzal as its official currency?
q.e: The quetzal is the official currency of Guatemala. Guatemala, officially the Republic of Guatemala, is a country in northern Central America.

q.p: Which country uses the Honduran lempira as its official currency?
q.e: The Honduran lempira is the official currency of Honduras. Honduras, officially the Republic of Honduras, is a country in Central America.

q.p: Which country uses the gourde as its official currency?
q.e: The gourde is the official currency of Haiti. It occupies the western side of the island, which it shares with the Dominican Republic.

q.p: Which country uses the new shekel as its official currency?
q.e: The new shekel is the official currency of Israel. Israel, officially the State of Israel, is a country in the Southern Levant region of West Asia.

q.p: Which country uses the Chinese yuan as its official currency?
q.e: The Chinese yuan is the official currency of Beiyang government. It was dominated by Yuan Shikai and the other generals of his Beiyang Army, hence the name.

q.p: Which country uses the Lao kip as its official currency?
q.e: The Lao kip is the official currency of Laos. Laos, officially the Lao People's Democratic Republic (LPDR), is a country in Mainland Southeast Asia, and the only landlocked country in Southeast Asia.

q.p: Which country uses the Maldivian rufiyaa as its official currency?
q.e: The Maldivian rufiyaa is the official currency of Maldives. The Maldives is located southwest of India and Sri Lanka, about 750 kilometres (470 miles; 400 nautical miles) from the Asian continent's mainland.

q.p: Which country uses the kyat as its official currency?
q.e: The kyat is the official currency of Myanmar. It is the largest country by area in Mainland Southeast Asia and has a population of about 55 million.

q.p: Which country uses the baht as its official currency?
q.e: The baht is the official currency of Thailand. Thailand, officially the Kingdom of Thailand, and formerly known as Siam until 1939, is a country located in Mainland Southeast Asia.

q.p: Which country uses the tael as its official currency?
o: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
q.e: The tael is the official currency of Qing dynasty. The last imperial dynasty in Chinese history, the Qing dynasty was preceded by the Ming dynasty and succeeded by the Republic of China.

q.p: Which country uses the won as its official currency?
q.e: The won is the official currency of South Korea. South Korea, officially the Republic of Korea (ROK), is a country in East Asia.

q.p: Which country uses the afghani as its official currency?
q.e: The afghani is the official currency of Afghanistan. Afghanistan, officially the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan, is a landlocked country located at the crossroads of Central and South Asia.

q.p: Which country uses the Moroccan franc as its official currency?
q.e: The Moroccan franc is the official currency of French protectorate in Morocco. The protectorate lasted until after World War II with the dissolution of the Treaty of Fez on 2 March 1956, with the Franco-Moroccan Joint Declaration.

q.p: Which country uses the kwanza as its official currency?
q.e: The kwanza is the official currency of Angola. Angola, officially the Republic of Angola, is a country on the western coast of Southern Africa.

q.p: Which country uses the ngultrum as its official currency?
q.e: The ngultrum is the official currency of Bhutan. With a population of over 800,000 (800,871) and a territory of 38,394 square kilometres (14,824 sq mi), Bhutan ranks 133rd in land area and 160th in population.

q.p: Which country uses the Philippine peso as its official currency?
q.e: The Philippine peso is the official currency of Philippines. The Philippines, officially the Republic of the Philippines, is an archipelagic country in Southeast Asia.

q.p: Which country uses the peso as its official currency?
q.e: The peso is the official currency of Mexico. Mexico, officially the United Mexican States, is a country in North America.

q.p: Which country uses the nakfa as its official currency?
q.e: The nakfa is the official currency of Eritrea. Eritrea, officially the State of Eritrea, is a country in the Horn of Africa region of East Africa.

q.p: Which country uses the bimetallism as its official currency?
q.e: The bimetallism is the official currency of Ming dynasty. The Ming dynasty, officially the Great Ming, was an imperial dynasty of China that ruled from 1368 to 1644, following the collapse of the Mongol-led Yuan dynasty.

q.p: This provincial capital in the southern Netherlands, colloquially known as Den Bosch, is home to over 160,000 people — which city?
q.e: 's-Hertogenbosch is a city and municipality in the Netherlands with a population of 160,783.

q.p: The largest city and former capital of Ivory Coast, this cultural crossroads of West Africa is the most populous French-speaking city in the region — name the city?
q.e: Abidjan (N'ko:) is the largest city and the former capital of Ivory Coast. Abidjan ( AB-ih-JAHN, French: [abidʒɑ̃]; N'ko: ߊߓߌߖߊ߲߬) is the largest city and the former capital of Ivory Coast.

q.p: Home to the giant sovereign-wealth fund ADIA, this capital sits on a T-shaped island in the Persian Gulf and ranks just behind Dubai in population — which city?
q.e: Abu Dhabi is the capital city of the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

q.p: Sitting on a deep, semicircular Pacific bay 380 km south of Mexico City, this seaport is the largest city in the state of Guerrero — what city is it?
q.e: Acapulco (US also AHK-; Nahuatl languages: Acapolco), is a city and major seaport in the state of Guerrero on the Pacific Coast of Mexico, 380 kilometres (240 mi) south of Mexico City.

q.p: This West African capital sits on the Gulf of Guinea and is home to over 5 million people across its greater metropolitan region — name the city?
q.e: Accra is the capital and largest city of Ghana, located on the southern coast at the Gulf of Guinea, which is part of the Atlantic Ocean.

q.p: Which Argentine peak in the Andes, standing at 6,967 meters, is the highest mountain in both the Americas and the Southern Hemisphere, and one of the celebrated Seven Summits?
q.e: Aconcagua (Spanish) is a mountain in the Principal Cordillera of the Andes range, located in Mendoza Province, Argentina.

q.p: Covering about 20% of Earth's land area, this is the world's second-largest continent — and home to the planet's youngest population, with a median age under 20. What is it?
q.e: Africa is the world's second-largest and second-most populous continent after Asia.

q.p: This city on the west coast of Corsica is the island's capital and largest settlement, and grew up around a citadel the Genoese built there in 1492 — what city is it?
q.e: Ajaccio is the capital and largest city of Corsica, France. It forms a French commune, prefecture of the department of Corse-du-Sud, and head office of the Collectivité territoriale de Corse (capital city of Corsica).

q.p: This non-contiguous U.S. state borders Canada's Yukon and sits closer to Asia than any other state, sharing a Bering Strait line with Russia — which state is it?
q.e: Alaska (-) is a non-contiguous U.S. Alaska (ə-LASS-kə) is a non-contiguous U.S. state located in the northwestern regions of North America.

q.p: Sitting on the Mediterranean coast, this North African capital is the third-largest city on that sea and the largest city in its own country — what city is it?
q.e: Algiers is the capital city of Algeria, located on the Mediterranean Sea in the north-central portion of the country.

q.p: Begun in 1238 on Granada's Sabika hill by the first Nasrid emir, this is celebrated as the only well-preserved palace surviving from the medieval Islamic world — what is it?
q.e: Alhambra is a palatine city and fortress complex located in Granada, Spain.

q.p: Home to the Arrernte people for tens of thousands of years, this outback Australian town is the Northern Territory's third-largest settlement — which town?
q.e: Alice Springs (Eastern) is a town in the Northern Territory, Australia; it is the third-largest settlement in the Northern Territory after Darwin and Palmerston.

q.p: Covering 28.4% of Earth's land area, this 'New World' landmass would rank as the second-largest continent by area if counted as a single one. What is it?
q.e: Americas are a landmass comprising the totality of North America and South America.

q.p: Home to France's largest Gothic cathedral and the birthplace of Emmanuel Macron, this northern French city was also where Jules Verne spent his final decades — which city?
q.e: Amiens is a city and commune in northern France, located 120 km (75 mi) north of Paris and 100 km (62 mi) south-west of Lille.

q.p: Sitting roughly 47 kilometers northeast of Lahore, Pakistan, this major Punjabi cultural and economic hub is home to over a million people — which city?
q.e: Amritsar is the second-largest city in the Indian state of Punjab, after Ludhiana.

q.p: This state on India's southeastern coast is the country's seventh-largest by area, with Telugu as its official language and Amaravati as its capital — which state?
q.e: Andhra Pradesh is a state on the east coast of southern India.

q.p: Legend credits Charlemagne with founding this tiny Pyrenean state, which is still co-ruled by two princes — a Spanish bishop and the president of France. Which country?
q.e: Andorra is a landlocked country on the Iberian Peninsula, in the eastern Pyrenees in southwestern Europe, bordered by France to the north and Spain to the south.

q.p: Located roughly 300 km southwest of Paris and serving as prefecture of the Maine-et-Loire department, this city was a key stronghold for centuries — which city?
q.e: Angers is a city in western France, about 300 km (190 mi) southwest of Paris.

q.p: The second-largest Portuguese-speaking country after Brazil, this Southern African nation on the Atlantic coast is bordered by Namibia, the DRC and Zambia — which country?
q.e: Angola is a country on the western coast of Southern Africa.

q.p: Layered with Hittite, Phrygian, Roman, and Ottoman sites, this central Anatolian city — once called Ancyra — serves as Turkey's capital — which city is it?
q.e: Ankara is the capital city of Turkey. Located in the central part of Anatolia, the city has a population of over 5.3 million residents in its urban center, out of 6 million residents in Ankara Province.

q.p: On the Chesapeake at the mouth of the Severn River, this state capital briefly served as the temporary national capital of the United States in 1783–1784. Which city?
q.e: Annapolis, Maryland (-) is the capital of the U.S. It is the county seat of Anne Arundel County and its only incorporated city.

q.p: Sitting at the northern tip of its namesake lake, 35 kilometres south of Geneva, this French city is nicknamed the 'Pearl of the French Alps' — name it?
q.e: Annecy is the prefecture and largest city of the Haute-Savoie department in the Auvergne-Rhne-Alpes region of Southeastern France.

q.p: About 40% larger than Europe and blanketed by an ice sheet nearly two kilometers thick on average, this southernmost continent contains the geographic South Pole — which continent?
q.e: Antarctica is Earth's southernmost and least-populated continent.

q.p: This Caribbean archipelago splits into a 'Greater' and 'Lesser' half, bordered by the Gulf of Mexico, the Caribbean Sea, and the Atlantic — what's it called?
q.e: Antilles is an archipelago within the West Indies in the Caribbean region of the Americas.

q.p: Running roughly 1,200 kilometers down the length of peninsular Italy, this mountain range meets the Ligurian Alps in the northwest and ends near Reggio di Calabria — what is it?
q.e: Apennine Mountains are a mountain range consisting of parallel smaller chains extending c.

q.p: Which line of latitude, sitting at about 66°34' N, marks the boundary where the sun doesn't rise at all during the winter solstice, or set at all during the summer solstice?
q.e: Arctic Circle is one of the two polar circles, and the northernmost of the five major circles of latitude.

q.p: This landlocked Southern state takes its name from the Osage and ranges from the Ozark Mountains to the Delta lowlands along the Mississippi — which state is it?
q.e: Arkansas is a landlocked state in the West South Central region of the Southern United States.

q.p: Home to the Netherlands Open Air Museum and Royal Burgers' Zoo, this Gelderland capital straddles the Nederrijn river near the German border — which city?
q.e: Arnhem is a city and municipality situated in the eastern part of the Netherlands, near the German border.

q.p: This coastal Israeli city near the Gaza Strip border takes its modern name from an ancient seaport that was destroyed in 1270 — name the city?
q.e: Ashkelon is a coastal city in the Southern District of Israel on the Mediterranean coast, 50 kilometres (30 mi) south of Tel Aviv, and 13 kilometres (8 mi) north of the border with the Gaza Strip.

q.p: Home to roughly 60% of all humanity and the cradle of many of the first civilisations, it shares the Eurasian landmass with Europe — which continent?
q.e: Asia (UK also) is the largest continent in the world by both land area and population.

q.p: Located south of the Eastern Himalayas along the Brahmaputra Valley and bordering both Bhutan and Bangladesh, this is northeastern India's most populous state — which state?
q.e: Assam is a state in Northeast India, located south of the Eastern Himalayas along the Brahmaputra Valley and Barak River valleys.

q.p: Sitting on the Ishim river, this city took over as Kazakhstan's capital from Almaty in 1997 and briefly bore a former president's name before reverting in 2022 — what is it?
q.e: Astana is the capital city of Kazakhstan. The city lies on the banks of the Ishim river in the north of Kazakhstan and is located within the Akmola Region but is self-administering.

q.p: Spanning over 3,400 years of recorded history, this Mediterranean capital anchors the eighth-largest urban area in the European Union. Which Greek city?
q.e: Athens is the capital and largest city of Greece. A significant coastal urban area in the Mediterranean, Athens is also the capital of the Attica region and is the southernmost capital on the European mainland.

q.p: Capital of Georgia and the 36th-most populous city in the US, its metro area of 6.4 million makes it the sixth-largest in the nation. Which city?
q.e: Atlanta is the capital and most populous city of the U.S. It is the county seat of Fulton County and extends into neighboring DeKalb County.

q.p: Home to over 1.5 million people between the Hauraki Gulf and the Manukau Harbour, which city is New Zealand's most populous?
q.e: Auckland is a large metropolitan city in the North Island of New Zealand.

q.p: Located about 50 km west of Munich, this university town is the third-largest city in Bavaria and the regional seat of Swabia — name the city?
q.e: Augsburg (Swabian) is a city in the Bavarian part of Swabia, Germany, around 50 kilometres (31 mi) west of the Bavarian capital Munich.

q.p: Founded in 1968 by Mirra Alfassa, this planned 'City of Dawn' township sits mostly in Tamil Nadu, India — what is it called?
q.e: Auroville (City of Dawn) is an experimental township in Viluppuram district, mostly in the state of Tamil Nadu, India, with some parts in the Union Territory of Puducherry in India.

q.p: Just north of Donetsk and within the separatist republic's claimed boundaries, this Ukrainian city became a brutal battleground after Russia's full-scale invasion — what is it?
q.e: Avdiivka is a city in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine.

q.p: Around 80 percent of this Gulf archipelago's land sits on one main island, and most of its population are actually expatriates — which country?
q.e: Bahrain is an island country in West Asia.

q.p: Sitting on a river of nearly the same name about 90 kilometers north of Donetsk, this eastern Ukrainian city became a byword for grinding urban warfare in 2022–23 — name it?
q.e: Bakhmut is a city in eastern Ukraine. Bakhmut was designated a city of regional significance until 2020, when the designation was abolished.

q.p: Lying off Spain's eastern coast in the western Mediterranean, this archipelago and autonomous community includes Palma de Mallorca as its capital — which island group?
q.e: Balearic Islands are an archipelago in the western Mediterranean Sea, near the eastern coast of the Iberian Peninsula.

q.p: Divided into seven communes and sited near river rapids on the Niger, this West African capital ranks behind Lagos, Abidjan, and four others in regional population — which city?
q.e: Bamako is the capital and largest city of Mali with a 2022 population of 4,227,569.

q.p: This is the second-largest city in Bosnia and Herzegovina and serves as the main political and economic hub of Republika Srpska — what city is it?
q.e: Banja Luka (Serbian) or Banjaluka (Serbian) is the second largest city in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the most populous in Republika Srpska.

q.p: Colombia's fourth-most populous city, this Caribbean port lies near the delta of the Magdalena River and serves as capital of the Atlántico department — what city is it?
q.e: Barranquilla (Latin American) is the capital district of the Atlntico department in Colombia.

q.p: Home to the first mosque built outside the Arabian Peninsula, this Iraqi port city near the Iran border regularly sees summer temperatures top 50°C — which city?
q.e: Basra is a port city in southern Iraq.

q.p: Sitting at the foot of the Caucasus in a humid subtropical zone, this deep-water Black Sea port is the capital of Georgia's Autonomous Republic of Adjara — which city?
q.e: Batumi is the second-largest city of Georgia and the capital of the Autonomous Republic of Adjara.

q.p: Often dubbed the 'Capital of the Negev,' this southern Israeli city marks the lower end of the biblical phrase 'From Dan to ___' — which desert city is it?
q.e: Beersheba (beer-), officially Be'er-Sheva (bair-SHEV-), is the largest city in the Negev desert of southern Israel.

q.p: This peninsula city has been inhabited for more than 5,000 years and is the capital of its nation — can you name it?
q.e: Beirut (bay-ROOT) is the capital and largest city of Lebanon.

q.p: A landlocked Eastern European nation bordering Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia, with Minsk as its capital—what's this country?
q.e: Belarus is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe. It is bordered by Russia to the east and northeast, Ukraine to the south, Poland to the west, and Lithuania and Latvia to the northwest.

q.p: Founded in 1616 and now Brazil's 12th most populous city, this northern port sits about 100 km upriver from the Atlantic on the edge of the Amazon delta — which city?
q.e: Belém (Portuguese for Bethlehem; initially called Nossa Senhora de Belm do Gro-Par, in English Our Lady of Bethlehem of Great Par), often called Belm of Par, is the capital and largest city of the state of Par in the north of Brazil.

q.p: Known as India's "Garden City" for its parks and greenery, this southern metropolis is the third-most populous city in India and the largest in South India. Which city?
q.e: Bengaluru (its official name until 1 November 2014), is the capital and largest city of the southern Indian state of Karnataka.

q.p: This alpine city in Italy's Lombardy region sits about 40 km northeast of Milan, with a namesake mountain range beginning just to its north — name the city?
q.e: Bergamo is a city in the alpine Lombardy region of northern Italy. Bergamo ( BUR-gə-moh, Italian: [ˈbɛrɡamo]; Bergamasque: Bèrghem [ˈbɛrɡɛm]) is a city in the alpine Lombardy region of northern Italy.

q.p: Norway's second-largest city, surrounded by peaks that earn it the nickname "city of seven mountains," sits on the country's west coast — what city is it?
q.e: Bergen (Norwegian) is a city and municipality in the Vestland county on the west coast of Norway.

q.p: It's only Switzerland's fifth-most populous city, trailing Zurich, Geneva, Basel and Lausanne, yet it serves as the country's de facto seat of government — which city is it?
q.e: Bern (Swiss Standard), or Berne, is the de facto capital of Switzerland, referred to as the "federal city".

q.p: Formally established in 1948 but tracing its history to the 1st century BCE, this Indian city forms a 'Golden Triangle' with Puri and Konark — which city?
q.e: Bhubaneswar (/bbnesw/) is the capital and the largest city of the Indian state of Odisha.

q.p: Located about 200 km northeast of Warsaw on the Biała River, this is the largest city in northeastern Poland and sits near the EU's eastern border with Belarus. Name the city?
q.e: Białystok is the largest city in northeastern Poland and the capital of the Podlaskie Voivodeship.

q.p: Home to redwood forests and dramatic cliffs where mountains meet the Pacific, this stretch of California's Central Coast draws up to 7 million visitors a year — which destination?
q.e: Big Sur is a rugged and mountainous section of the Central Coast of the U.S.

q.p: Split by the Ganges as it flows west to east, this eastern Indian state borders Nepal to the north and is the country's second most populous — which state?
q.e: Bihar is a state in eastern India. It borders Uttar Pradesh to its west, Nepal to the north, the northern part of West Bengal to the east, and Jharkhand to the south.

q.p: Nicknamed the 'Magic City' for its rapid early growth, this is the most populous city in its state and the trade hub for everything east of the Continental Divide — which one?
q.e: Billings, Montana is the most populous city in the U.S. The population was 117,116 at the 2020 census, while the Billings metropolitan area has an estimated 193,000 people.

q.p: Once just a hamlet, this Irish Sea coast resort town grew rapidly after sea bathing became fashionable in the mid-1700s and became a borough in 1876 — which town?
q.e: Blackpool is a seaside town in Lancashire, England.

q.p: This physiographic province of the Appalachian Highlands runs through eight eastern states and divides near the Roanoke River gap — which range?
q.e: Blue Ridge Mountains are a physiographic province of the larger Appalachian Highlands range.

q.p: The second-largest city of Westphalia after Dortmund, this German university city anchors part of Europe's biggest urban area, the Ruhr — which city?
q.e: Bochum is a city in North Rhine-Westphalia.

q.p: Known in antiquity as Halicarnassus, this Turkish port town was once home to one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, the tomb of a Carian ruler — what town is it?
q.e: Bodrum (Turkish) is a town and district of Mula Province in Turkey.

q.p: The westernmost and largest historical region of the Czech Republic, it grew from a duchy into a kingdom within the Holy Roman Empire — what's it called?
q.e: Bohemia (boh-) is the westernmost and largest historical region of the Czech Republic. Bohemia ( boh-HEE-mee-ə; Czech: Čechy [ˈtʃɛxɪ]; German: Böhmen [ˈbøːmən]) is the westernmost and largest historical region of the Czech Republic.

q.p: Founded as a military outpost during an 1863 gold rush and now sitting in the Treasure Valley, this river city is its state's capital and largest — which city is it?
q.e: Boise, Idaho (locally also) is the capital and most populous city in the U.S.

q.p: This French Polynesian island is ringed by a lagoon and barrier reef, with the remnants of an extinct volcano rising to twin peaks at its center. What island is it?
q.e: Bora Bora is a French island group in the Leeward Islands, comprising the western part of the Society Islands of French Polynesia, an overseas collectivity of the French Republic in the South Pacific.

q.p: Just over 10 square kilometers in size and home to about 38,000 people as of 2020, this Philippine island is famous worldwide for its white sand beaches — which island?
q.e: Boracay (sometimes shortened by non-natives as Bora) is a resort island in the Western Visayas region of the Philippines, located 0.8 kilometers (0.50 mi) off the northwest coast of Panay Island.

q.p: Sitting on the river Garonne in southwestern France, this port city anchors the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region and lends its name to the surrounding wine country — which city is it?
q.e: Bordeaux (bor-DOH; Gascon: Bordèu) is a city on the river Garonne in the Gironde department, southwestern France.

q.p: Crossed neatly in half by the equator, this is the world's third-largest island — and Indonesians call its share Kalimantan. Which island?
q.e: Borneo is the third-largest island in the world, with an area of 748,168 km2 (288,869 sq mi), and population of 23,053,723 (2020 national censuses).

q.p: Third-largest city in the Northeast, founded on a peninsula by English Puritans in 1630—named after an English town—what's this New England hub?
q.e: Boston is the capital and most populous city of the U.S.

q.p: The Batswana make up nearly 80% of this landlocked Southern African nation, where the Kalahari Desert blankets some 70% of the territory — which country?
q.e: Botswana is a landlocked country in Southern Africa. Botswana is topographically flat, with approximately 70% of its territory being a part of the Kalahari Desert.

q.p: This West Yorkshire city, about nine miles west of Leeds, boomed in the 1800s as an international center of textile manufacturing — which city is it?
q.e: Bradford is a city in West Yorkshire, England. The wider metropolitan borough had a population of 546,976 at the same census, making it one of the most populous districts in England.

q.p: Built from 1788 to 1791 for King Frederick William II and crowned by a bronze quadriga, which Berlin monument marked the start of the road toward its namesake town on the Havel?
q.e: Brandenburg Gate is an 18th-century neoclassical monument in Berlin, Germany.

q.p: President Juscelino Kubitschek founded this purpose-built capital in 1960 to pull Brazil's seat of government toward a more central location — which city is it?
q.e: Brasília (br-, Brazilian) is the capital city of Brazil and the Federal District.

q.p: Home to over 2.1 million people, this UNESCO-designated City of Music serves as the capital of the Republic of the Congo — which city?
q.e: Brazzaville (French) is the capital and largest city of the Republic of the Congo.

q.p: This Transylvanian city, Romania's sixth most populous, serves as county seat roughly 166 kilometers north of Bucharest — what city is it?
q.e: Brașov (Transylvanian) is a city in Transylvania, Romania and the county seat (i.e.

q.p: Once merged into the city of Wesermünde in 1939, this German port city was restored to city-state Bremen's control in 1947 — which city?
q.e: Bremerhaven (German; Low) is a port city on the east bank of the Weser estuary in northern Germany.

q.p: Sitting on a peninsula of its namesake river about 15 km from Moreton Bay, this is Queensland's capital and Australia's third most populous city — which city?
q.e: Brisbane (Turrbal/) is the capital and largest city of the Australian state of Queensland and the third-most populous city in Australia, with a population of approximately 2.8 million.

q.p: Sitting on the River Avon with a short coastline on its own Channel, this is the most populous city in South West England — which city is it?
q.e: Bristol is a city and ceremonial county in South West England.

q.p: Which Czech city, sitting at the meeting point of the Svitava and Svratka rivers, is the country's second-largest after Prague and once served as capital of Moravia?
q.e: Brno (Czech) is a city in the South Moravian Region of the Czech Republic.

q.p: Coextensive with Kings County and sitting at the western end of Long Island, which is the most populous of New York City's five boroughs?
q.e: Brooklyn is the most populous of the five boroughs and counties in New York City, United States.

q.p: The capital of West Flanders and Belgium's sixth most populous city, this Dutch-speaking city's historic core is a celebrated World Heritage Site — which city?
q.e: Bruges (BROOZH; Dutch: Brugge) is the capital and largest city of the province of West Flanders, in the Flemish Region of Belgium.

q.p: On Borneo's northern coast, this Malay-speaking nation has its territory split in two by Sarawak's Limbang district — which country?
q.e: Brunei is a country in Southeast Asia, situated on the northern coast of the island of Borneo.

q.p: Bordered by Oxfordshire, Berkshire, and Greater London, which county's largest settlement is Milton Keynes, with historic towns Aylesbury and High Wycombe besides?
q.e: Buckinghamshire (abbreviated Bucks) is a ceremonial county in South East England.

q.p: With just under 17,500 residents, this Montenegrin resort town's medieval walls have watched over the Adriatic for two and a half millennia — which town?
q.e: Budva is a town in the Coastal region of Montenegro.

q.p: A Silk Road hub for trade and scholarship, birthplace of Imam Bukhari and once capital of its own emirate, which Uzbek city packs in some 140 architectural monuments?
q.e: Bukhara (buu-KHAR-) is the seventh-largest city in Uzbekistan by population, with 280,187 residents as of 1 January 2020.

q.p: Sitting south of the Danube and west of the Black Sea, this Balkan nation borders Greece and Turkey to the south and Romania across the river to the north — which country?
q.e: Bulgaria is a country in Southeast Europe.

q.p: Capital Ouagadougou, home to the Mossi people who founded kingdoms here centuries ago, this West African nation shed its old name 'Upper Volta' in 1984 — which country is it?
q.e: Burkina Faso is a landlocked country in West Africa.

q.p: Which South Korean city, the country's second-most populous after Seoul with over 3.3 million residents, is home to the nation's busiest port — the sixth-busiest in the world?
q.e: Busan is the second most populous city in South Korea, after Seoul; it has a population of over 3.3 million as of 2024.

q.p: Third-largest commune in Normandy after Le Havre and Rouen, this city serves as prefecture of Calvados and offers a ferry crossing to England — which city?
q.e: Caen is a city and commune 15 km (9.3 mi) inland from the northwestern coast of France.

q.p: Known in Sardinian as Casteddu, this ancient port is the capital and largest city of its Mediterranean island — what is it?
q.e: Cagliari is a municipality and the capital and largest city of the island of Sardinia, an autonomous region of Italy.

q.p: As of 2021, this city in Alberta, Canada had a population of 1.3 million and is the third-largest city in Canada, located at the confluence of two rivers. What is it?
q.e: Calgary is the largest city in the Canadian province of Alberta.

q.p: With a coastline on the Bight of Biafra and 250 native languages spoken alongside English and French, this Central African nation borders Nigeria, Chad, and Gabon — which country?
q.e: Cameroon is a country in Central Africa. Its coastline lies on the Bight of Biafra, part of the Gulf of Guinea, and the Atlantic Ocean.

q.p: Located about 100 kilometers off Africa's northwest coast, this Spanish archipelago — including Tenerife and Lanzarote — is the EU's most populous overseas territory — name it?
q.e: Canary Islands are an archipelago in the Atlantic Ocean and the southernmost autonomous community of Spain, located about 100 kilometres (60 mi) off the northwest coast of Africa.

q.p: South Africa's oldest city and legislative capital, this harbour city sits beneath a famous flat-topped mountain and is the country's second-largest by population — which city?
q.e: Cape Town is the legislative capital of South Africa. The city is known for its harbour, its natural setting in the Cape Floristic Region, and for landmarks such as Table Mountain and Cape Point.

q.p: This historical region in Central Anatolia was described by Herodotus as stretching from the Taurus Mountains to the Black Sea region — what is it?
q.e: Cappadocia is a historical region in Central Anatolia region, Turkey. It is largely in the provinces of Nevşehir, Kayseri, Aksaray, Kırşehir, Sivas and Niğde.

q.p: This is the second-largest city on the Italian island of Sicily after Palermo, hosting the island's main airport — the fifth-busiest in all of Italy — what's this city called?
q.e: Catania (UK also, US also, Sicilian and) is the second-largest city in the autonomous island region of Sicily in Italy, after Palermo, both by area and by population.

q.p: The third-tallest Orthodox church in the world, this Moscow landmark near the Kremlin was blown up in 1931 to clear ground for a planned Palace of the Soviets — which building?
q.e: Cathedral of Christ the Saviour is a Russian Orthodox cathedral in Moscow, Russia, on the northern bank of the Moskva River, a few hundred metres southwest of the Kremlin.

q.p: Conventionally treated as a natural barrier dividing Europe from Asia, this region spans parts of southern Russia, Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan — what is it?
q.e: Caucasus is a geographical region spanning parts of Eastern Europe and Western Asia.

q.p: Bordered by Morocco on the North African coast, this Spanish autonomous city sits at the boundary between the Mediterranean Sea and the Atlantic Ocean. What city is it?
q.e: Ceuta (Moroccan) is an autonomous city of Spain on the North African coast.

q.p: Popular with summer tourists, this peninsula regional unit of Greece is capped at its eastern end by the self-governing monastic community of Mount Athos — which region?
q.e: Chalkidiki is a peninsula and regional unit of Greece, in coastal Macedonia.

q.p: This Indian city serves as the shared capital of two separate states, Punjab and Haryana, despite being a union territory in its own right — what city is it?
q.e: Chandigarh is a city and union territory in northwestern India, serving as a shared capital for the states of Punjab and Haryana.

q.p: As the largest city in both its province and the whole of French-speaking Belgium, this Sambre-valley city's people are known as Carolorégiens. Which city?
q.e: Charleroi is a city and a municipality of Wallonia, located in the province of Hainaut, Belgium.

q.p: Founded by the English in 1670 as Charles Town and sitting where the Ashley, Cooper, and Wando rivers meet the Atlantic, which is its state's most populous city?
q.e: Charleston, South Carolina is the most populous city in the U.S. It ranks as the third-most-populous metropolitan area in the state and the 71st-most-populous in the U.S.

q.p: The most populous city in its state and the county seat of Mecklenburg County, it ranked among the country's fastest-growing metro areas between 2004 and 2014 — which city?
q.e: Charlotte, North Carolina is the most populous city in the U.S. The Charlotte metropolitan area, with an estimated 2.88 million residents, is the 21st-largest metropolitan area in the U.S.

q.p: Home to the city of Chester and split into four unitary authorities including Halton, this county lies in North West England along the Dee Estuary — name it?
q.e: Cheshire (-eer) is a ceremonial county in North West England.

q.p: Sitting on the River Dee near the Welsh border, this English city's first cathedral began as a minster church founded by a Mercian king in 689 — which city?
q.e: Chester is a cathedral city in Cheshire, England, on the River Dee, very close to the England-Wales border.

q.p: Founded in 1867 as a junction on the Union Pacific Railroad and named for a Native American people, this state capital sits on Crow Creek near Warren Air Force Base — which city?
q.e: Cheyenne, Wyoming (shy-AN or shy-EN) is the capital and most populous city of the U.S.

q.p: Carved out of Madhya Pradesh and granted statehood in 2000, this landlocked central Indian state is home to the ancient Sitabenga Caves. What state is it?
q.e: Chhattisgarh is a landlocked state in central India. Chhattisgarh (Hindi: [ˈtʃʰət̪ːiːsgəɽʱ]) is a landlocked state in central India.

q.p: The southernmost country in the world stretches along a narrow strip between the Andes Mountains and the Pacific—where is this?
q.e: Chile is a country in western South America.

q.p: Once known by its Russian name Kishinev, this capital sits on the river Bîc and is its country's main industrial and commercial centre — which city, capital of Moldova?
q.e: Chișinău (formerly known by its Russian form Kishinev) is the capital and largest city of Moldova.

q.p: Once ruled by an elected Grand Prince before autonomous tribes took hold, this North Caucasus region along the Black Sea fell to Russian conquest in the 1860s — what was it called?
q.e: Circassia (sir-KASH-), also known as Zichia, was a country and a historical region in Eastern Europe.

q.p: This London borough contains the Houses of Parliament, Buckingham Palace, and Downing Street, plus the West End's Oxford Street and Soho — which borough is it?
q.e: City of Westminster is a London borough with city status in Greater London, England.

q.p: This Ohio city on the southern shore of Lake Erie is the county seat of Cuyahoga County and the most populous city on the entire lake. What city is it?
q.e: Cleveland is a city in the U.S. Cleveland ( KLEEV-lənd) is a city in the U.S. state of Ohio and the county seat of Cuyahoga County.

q.p: Located in the Someșul Mic river valley and considered the unofficial capital of Transylvania, this is Romania's second-most populous city — name it?
q.e: Cluj-Napoca is a city in northwestern Romania. The Cluj-Napoca metropolitan area had a population of 411,379 people, while the population of the peri-urban area is approximately 420,000.

q.p: Sitting on the Noyyal River in the shadow of the Western Ghats, this is Tamil Nadu's second-largest city after Chennai. Name it?
q.e: Coimbatore is a metropolitan city in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu.

q.p: A South American nation with insular regions in North America, bordered by Venezuela, Brazil, Peru, Ecuador, Panama and the Caribbean Sea—what's the country?
q.e: Colombia is a country located in South America, with insular regions in North America. Colombia is divided into 32 departments.

q.p: This South Asian island nation's executive and judicial capital also serves as its financial hub and most populous city, home to a metro area of 5.6 million — which city is it?
q.e: Colombo (k-) is Sri Lanka's executive and judicial capital, as well as the country's most populous city.

q.p: The most populous city in its state, it grew from Native American settlements along the Scioto River and is the county seat of Franklin County — which state capital?
q.e: Columbus, Ohio (k-) is the capital and most populous city of the U.S.

q.p: Sitting on the southwestern branch of a namesake lake near the Alps in Lombardy, this Italian city is known for its Duomo and opulent villas — what city is it?
q.e: Como is a city and comune (municipality) in Lombardy, Italy.

q.p: Self-governing in free association with New Zealand, this 15-island Polynesian nation has a capital, Avarua, located on its largest island, Rarotonga — name the country?
q.e: Cook Islands are an island country and associated state of New Zealand in Polynesia, part of Oceania, in the South Pacific Ocean.

q.p: A crescent moon, a sundial, and chairs all carved from multi-ton oolite limestone make up which Miami-Dade attraction built by one eccentric man, Edward Leedskalnin?
q.e: Coral Castle is an oolite limestone structure created by the Latvian-American eccentric Edward Leedskalnin (1887-1951).

q.p: Founded in 1858 after an earthquake destroyed its ancient predecessor, this Peloponnese city serves as capital of its surrounding regional unit in Greece. Name the city?
q.e: Corinth (modern city) is a city in the Peloponnese in Greece. Corinth ( KORR-inth; Greek: Κόρινθος, romanized: Kórinthos, Modern Greek pronunciation: [ˈkorinθos]) is a city in the Peloponnese in Greece.

q.p: This English cathedral city on the River Sherbourne received its city status by royal charter in 1345 and was historically part of Warwickshire until the 1970s — what city is it?
q.e: Coventry (or rarely KUV-) is a cathedral city and metropolitan borough in the West Midlands county, in England, on the River Sherbourne.

q.p: This northern Italian city on the Po River is renowned for producing some of history's finest violins, crafted by luthiers such as Stradivari and the Amati family — which city?
q.e: Cremona (krim-, UK also krem-,; Cremuns: Cremna) is a city and comune (municipality) in northern Italy, situated in Lombardy, on the left bank of the Po river in the middle of the Po Valley.

q.p: Connected to the mainland by a narrow isthmus and, since 2018, by a bridge spanning the Strait of Kerch, this Black Sea peninsula sits between Ukraine and Russia — name it?
q.e: Crimea (kry-MEE-) is a peninsula in Eastern Europe, on the northern coast of the Black Sea, almost entirely surrounded by the Black Sea and the smaller Sea of Azov.

q.p: A Central European nation on the Adriatic coast with over 1,000 islands, bordered by Slovenia, Hungary, Serbia, Bosnia and Montenegro—what's this country?
q.e: Croatia is a country in Central and Southeast Europe, on the coast of the Adriatic Sea.

q.p: This Tigris-side capital of the Sasanian Empire fell to Arab conquerors in 637 AD, marking a key moment in the Muslim conquest of Persia — which ancient city?
q.e: Ctesiphon (TESS-if-on; Middle Persian: Tyspwn or Tysfwn) was an ancient city in modern Iraq, on the eastern bank of the Tigris, about 35 kilometres (22 mi) southeast of Baghdad.

q.p: Located east of the Yucatán Peninsula and south of Florida, this Caribbean island nation is the third-most populous in the region. What country is it?
q.e: Cuba is an island country in the Caribbean. It comprises the eponymous main island as well as 4,195 islands, islets, and cays.

q.p: Home to Carlisle, Penrith, and Kendal, this rural ceremonial county in North West England shares a border with two Scottish council areas — which county?
q.e: Cumbria is a ceremonial county in North West England. Cumbria is predominantly rural, with an area of 6,769 km2 (2,614 sq mi) and an estimated population of 510,680 in 2024.

q.p: Its capital is Willemstad, and together with Aruba and Bonaire it makes up the Dutch "ABC islands" in the southern Caribbean. Which constituent country of the Netherlands is this?
q.e: Curaçao is a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

q.p: Blending rhythm and blues with gospel, jazz, and country influences, this genre emerged in the United States in the late 1940s but didn't get its name until 1954. What genre is it?
q.e: Cyclades are an island group in the Aegean Sea, southeast of mainland Greece and a former administrative prefecture of Greece.

q.p: Situated on the westernmost point of mainland Africa, this coastal capital city grew near an island once used as a base for the Atlantic slave trade — name the city?
q.e: Dakar (UK also:) is the capital and largest city of Senegal.

q.p: Perched above 2,000 metres in the Eastern Himalayas of West Bengal, with the world's third-highest mountain visible to the north on clear days, which city is it?
q.e: Darjeeling is a city in the northernmost region of the Indian state of West Bengal.

q.p: Holding the official title 'City of Science', this German city in Hesse hosts a major European satellite-meteorology organization among its many research institutions. Name it?
q.e: Darmstadt (UK also -shtat, US also -s(h)taht) is a city in the state of Hesse in Germany, located in the southern part of the Rhine-Main-Area (Frankfurt Metropolitan Region).

q.p: Home to the Ford Motor Company and its founder, this Detroit suburb was first settled by French Canadian voyageurs who named it for its abundant springs — which city?
q.e: Dearborn, Michigan is a city in Wayne County in the U.S.

q.p: Designated a 'Counter Magnet' to ease Delhi's population pressure, this Himalayan-foothill city is the most populous in its Indian state — which city?
q.e: Dehradun (DAIR- DOON), is the winter capital and the most populous city of the Indian state of Uttarakhand.

q.p: Home to a university of technology and painter Jan Vermeer, this Dutch city sits between Rotterdam and The Hague and is considered microbiology's birthplace — which city?
q.e: Delft (Dutch) is a city and municipality in the province of South Holland, Netherlands.

q.p: Nestled in the South Platte River valley just east of the Rocky Mountains' Front Range, this U.S. state capital is home to 715,522 residents — what city are we describing?
q.e: Denver is the capital and most populous city of the U.S.

q.p: This Midwestern capital, an insurance-industry hub, takes its name from a nearby river whose French title may mean "River of the Monks." Which city is it?
q.e: Des Moines, Iowa is the capital and most populous city in the U.S.

q.p: This Michigan city of 639,000 is the largest US city on the Canada border, and its metro area of 4.4 million is the 14th-largest in the nation. Which city?
q.e: Detroit (dih-TROYT, locally also) is the most populous city in the U.S.

q.p: Formerly known as Dacca, this riverside capital is the largest Bengali-speaking city on Earth and ranks 55th in the world by GDP — what is it?
q.e: Dhaka (or DAK-), formerly known as Dacca, is the capital and largest city of Bangladesh.

q.p: Since 1960, this Himalayan town in India's Himachal Pradesh has been home to the 14th Dalai Lama and the Tibetan government-in-exile — what town is it?
q.e: Dharamshala (also spelled Dharamsala) is a town in the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh.

q.p: This eastern French city is the prefecture of the Côte-d'Or department and the most populous commune in its region — name the city?
q.e: Dijon is a city and the prefecture of the Cte-d'Or department of the Bourgogne-Franche-Comt region in eastern France.

q.p: Perched above the Tigris behind a famous fortress, this largest Kurdish-majority city in Turkey has been continuously lived in since roughly 8,000 BCE — which city is it?
q.e: Diyarbakır is the largest Kurdish-majority city in Turkey. It is considered one of the oldest continually inhabited cities in the world, having been continually inhabited since c. 8,000 BCE.

q.p: Home to over 160,000 people as of the 2014 census, this island off Tunisia's coast is North Africa's largest and was UNESCO-listed in 2023 — which island?
q.e: Djerba (Berber languages: erba), also transliterated as Jerba or Jarbah, is a Tunisian island and the largest island of North Africa at 514 square kilometers (198 sq mi), in the Gulf of Gabs, off the coast of Tunisia.
