q.p: A railroad running inland to Dire Dawa and Addis Ababa once made this tiny Horn of Africa country — formerly French Somaliland — a vital trade gateway. Which nation is it?
q.e: Djibouti is a country in the Horn of Africa, bordered by Somalia to the south, Ethiopia to the southwest, Eritrea in the north, and the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden to the east.

q.p: Rising in Russia's Valdai Hills and flowing through Belarus and Ukraine to the Black Sea, this roughly 2,200-km waterway is the fourth-longest river in Europe — what is it?
q.e: Dnieper ((d-)), also known as the Dnipro ((d-)), is one of the major transboundary rivers of Europe, rising in the Valdai Hills near Smolensk, Russia, before flowing through Belarus and Ukraine to the Black Sea.

q.p: Part of the Southern Limestone Alps and known to Italians as the Monti Pallidi, this range sprawls across Veneto, Trentino-Alto Adige and Friuli — what is it?
q.e: Dolomites are a mountain range in northeastern Italy.

q.p: Its capital Roseau sits on the western shore of this 750-square-kilometer Caribbean isle, first settled by the Arawak who arrived from South America — what's the country?
q.e: Dominica is an island country in the Caribbean. It is part of the Windward Islands chain in the Lesser Antilles archipelago in the Caribbean Sea.

q.p: Located on the eastern two-thirds of Hispaniola, sharing the island with Haiti, this Caribbean nation is the second-largest by area in the Antilles—what's its name?
q.e: Dominican Republic is an island country on the eastern part of the Caribbean island of Hispaniola in the Greater Antilles of the Caribbean Sea in the North Atlantic Ocean.

q.p: Europe's fifth-longest river, this waterway flows from central Russia to the Sea of Azov, roughly paralleling the Volga to its east — which river?
q.e: Don (river) is the fifth-longest river in Europe. Its basin is between the Dnieper basin to the west, the lower Volga basin immediately to the east, and the Oka basin (tributary of the Volga) to the north.

q.p: The capital of Saxony and Germany's second-largest city on the River Elbe, this metropolis of 790,000 is the fourth largest by area in the country. Where is this?
q.e: Dresden (Upper; Upper) is the capital city of the German state of Saxony and its second most populous city after Leipzig.

q.p: Sitting on a bay at the mouth of the River Liffey in the province of Leinster, this city is Ireland's capital and by far its largest — which city?
q.e: Dublin is the capital and largest city of Ireland. Various definitions of a metropolitan Greater Dublin Area exist.

q.p: Sitting at the confluence of two rivers in western Germany's Ruhr region, this half-million-population city has long been a hub of trade and industry — what is it?
q.e: Duisburg (Low) is a major city in western Germany, located in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia.

q.p: Scotland's fourth-largest city, on the north bank of the Firth of Tay, was once the center of the world's jute industry — which city is it?
q.e:
Dundee is the fourth-largest city in Scotland. The 2020 mid-year population estimate for the locality was 
148,210.

q.p: Known in Zulu as eThekwini, meaning 'bay,' this South African city is the busiest port in sub-Saharan Africa and the country's third-most populous — what city is it?
q.e: Durban is the third-most populous city in South Africa, after Johannesburg and Cape Town, and the largest city in the province of KwaZulu-Natal.

q.p: Capital of North Rhine-Westphalia and a central hub of the Rhine-Ruhr region, this city grew from a tiny settlement at the mouth of the small Düssel river — what is it?
q.e: Düsseldorf is the capital city of North Rhine-Westphalia, the most populous state of Germany.

q.p: Bounded to the east by the Ural Mountains and home to Russia as its largest country, which loosely-defined subregion of the continent is this?
q.e: Eastern Europe is a subregion of the European continent. Its eastern boundary is marked by the Ural Mountains, and its western boundary is defined in various ways.

q.p: Second only to the Tagus in length on the Iberian Peninsula, this river flows 930 kilometers from Cantabria to a Catalonian delta on the Mediterranean — which river?
q.e: Ebro (Spanish and Basque) is a river of the north and northeast of the Iberian Peninsula, in Spain.

q.p: Bordered by Colombia and Peru, this nation won independence in 1820 as part of Gran Colombia and includes the Galápagos in its territory — which country?
q.e: Ecuador is a country in northwestern South America, bordered by Colombia on the north, Peru on the east and south, and the Pacific Ocean on the west.

q.p: Seat of Scotland's government and highest courts since at least the 15th century, this is the country's second-most-populous city behind Glasgow — which one is it?
q.e: Edinburgh is the capital city of Scotland and one of its 32 council areas.

q.p: Its northern face climbs more than 3,000 metres straight out of two Swiss valleys, making it one of the most emblematic sights of the Bernese Oberland — which Alpine peak is it?
q.e: Eiger (Swiss Standard German) is a 3,967-metre (13,015 ft) mountain of the Bernese Alps, overlooking Grindelwald and Lauterbrunnen in the Bernese Oberland of Switzerland, just north of the main watershed and border with Valais.

q.p: Which Mediterranean island off Tuscany, Italy's third-largest after Sicily and Sardinia, sits just 10 km from the mainland town of Piombino?
q.e: Elba is a Mediterranean island in Tuscany, Italy, 10 km (6.2 mi) from the coastal town of Piombino on the Italian mainland, and the largest island of the Tuscan Archipelago.

q.p: Rising in the Giant Mountains of the northern Czech Republic, this river flows through Bohemia and Germany before reaching the North Sea near Hamburg — name the river?
q.e: Elbe is one of the major rivers of Central Europe.

q.p: This 102-story Art Deco tower rose in Manhattan in just over a year, from 1930 to 1931, and reigned as the world's tallest until 1970 — which landmark is it?
q.e: Empire State Building is a 102-story, supertall skyscraper in the Midtown South neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, United States.

q.p: Part of the United Kingdom, this island nation shares land borders with Scotland and Wales, while containing London and 56 million residents as of the 2021 census. What is it?
q.e: England is a country that is part of the United Kingdom.

q.p: Bordered by Ethiopia, Sudan and Djibouti, this East African country once formed the heart of the ancient Kingdom of Aksum — which nation?
q.e: Eritrea is a country in the Horn of Africa region of East Africa.

q.p: Bordered by the North Sea to the east and Greater London to the southwest, this East of England county's largest settlement is Southend-on-Sea — what county is it?
q.e: Essex is a ceremonial county in the East of England. The county has an area of 3,670 km2 (1,420 sq mi) and had an estimated population of 1,929,610 in 2024.

q.p: This Baltic nation sits south of Finland and west of Russia, consisting of a mainland and over 2,300 islands in the Baltic Sea—which country?
q.e: Estonia is a country in the Baltic region of Northern Europe.

q.p: Historically called Swaziland and KaNgwane, this landlocked Southern African nation borders South Africa on all sides except the east — what's its current official name?
q.e: Eswatini (historically called KaNgwane), also known by its former official names Swaziland and the Kingdom of Swaziland, is a landlocked country in Southern Africa.

q.p: Lying entirely in the Northern Hemisphere and conventionally divided from Asia by the Ural Mountains and the Caspian Sea, this is the second-smallest continent — what is it?
q.e: Europe is a continent located entirely in the Northern Hemisphere and mostly in the Eastern Hemisphere.

q.p: Once an affluent hub of the wool trade, this South West England cathedral city is now home to two university campuses and sits between Plymouth and Bristol — which city?
q.e: Exeter is a cathedral city and the county town of Devon in South West England.

q.p: Located in Al Anbar Governorate and grown to a population of about 250,900 by 2018, which Sunni-majority Iraqi city saw two major urban battles during the Iraq War insurgency?
q.e: Fallujah is a city in Al Anbar Governorate, Iraq. Fallujah (Arabic: ٱلْفَلُّوجَة al-Fallūjah [el.fɐl.ˈluː.dʒɐ]) is a city in Al Anbar Governorate, Iraq.

q.p: Founded in 1871 on the Red River floodplain, this city forms a twin-city metro area with Moorhead, Minnesota, just across the state line — which city?
q.e: Fargo, North Dakota is the most populous city in the U.S.

q.p: Home to the khanqah of Sheikh Salim Chishti, this Mughal capital near Agra served that role for just 14 years before Akbar moved on — which town?
q.e: Fatehpur Sikri is a town in the Agra District of Uttar Pradesh, India.

q.p: Some 87% of this Pacific nation's people live on just two islands, Viti Levu and Vanua Levu, with Suva as its capital — which archipelagic country?
q.e: Fiji is an archipelagic country in Melanesia, part of Oceania in the South Pacific Ocean.

q.p: A Nordic nation bordering Sweden, Norway and Russia, with Helsinki as its capital and a population of 5.7 million—what's the country?
q.e: Finland is a Nordic country in Northern Europe.

q.p: Adopted in 1962, whose national banner pairs green and white vertical stripes with a red crescent and star symbolizing Islam?
q.e: Flag of Algeria consists of two equal vertical bars, green and white, charged in the center with a red star and crescent, a symbol of Islam as the nation's prominent faith.

q.p: Introduced in 2012, this red-green bicolour national banner carries a red-on-white ornament pattern near the hoist, adapted from a 1951 Soviet-era design — which country claims it?
q.e: Flag of Belarus is an unequal red-green bicolour with a red-on-white ornament pattern placed at the hoist (staff) end.

q.p: First flown in 1848 by a loose confederation of states and reintroduced by a postwar republic in 1949, this black-red-gold tricolor belongs to which European nation?
q.e: Flag of Germany is a tricolour consisting of three equal horizontal bands displaying the national colours of).

q.p: First raised during the 1945 declaration of independence in Jakarta, this red-over-white national banner shares its exact dimensions with the ensign of Singapore. What is it?
q.e: Flag of Indonesia is bicolor, with two horizontal bands, red (top) and white (bottom) with an overall ratio of 2: The design of the flag has remained unchanged since.

q.p: Adopted in October 1948, this white banner features a six-pointed star centered between two horizontal blue stripes echoing a prayer shawl — which national banner is it?
q.e: Flag of Israel was officially adopted on 28 October 1948.

q.p: Adopted after independence from Spain, this vertical green-white-red tricolor features an eagle devouring a serpent atop a cactus at its center — whose national banner is it?
q.e: Flag of Mexico is a vertical tricolour of green, white, and red with the national coat of arms charged in the center of the white stripe.

q.p: Two horizontal stripes, white above red, colors officially adopted in 1831 though tied to a royal white eagle since the Middle Ages — this is the banner of which country?
q.e: Flag of Poland (flaga Polski) consists of two horizontal stripes of equal width, the upper one white and the lower one red.

q.p: Introduced by Peter the Great in 1693 and later banned by the Bolsheviks after 1917, this white-blue-red tricolor is the national banner of which country?
q.e: Flag of Russia is a tricolour of three equal horizontal bands: white on the top, blue in the middle, and red on the bottom.

q.p: Featuring a green field with the Islamic creed in white Arabic script above a sword, this national banner has been used since March 1973 — which country's is it?
q.e: Flag of Saudi Arabia is a green background with Arabic inscription and a sword in white.

q.p: This Nordic cross emblem, a gold cross on a light-blue field, traces its colors back to a 1442 royal coat of arms and to a king's heraldry from 1275 — which national banner is it?
q.e: Flag of Sweden (Sveriges flagga) consists of a yellow or gold Nordic cross (i.e. a horizontal cross extending to the edges, with the crossbar closer to the hoist than the fly) on a field of light blue.

q.p: Spanning an island plus part of the mainland, this coastal Brazilian state capital in Santa Catarina is the second-largest city in its state — what is it?
q.e: Florianópolis is the capital and second largest city of the state of Santa Catarina, in the South Region of Brazil.

q.p: Bordered by Alabama, Georgia and the Bahamas to the southeast, this 23-million-strong state is the only one fronting both the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic — what is it?
q.e:
Florida is a state in the Southeastern and South Atlantic
regions of the United States.

q.p: Named after a series of forts from the Second Seminole War, this Broward County seat sits 30 miles north of Miami along the Atlantic — what city is it?
q.e: Fort Lauderdale, Florida is a coastal city located in the U.S.

q.p: Whose name is Portuguese for 'Fortress,' this state capital of Ceará in Northeastern Brazil surpassed Salvador in 2024 to become the country's fourth-largest city — which city?
q.e: Fortaleza (Brazilian; Portuguese for 'Fortress') is the state capital of Cear, located in Northeastern Brazil.

q.p: A UNESCO biosphere reserve just 60 miles off the coast of North Africa, this Spanish island in the Atlantic is the second largest of the Canary Islands. Which island is it?
q.e: Fuerteventura is one of the Canary Islands, in the Atlantic Ocean, geographically part of Macaronesia, and politically part of Spain.

q.p: An autonomous community in the northwest corner of the Iberian Peninsula, it borders Portugal, faces the Atlantic, and boasts over 1,660 km of coastline — what is it?
q.e: Galicia (Spain) (g-LISH-(ee-)) or Galiza) is an autonomous community of Spain and historic nationality under Spanish law.

q.p: Who among these is a composer?
q.e: George Frideric Handel is a composer. Handel started three commercial opera companies to supply the English nobility with Italian opera.

q.p: Which of these is a composer?
q.e: Johannes Brahms is a composer. Johannes Brahms (German: [joˈhanəs ˈbʁaːms]; 7 May 1833 – 3 April 1897) was a German composer, virtuoso pianist, and conductor of the mid-Romantic period.

q.p: Which one below is best known as a composer?
q.e: Gioachino Rossini is a composer. Gioachino Antonio Rossini (29 February 1792 – 13 November 1868) was an Italian composer and conductor of the late Classical and early Romantic eras.

q.p: Pick the composer from these four.
q.e: Udo Lindenberg is a composer.

q.p: Which of these four is a composer?
q.e: James Horner is a composer. James Roy Horner (August 14, 1953 – June 22, 2015) was an American film composer.

q.p: In what year was Ravi Shankar born?
q.e: Ravi Shankar: Shankar was awarded India's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna, in 1999.

q.p: In what year was Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha born?
q.e: Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha: Victoria granted him the title Prince Consort in 1857.

q.p: In what year was Roger Taylor (Queen drummer) born?
q.e: Roger Taylor (Queen drummer): Roger Meddows Taylor (born 26 July 1949) is an English musician, songwriter and record producer.

q.p: In what year was Édith Piaf born?
q.e: Édith Piaf: Édith Giovanna Gassion (19 December 1915 – 10 October 1963), known as Édith Piaf (French: [edit pjaf]), was a French singer and lyricist.

q.p: In what year was Tyler, the Creator born?
q.e: Tyler, the Creator: Tyler Gregory Okonma (born March 6, 1991), known professionally as Tyler, the Creator, is an American rapper and record producer.

q.p: In what year was John Paul Jones (musician) born?
q.e: John Paul Jones (musician): Jones developed a solo career after drummer John Bonham died and Led Zeppelin disbanded in 1980.

q.p: In what year was 21 Savage born?
q.e: 21 Savage: Shéyaa Bin Abraham-Joseph (born October 22, 1992), known professionally as 21 Savage, is a British rapper based in Atlanta, Georgia.

q.p: In what year was 6ix9ine born?
q.e: 6ix9ine: Daniel Hernandez (born May 8, 1996), known professionally as 6ix9ine (pronounced "six nine"), Tekashi69, or Tekashi 6ix9ine, is an American rapper.

q.p: In what year was André 3000 born?
q.e: André 3000: André Lauren Benjamin (born May 27, 1975), known professionally as André 3000, is an American rapper, singer, record producer and actor.

q.p: In what year did Ravi Shankar die?
q.e: Ravi Shankar: Shankar was awarded India's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna, in 1999.

q.p: In what year did Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha die?
q.e: Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha: Victoria granted him the title Prince Consort in 1857.

q.p: In what year did Édith Piaf die?
q.e: Édith Piaf: Édith Giovanna Gassion (19 December 1915 – 10 October 1963), known as Édith Piaf (French: [edit pjaf]), was a French singer and lyricist.

q.p: In what year was Deep Purple founded?
q.e: Deep Purple are a British rock band formed in London in 1968.

q.p: In what year was Hey! Say! JUMP founded?
q.e: Hey! Say! JUMP: JUMP (HSJ or JUMP) is a seven-member Japanese boy band under the Japanese talent agency Starto Entertainment (formerly known as Johnny & Associates).

q.p: In what year was Johnny & Associates founded?
q.e: Johnny & Associates: Johnny & Associates, Inc. was a Japanese talent agency formed by Johnny Kitagawa in 1962, which managed groups of male idols known as Johnny's.

q.p: In what year was Symphony No. 9 (Beethoven) founded?
q.e: Symphony No. 9 (Beethoven): The Symphony No. 9 in D minor, Op. 125, is a choral symphony, the final complete symphony by Ludwig van Beethoven, composed between 1822 and 1824.

q.p: In what year was Ghost (Swedish band) founded?
q.e: Ghost (Swedish band): The band released their debut album, Opus Eponymous, in 2010, which earned them international recognition.

q.p: In what year was Shell plc founded?
q.e: Shell plc is a British multinational oil and gas company, headquartered in London, England.

q.p: In what year was Maroon 5 founded?
q.e: Maroon 5 is an American pop rock band formed in Los Angeles, California.

q.p: In what year was Requiem (Mozart) founded?
q.e: Requiem (Mozart): The Requiem in D minor, K. 626, is a Requiem Mass by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756–1791).

q.p: In what year was The Mamas & the Papas founded?
q.e: The Mamas & the Papas were an American-Canadian folk rock vocal group that recorded and performed from 1965 to 1968, with a brief reunion in 1971.

q.p: In what year was New Kids on the Block founded?
q.e: New Kids on the Block (stylized as NKOTB) are an American vocal group from Dorchester, Massachusetts.

q.p: In what year was 2PM founded?
q.e: 2PM (Korean: 투피엠) is a South Korean boy band formed by JYP Entertainment in 2008 composed of six members: Jun.

q.p: In what year was AC/DC founded?
q.e: AC/DC are an Australian rock band formed in Sydney in 1973.

q.p: In what year was Panic! at the Disco founded?
q.e: Panic! at the Disco: Following several lineup changes, Panic! at the Disco operated as the solo project of frontman Urie from 2015 until its discontinuation in 2023.

q.p: In what year was Earth, Wind & Fire founded?
q.e: Earth, Wind & Fire (abbreviated as EW&F or EWF) is an American band formed in Chicago, Illinois, in 1969.

q.p: In what year was AT&T founded?
q.e: AT&T: On the New York Stock Exchange, AT&T trades under the ticker symbol "T," and has a market capitalization of $186.83 billion.

q.p: In what year was Thirty Seconds to Mars founded?
q.e: Thirty Seconds to Mars (commonly stylized as 30 Seconds to Mars) is an American rock band formed in Los Angeles, California, in 1998.

q.p: In what year was Deutschlandlied written?
q.e: Deutschlandlied: The "Deutschlandlied", officially titled "Das Lied der Deutschen", is a German poem written by August Heinrich Hoffmann von Fallersleben.

q.p: In what year was System of a Down founded?
q.e: System of a Down is an Armenian-American heavy metal band formed in Glendale, California, in 1994.

q.p: In what year was Tesla, Inc. founded?
q.e: Tesla, Inc.: Tesla, Inc. ( TEZ-lə or TESS-lə) is an American multinational automotive and clean energy company.

q.p: In what year was Alice in Chains founded?
q.e: Alice in Chains (often abbreviated as AiC) is an American rock band formed in Seattle in 1987.

q.p: In what year was Piano discovered?
q.e: Piano: A piano is a keyboard instrument that produces sound when its keys are pressed, activating an action mechanism where hammers strike strings.

q.p: In what year was Utopia (Travis Scott album) first released?
q.e: Utopia is the fourth studio album by American rapper Travis Scott.

q.p: In what year was Sour first released?
q.e: Sour (stylized in all caps) is the debut studio album by American singer-songwriter Olivia Rodrigo.

q.p: In what year was Red (Taylor's Version) first released?
q.e: Red (Taylor's Version) is the second re-recorded album by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift, released on November 12, 2021, through Republic Records.

q.p: In what year was 72 Seasons first released?
q.e: 72 Seasons: The album generally received positive reviews from critics, who mostly praised Hetfield's lyrics and vocal performance but criticized the album's length.

q.p: In what year was Did You Know That There's a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd first released?
q.e: Did You Know That There's a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd is the ninth studio album by American singer-songwriter Lana Del Rey.

q.p: In what year was Flowers (Miley Cyrus song) first released?
q.e: Flowers (Miley Cyrus song): "Flowers" is a song by American singer Miley Cyrus from her eighth studio album Endless Summer Vacation (2023).

q.p: In what year was Symphony No. 9 (Beethoven) first released?
q.e: Symphony No. 9 (Beethoven): The Symphony No. 9 in D minor, Op. 125, is a choral symphony, the final complete symphony by Ludwig van Beethoven, composed between 1822 and 1824.

q.p: In what year was 1989 (Taylor's Version) first released?
q.e: 1989 (Taylor's Version) is the fourth re-recorded album by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift.

q.p: In what year was Bella ciao first released?
q.e: Bella ciao: Versions of "Bella ciao" continue to be sung worldwide as a hymn of resistance against Nazism, fascism, injustice and oppression.

q.p: In what year was Happy Birthday to You first released?
q.e: Happy Birthday to You: "Happy Birthday to You", or simply "Happy Birthday", is an American song traditionally sung to celebrate a person's birthday.

q.p: In what year was 1989 first released?
q.e: 1989 is the fifth studio album by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift.

q.p: In what year was Now and Then (Beatles song) first released?
q.e: Now and Then (Beatles song): "Now and Then" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles, released on 2 November 2023.

q.p: In what year was All I Want for Christmas Is You first released?
q.e: All I Want for Christmas Is You: "All I Want for Christmas Is You" is a song by American singer-songwriter Mariah Carey from her fourth studio album and first holiday album, Merry Christmas (1994).

q.p: In what year was Nothing Compares 2 U first released?
q.e: Nothing Compares 2 U: "Nothing Compares 2 U" is a 1985 song written by American musician Prince for his project, The Family, featured on its 1985 debut album.

q.p: About how tall is Aoi Yūki?
q.e: The height of Aoi Yūki is about 1.48 m.

q.p: About how tall is Édith Piaf?
q.e: The height of Édith Piaf is about 1.47 m. Édith Giovanna Gassion (19 December 1915 – 10 October 1963), known as Édith Piaf (French: [edit pjaf]), was a French singer and lyricist.

q.p: Who founded The Rolling Stones?
q.e: The Rolling Stones: Brian Jones. The Rolling Stones are an English rock band formed in London in 1962.

q.p: Who founded Death Cab for Cutie?
q.e: Death Cab for Cutie: Ben Gibbard. Death Cab for Cutie (commonly abbreviated to DCFC or Death Cab) is an American rock band formed in Bellingham, Washington, in 1997.

q.p: Who created BeReal?
q.e: BeReal: Alexis Barreyat. BeReal (stylized on the app logo as BeReal.) is a French social-networking app released in 2020, developed by Alexis Barreyat and Kévin Perreau.

q.p: Who created Oi u luzi chervona kalyna?
q.e: Oi u luzi chervona kalyna: Stepan Charnetsky. It is translated into English as "Oh, the Red Viburnum in the Meadow".

q.p: Who created Wish You Were Here (Pink Floyd album)?
q.e: Wish You Were Here (Pink Floyd album): Hipgnosis. Based on material composed while performing in Europe, Wish You Were Here was recorded over numerous sessions throughout 1975 at EMI Studios in London.

q.p: Who created Born in the U.S.A.?
q.e: Born in the U.S.A.: Andrea Kleine. Born in the U.S.A. is the seventh studio album by the American singer-songwriter Bruce Springsteen, released on June 4, 1984, through Columbia Records.

q.p: Who created Peter and the Wolf?
q.e: Peter and the Wolf: Sergei Prokofiev. The narrator tells a Russian folk tale, which the orchestra illustrates by using different instruments to play themes that represent each character in the story.

q.p: Who is the performer of California Dreamin'?
q.e: California Dreamin': The Mamas & the Papas. "California Dreamin'" is a song written by John and Michelle Phillips.

q.p: Who is the performer of Fly Me to the Moon?
q.e: Fly Me to the Moon: Nat King Cole. "Fly Me to the Moon", originally titled "In Other Words", is a song written in 1954 by Bart Howard.

q.p: Who is the performer of Everybody Wants to Rule the World?
q.e: Everybody Wants to Rule the World: Patti Smith. "Everybody Wants to Rule the World" is a song by the English pop rock band Tears for Fears from their second studio album Songs from the Big Chair (1985).

q.p: Who is the performer of Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers?
q.e: Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers: Kendrick Lamar. The album serves as his first release under his creative company PGLang, and his final project with both TDE and Aftermath.

q.p: Who is the performer of 72 Seasons?
q.e: 72 Seasons: Metallica. The album generally received positive reviews from critics, who mostly praised Hetfield's lyrics and vocal performance but criticized the album's length.

q.p: Who is the performer of Did You Know That There's a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd?
q.e: Did You Know That There's a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd: Lana Del Rey. Did You Know That There's a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd is the ninth studio album by American singer-songwriter Lana Del Rey.

q.p: Who is the performer of Money for Nothing?
q.e: Money for Nothing: Dire Straits. "Money for Nothing" is a song by the British rock band Dire Straits, the second track on their fifth studio album Brothers in Arms (1985).

q.p: Who is the performer of Do They Know It's Christmas??
q.e: Do They Know It's Christmas?: Band Aid. "Do They Know It's Christmas?" is a charity song written in 1984 by Bob Geldof and Midge Ure to raise money for the 1983–1985 famine in Ethiopia.

q.p: Who is the performer of La Vie en rose?
q.e: La Vie en rose: Marianne Michel. The song became popular in the United States in 1950, when seven versions reached the Billboard charts.

q.p: Who is the performer of Pink Friday 2?
q.e: Pink Friday 2: Nicki Minaj. Pink Friday 2 is the fifth and final studio album by rapper Nicki Minaj, released on December 8, 2023, through Republic Records.

q.p: Who is the performer of 4′33″?
q.e: 4′33″: John Cage. 4′33″ is a modernist composition by American experimental composer John Cage.

q.p: Who is the performer of Ambient 1: Music for Airports?
q.e: Ambient 1: Music for Airports: Brian Eno. Ambient 1: Music for Airports is a studio album by the English musician Brian Eno.

q.p: Who is the performer of Je t'aime... moi non plus?
q.e: Je t'aime... moi non plus: Serge Gainsbourg. "Je t'aime... moi non plus" (French for 'I love you... me neither') is a 1967 song written by Serge Gainsbourg for Brigitte Bardot.

q.p: Who is the performer of Wolfenstein: The New Order?
q.e: Wolfenstein: The New Order: Mick Gordon. Wolfenstein: The New Order is a 2014 first-person shooter game developed by MachineGames and published by Bethesda Softworks.

q.p: Who is the performer of ...Baby One More Time?
q.e: ...Baby One More Time: Britney Spears. "...Baby One More Time" is the debut single by the American singer Britney Spears, from her 1999 debut album,...Baby One More Time.

q.p: Who is the performer of Back in Black?
q.e: Back in Black: AC/DC. Back in Black is the seventh studio album by Australian rock band AC/DC, released on 25 July 1980, by Albert Productions and Atlantic Records.

q.p: Who is the performer of Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This)?
q.e: Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This): Eurythmics. "Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This)" is a song by the British synth-pop duo Eurythmics.

q.p: Who is the performer of Dragostea din tei?
q.e: Dragostea din tei: O-Zone. It was written by the band's founder Dan Balan and produced by Bogdan Popoiag.

q.p: Who is the performer of Uncharted 4: A Thief's End?
q.e: Uncharted 4: A Thief's End: Henry Jackman. Uncharted 4: A Thief's End is a 2016 action-adventure game developed by Naughty Dog and published by Sony Computer Entertainment.

q.p: Who is the performer of Swing Low, Sweet Chariot?
q.e: Swing Low, Sweet Chariot: Eric Clapton. "Swing Low, Sweet Chariot" is an African-American spiritual song and one of the best-known Christian hymns.

q.p: Who is the performer of 1989?
q.e: 1989 (album): Taylor Swift. 1989 is the fifth studio album by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift.

q.p: Who is the performer of Kill 'Em All?
q.e: Kill 'Em All: Metallica. Kill 'Em All is the debut album by the American heavy metal band Metallica, released on July 25, 1983, through the independent label Megaforce Records.

q.p: Who is the performer of Symphony No. 5 (Beethoven)?
q.e: Symphony No. 5 (Beethoven): Kevin MacLeod. It is one of the best-known of all symphonies and one of the most frequently played.

q.p: Who is the performer of Help!?
q.e: Help!: The Beatles. Help! is the fifth studio album by the English rock band the Beatles and the soundtrack to the film Help!.

q.p: Who is the performer of The Piper at the Gates of Dawn?
q.e: The Piper at the Gates of Dawn: Pink Floyd. The Piper at the Gates of Dawn is the debut studio album by the English rock band Pink Floyd, released on 4 August 1967 by EMI Columbia.

q.p: Who is the performer of ...And Justice for All?
q.e: ...And Justice for All (album): Metallica....And Justice for All is the fourth studio album by American heavy metal band Metallica, released on September 7, 1988, by Elektra Records.

q.p: Who is the performer of Highway 61 Revisited?
q.e: Highway 61 Revisited: Bob Dylan. Highway 61 Revisited is the sixth studio album by the American singer-songwriter Bob Dylan, released on August 30, 1965, by Columbia Records.

q.p: Who is the performer of Que Sera, Sera (Whatever Will Be, Will Be)?
q.e: Que Sera, Sera (Whatever Will Be, Will Be): Doris Day. "Qué Será, Será (Whatever Will Be, Will Be)" is a song written by Jay Livingston and Ray Evans and first published in 1955.

q.p: Who is the performer of A Day in the Life?
q.e: A Day in the Life: The Beatles. "A Day in the Life" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles that was released as the final track of their 1967 album Sgt.

q.p: Who is the performer of Now and Then (Beatles song)?
q.e: Now and Then (Beatles song): John Lennon. "Now and Then" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles, released on 2 November 2023.

q.p: Who is the performer of The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past?
q.e: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past: Koji Kondo. The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past is a 1991 action-adventure game developed and published by Nintendo for the Super Nintendo Entertainment System (SNES).

q.p: Who is the performer of Always on My Mind?
q.e: Always on My Mind: B. J. Thomas. The song has been a crossover hit, charting in both the country and western and pop categories.

q.p: Who is the performer of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2?
q.e: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2: Lorne Balfe. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 is a 2009 first-person shooter game developed by Infinity Ward and published by Activision.

q.p: Who is the performer of Band on the Run?
q.e: Band on the Run: Wings. It was Paul McCartney's fifth album after leaving the Beatles in April 1970 and his final album on Apple Records.

q.p: Who is the performer of Sympathy for the Devil?
q.e: Sympathy for the Devil: The Rolling Stones. "Sympathy for the Devil" is a song by the English rock band the Rolling Stones.

q.p: Who is the performer of Killing Me Softly with His Song?
q.e: Killing Me Softly with His Song: Lori Lieberman. "Killing Me Softly with His Song" is a song composed by Charles Fox with lyrics by Norman Gimbel.

q.p: Who is the performer of Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness?
q.e: Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness: The Smashing Pumpkins. It was produced by the singer and guitarist Billy Corgan, alongside the producers Flood and Alan Moulder.

q.p: Who is the performer of The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars?
q.e: The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars: David Bowie. It was recorded from November 1971 to February 1972 at Trident Studios in London.

q.p: Who is the performer of Get Rich or Die Tryin'?
q.e: Get Rich or Die Tryin': 50 Cent. Get Rich or Die Tryin' is the debut studio album by American rapper 50 Cent.

q.p: Who is the performer of The Girl from Ipanema?
q.e: The Girl from Ipanema: Antônio Carlos Jobim. "Garota de Ipanema" (Portuguese pronunciation: [ɡaˈɾotɐ dʒipɐ̃ˈnemɐ]), or "The Girl from Ipanema", is a Brazilian bossa nova and jazz song.

q.p: Who is the performer of Sweet Child o' Mine?
q.e: Sweet Child o' Mine: Guns N' Roses. "Sweet Child o' Mine" is a song by American rock band Guns N' Roses, released on their debut studio album, Appetite for Destruction (1987).

q.p: Who is the performer of (What's the Story) Morning Glory??
q.e: (What's the Story) Morning Glory?: Oasis. (What's the Story) Morning Glory? is the second studio album by the English rock band Oasis.

q.p: Who is the performer of Selected Ambient Works 85–92?
q.e: Selected Ambient Works 85–92: Aphex Twin. Selected Ambient Works 85–92 is the debut album by the British electronic music artist and producer Aphex Twin, whose real name is Richard D.

q.p: In which country is Deep Purple based?
q.e: Deep Purple: United Kingdom. Deep Purple are a British rock band formed in London in 1968.

q.p: In which country is Ive?
q.e: Ive (group): South Korea. Ive (Korean: 아이브; RR: Aibeu; stylized in all caps) is a South Korean girl group formed by Starship Entertainment.

q.p: In which country was Johnny & Associates based?
q.e: Johnny & Associates: Japan. Johnny & Associates, Inc. was a Japanese talent agency formed by Johnny Kitagawa in 1962, which managed groups of male idols known as Johnny's.

q.p: Which country is Hatikvah from?
q.e: Hatikvah: Israel. Hatikvah (Hebrew: הַתִּקְוָה [hatikˈva]; lit. 'The Hope') is the national anthem of the State of Israel.

q.p: In which country was Tokio based?
q.e: Tokio (band): Japan. Tokio was a Japanese rock/pop band formed by Johnny & Associates that formed in 1989 and debuted in 1994.

q.p: In which country is 2NE1?
q.e: 2NE1: South Korea. 2NE1 (Korean: 투애니원; RR: Tuaeniwon; pronounced [tʰu.ɛ.ni.wʌn]) is a South Korean girl group formed by YG Entertainment in 2009.

q.p: In which country was Daft Punk?
q.e: Daft Punk: France. Daft Punk were a French electronic music duo formed in 1993 in Paris by Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo.

q.p: Which country is Il Canto degli Italiani from?
q.e: Il Canto degli Italiani: Italy. "Il Canto degli Italiani" is a patriotic song written by Goffredo Mameli and set to music by Michele Novaro in 1847, currently used as the national anthem of Italy.

q.p: In which country was HIM (Finnish band) based?
q.e: HIM (Finnish band): Finland. HIM (sometimes stylized as H.I.M.) was a Finnish rock band from Helsinki.

q.p: In which country is Interpol (band) based?
q.e: Interpol (band): United States. Interpol is an American rock band from Manhattan, New York.

q.p: In which country is Korol i Shut based?
q.e: Korol i Shut: Soviet Union.

q.p: In which country is Alice in Chains based?
q.e: Alice in Chains: United States. Alice in Chains (often abbreviated as AiC) is an American rock band formed in Seattle in 1987.

q.p: In which country is Vedic chant?
q.e: Vedic chant: India. The oral tradition of the Vedas (Śruti) consists of several pathas, "recitations" or ways of chanting the Vedic mantras.

q.p: In which country is Iz*One?
q.e: Iz*One: South Korea. Iz*One made their official debut on October 29, 2018, with their first extended play (EP) Color*Iz.

q.p: In which country is Nazareth (band)?
q.e: Nazareth (band): United Kingdom.

q.p: Who is credited with discovering Synthesizer?
q.e: Synthesizer: Robert Moog. A synthesizer (also synthesiser or synth) is an electronic musical instrument that generates audio signals.

q.p: Who is credited with discovering Western concert flute?
q.e: Western concert flute: Theobald Boehm. The Western concert flute can refer to the common C concert flute or to the family of transverse (side-blown) flutes to which the C flute belongs.

q.p: Who is credited with discovering Bluegrass music?
q.e: Bluegrass music: Bill Monroe. Bluegrass music is a genre of American roots music that developed in the 1940s in the Appalachian region of the United States.

q.p: Who is credited with discovering Electric guitar?
q.e: Electric guitar: George Beauchamp. An electric guitar is a guitar that, unlike a standard acoustic guitar, requires external electric sound amplification to be heard at typical performance volumes.

q.p: Accordion in hand, this musician has built a career on parody songs and polka medleys ever since Dr. Demento aired one of his tracks back in 1976 — who is he?
q.e: "Weird Al" Yankovic (born October 23, 1959) is an American musician, songwriter, and actor.

q.p: Signed to Universal Music Japan, this Kyoto-formed rock outfit mixes heavy metal, reggae, and bossa nova into its sound — which band?
q.e: 10-Feet is a Japanese rock band formed in 1997 in Kyoto, signed to Universal Music Japan and managed by Badass.

q.p: Born from a 2019 fight over master recordings, this 2023 re-recording of a 2014 album tucks in five previously unreleased "From the Vault" songs — which release is it?
q.e: 1989 (Taylor's Version) (Taylor's Version) is the fourth re-recorded album by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift.

q.p: Formed by YG Entertainment in 2009 with members Bom, CL, Dara, and Minzy, this South Korean girl group debuted via the single 'Lollipop' alongside labelmate BigBang — which group?
q.e: 2NE1 is a South Korean girl group formed by YG Entertainment in 2009. 2NE1 (Korean: 투애니원; RR: Tuaeniwon; pronounced [tʰu.ɛ.ni.wʌn]) is a South Korean girl group formed by YG Entertainment in 2009.

q.p: Fronted by future hitmaking songwriter Linda Perry, this San Francisco rock band scored a massive 1993 hit that remains a karaoke staple decades later — what band is it?
q.e: 4 Non Blondes is an American rock band formed in San Francisco in 1989.

q.p: After a guest spot on Trippie Redd's "Poles 1469," this aggressive, tattoo-covered rapper dropped the 2018 mixtape Day69 — who is he?
q.e: 6ix9ine (born May 8, 1996), known professionally as 6ix9ine, Tekashi69, or Tekashi 6ix9ine, is an American rapper.

q.p: The English-language rendition of this Nena song, retitled and rewritten with different lyrics, failed to chart in the US unlike the German original — which song?
q.e: 99 Luftballons is a song by the West German band Nena from their 1983 self-titled album.

q.p: Formed in Oslo in 1982 by Paul Waaktaar-Savoy, Magne Furuholmen, and Morten Harket, this Norwegian synth-pop band rose to fame during the mid-1980s. What is the band's name?
q.e: A-ha (often stylised as a-ha; Norwegian) are a Norwegian synth-pop band formed in Oslo in 1982.

q.p: Founded in Sydney in 1973 by guitar-slinging brothers Angus and Malcolm Young, this band insists its sound is simply "rock and roll" — which Rock and Roll Hall of Fame act is it?
q.e: AC/DC are an Australian rock band formed in Sydney in 1973.

q.p: Born in January 1978, this American singer is a founding member of the pop vocal group Backstreet Boys — who is he?
q.e: AJ McLean (born January 9, 1978) is an American singer.

q.p: Co-founding the Native Tongues collective in 1988, this Queens hip-hop group's jazz-infused sound shaped 1990s alternative rap — who are they?
q.e: A Tribe Called Quest was an American hip-hop group formed in Queens, New York City, in 1985, originally composed of rapper and main producer Q-Tip, rapper Phife Dawg, DJ and co-producer Ali Shaheed Muhammad, and rapper Jarobi White.

q.p: With lyrics by Keith Reid and a melody inspired by Bach, this 1967 Procol Harum debut single has since been covered more than 1,000 times — which song is it?
q.e: A Whiter Shade of Pale is a song by the English rock band Procol Harum that was issued as their debut single on 12 May 1967.

q.p: Originally used to separate Renaissance polyphony from Baroque concertato styles, this term now simply describes voices singing with no instruments at all — what is it?
q.e: A cappella (AH k-PEL-uh, UK also AK-uh-PEL-uh; Italian for 'in the style of the chapel') is music performed by a singer or singing group without any instrumental accompaniment.

q.p: Crowned the 'Princess of R&B,' this Detroit-raised singer sang on Star Search at age 10 and signed with Jive Records at 12 before her life was cut short in 2001 — who is she?
q.e: Aaliyah (ah-LEE-; January 16, 1979 - August 25, 2001) was an American singer, actress, dancer, and model.

q.p: The founding lead singer of an alternative metal band, this musician released his first full solo country album, 'The Road,' through Blaster Records in 2012 — who is he?
q.e: Aaron Lewis (born April 13, 1972) is an American musician who is best known as the lead vocalist, rhythm guitarist, and founding member of the post-grunge/alternative metal band Staind, with whom he released eight studio albums.

q.p: Born Wu Keng-lin in 1985, this Taiwanese entertainer worked as an actor, singer, TV host, and businessman, and was also a member of the boy band Fahrenheit — name this performer?
q.e: Aaron Yan (traditional; simplified; Peh-e-j: Im A-ln, born Wu Keng-lin on 20 November 1985) is a Taiwanese actor, singer, television host and businessman.

q.p: Though it wasn't the last Beatles album released, it was the last one they actually recorded — a 1969 record that made prominent use of the Moog synthesiser. Which album?
q.e: Abbey Road is the eleventh studio album by the English rock band the Beatles, released on 26 September 1969 by Apple Records.

q.p: Founded in 2017 in Taiwan's Yilan County, this rock trio pairs a lead vocalist-guitarist with a second singer and a drummer. Name the band?
q.e: Accusefive (pinyin: Gowrn; Peh-e-j: K-g-lng) is a Taiwanese rock band founded in 2017 in Yilan County, composed of lead vocalist and guitarist Pan Yun-an, singer Tsai Hsin-lun (Chuan Ching/Quan Qing), and drummer Richard Lin.

q.p: The 2009 American Idol runner-up behind the Grammy-nominated single "Whataya Want from Me" went on to share the stage with Queen — which singer?
q.e: Adam Lambert (born January 29, 1982) is an American singer, songwriter and actor.

q.p: The lead singer and only continuous member of Maroon 5, this musician and TV personality first performed with a band called Kara's Flowers — who is he?
q.e: Adam Levine (l-VEEN; born March 18, 1979) is an American singer, musician and television personality who is the lead singer, rhythm guitarist and sole continuous member of the pop rock band Maroon 5.

q.p: Debuting at 17 with a song that topped Billboard Japan's Hot 100, this Japanese singer became the youngest solo artist ever to hit 100 million plays on the chart — who is she?
q.e: Ado (singer) (born October 24, 2002) is a Japanese singer.

q.p: With roughly 150 million records sold and a nickname meaning "the springy one," this Italian showman is hailed as a pillar of his country's music. Who is he?
q.e: Adriano Celentano (born 6 January 1938) is an Italian singer-songwriter, actor, showman, and filmmaker.

q.p: Crowned champion in the WBO, WBC, and WBA across four separate weight divisions during the 2010s, this American pugilist later reinvented himself as an online streamer — who is he?
q.e: Adrien Broner (born July 28, 1989) is an American former professional boxer and online streamer.

q.p: Steven Tyler and Joe Perry, sometimes called the "Toxic Twins," front which blues-based hard rock band that formed in Boston in 1970?
q.e: Aerosmith is an American rock band formed in Boston in 1970. The group consists of lead vocalist Steven Tyler, bassist Tom Hamilton, drummer Joey Kramer, and guitarists Joe Perry and Brad Whitford.

q.p: After 'Til Tuesday split in 1990, this Berklee-trained musician went solo, later gaining wider recognition for scoring Paul Thomas Anderson's 'Magnolia' — who is she?
q.e: Aimee Mann (born September 8, 1960) is an American singer-songwriter.

q.p: Born in 1995, this Japanese singer-songwriter records for the label Unborde under Warner Music Japan — who is she?
q.e: Aimyon (born on March 6, 1995) is a Japanese singer and songwriter.

q.p: This American singer fronts indie rockers Nico Vega and once released a duo EP titled Egyptian with her husband, Imagine Dragons frontman Dan Reynolds — who is she?
q.e: Aja Volkman (born March 4, 1980) is an American singer and songwriter, best known as the frontwoman of the indie rock band Nico Vega.

q.p: This American singer's 1981 album Breakin' Away spent two years on the Billboard 200, and he also sang the theme song for the 1980s TV series Moonlighting — who is he?
q.e: Al Jarreau (March 12, 1940 - February 12, 2017) was an American singer.

q.p: An EGOT winner with eight Academy Awards to his name, this composer wrote the scores and songs for The Little Mermaid, Beauty and the Beast, Aladdin, and Pocahontas — who is he?
q.e: Alan Menken (born July 22, 1949) is an American composer and conductor.

q.p: After engineering Dark Side of the Moon, this Englishman finally won a Grammy in 2019 for an anniversary edition of his own album Eye in the Sky — who is he?
q.e: Alan Parsons (born 20 December 1948) is an English audio engineer, songwriter, musician, singer and record producer.

q.p: This Canadian-American actor played a sitcom TV dad on Growing Pains in the 1980s, while being the real-life father of a pop singer — who is he?
q.e: Alan Thicke (n Jeffrey; 1 March 1947 - 13 December 2016) was a Canadian-American actor, songwriter, and game/talk show host.

q.p: This Norwegian DJ, known for hits like "Faded" and "Alone," deliberately conceals his identity behind a hoodie and mask to preserve his anonymity — who is he?
q.e: Alan Walker (born 24 August 1997) is a Norwegian DJ and record producer.

q.p: This musician-actress plays piano, guitar, and sings in a pop-rock trio with her two older sisters, and broke into film with Paul Thomas Anderson's Licorice Pizza — who is she?
q.e: Alana Haim (born December 15, 1991) is an American musician and actress.

q.p: Dubbed the 'Queen of Alt-Rock Angst,' this Canadian-American singer became a 1990s phenomenon with her confessional songwriting and mezzo-soprano voice — who is she?
q.e: Alanis Morissette (-; born June 1, 1974) is a Canadian and American singer-songwriter and record producer.

q.p: Born in Guadalajara in 1971, which pop-crossover artist earned four Latin Grammys and a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame after starting out in mariachi and charro music?
q.e: Alejandro Fernández (Spanish; born 24 April 1971) is a Mexican singer.

q.p: This Scottish rocker leads Franz Ferdinand and has lent his voice to two supergroups, FFS and BNQT — who is he?
q.e: Alex Kapranos (born 20 March 1972) is a Scottish musician.

q.p: Born in December 1985 to a famous singer-songwriter and a supermodel, this pianist and singer put out the EP Sketches and plays NYC charity shows — who is she?
q.e: Alexa Ray Joel (born December 29, 1985) is an American singer, songwriter, and pianist.

q.p: Born Vincent Furnier in Phoenix, this singer earned the nickname 'The Godfather of Shock Rock' for macabre, prop-heavy stage shows — who is he?
q.e: Alice Cooper (born Vincent Damon Furnier; February 4, 1948) is an American singer and songwriter.

q.p: This Seattle band took its name from singer Layne Staley's previous group and built a signature sound on harmonized dual vocals over heavy-metal riffs — who are they?
q.e: Alice in Chains (often abbreviated as AiC) is an American rock band formed in Seattle in 1987.

q.p: A leading voice of 1990s Bollywood playback, she has racked up two National Film Awards and seven Filmfare wins, and received the Padma Bhushan in 2026 — which Indian singer?
q.e: Alka Yagnik (born 20 March 1966) is an Indian playback singer who worked predominantly in Hindi cinema from 1980s to mid 2010s.

q.p: This 1990s British girl group, later joined by sisters Nicole and Natalie Appleton, scored UK number ones with 'Never Ever' and 'Bootie Call' — which group?
q.e: All Saints (group) were a British girl group formed in London in 1993.

q.p: This 1970 triple album included songs the Beatles had overlooked, plus hits like 'What Is Life' and 'My Sweet Lord' — which George Harrison album?
q.e: All Things Must Pass is the third studio album by the English rock musician George Harrison.

q.p: Beginning her career in 1965, this Russian singer-songwriter earned iconic status across the former Soviet Union and was dubbed by the media "the Queen of" her genre — who is she?
q.e: Alla Pugacheva (born 15 April 1949) is a Russian singer and songwriter.

q.p: This German synth-pop band, formed in Münster in 1982 and named after a 1965 Jean-Luc Godard film, scored 1980s hits with 'Forever Young' and 'Big in Japan' — name the band?
q.e: Alphaville (band) is a German synth-pop band formed in Mnster in 1982. The group was founded by singer Marian Gold and musicians Bernhard Lloyd and Frank Mertens.

q.p: Known for roles in Easy A and the CW's iZombie, this actress-singer also performs as half of a sister musical duo — who is she?
q.e: Aly Michalka (mee-; born March 25, 1989) is an American actress, singer-songwriter, and musician.

q.p: Salvador Dalí's closest friend and muse for almost two decades, this model-turned-disco-star fronted Roxy Music's For Your Pleasure album cover — what's her name?
q.e: Amanda Lear (French; ne Tap or Tapp) is a French singer, songwriter, painter, television presenter, actress and former model.

q.p: Dubbed 'The Queen of Christian Pop,' this singer crossed from CCM into the mainstream and later married country star Vince Gill — who is she?
q.e: Amy Grant (born November 25, 1960) is an American singer-songwriter and musician.

q.p: A classically trained pianist who began writing music at 11, this singer co-founded a rock band at just 13 years old. Who is she?
q.e: Amy Lee (born December 13, 1981) is an American singer-songwriter and musician.

q.p: This South Korean singer and dancer leads a girl group under Starship Entertainment, after first debuting as a member of the South Korean-Japanese group Iz*One — who is she?
q.e: An Yu-jin (born September 1, 2003) is a South Korean singer and dancer.

q.p: Born in November 2003, this Brazilian singer is known by the nickname 'the Boiadeira' and is credited as one of agronejo music's key disseminators — who is she?
q.e: Ana Castela (born 16 November 2003), also known as the Boiadeira, is a Brazilian singer-songwriter.

q.p: This Spanish performer began as a child actress before her music career took off in Italy, highlighted by the 2018 hit 'D'estate non vale' and a 2022 Sanremo entry — who is she?
q.e: Ana Mena (born 25 February 1997) is a Spanish singer-songwriter and actress.

q.p: From 1989 to 2011 he was the primary songwriter of Korol i Shut before fronting his own band Knyazz — which Russian rocker is it?
q.e: Andrei Knyazev (musician) is a Russian rock musician, songwriter and singer who is the leader of the Saint-Petersburg band Knyazz.

q.p: Composer of more than 20 musicals, this English impresario wrote 'The Music of the Night' for Phantom of the Opera and the songs of Jesus Christ Superstar — who is he?
q.e: Andrew Lloyd Webber (born 22 March 1948) is an English composer and impresario of musical theatre.

q.p: Which English musician formed half of the chart-topping 1980s duo behind "Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go" and "Careless Whisper"?
q.e: Andrew Ridgeley (born 26 January 1963) is an English musician.

q.p: Which musician, holding both Israeli and Russian citizenship, founded the long-running band known as 'Time Machine'?
q.e: Andrey Makarevich (born 11 December 1953) is an Israeli and Soviet-Russian rock musician and the founder of Russia's oldest active rock band Mashina Vremeni (Time Machine).

q.p: His career spanned three worlds at once — Hollywood film scores, jazz piano in the Great American Songbook, and the conductor's podium — who is this German-American musician?
q.e: André Previn (born Andreas Ludwig Priwin; April 6, 1929 - February 28, 2019) was a German and American conductor, composer, and pianist.

q.p: This English musician was a founding member of the pioneering electronic band Depeche Mode, and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with the group in 2020 — who is he?
q.e: Andy Fletcher (musician) (8 July 1961 - 26 May 2022), also known as Fletch, was an English musician and founding member of the electronic band Depeche Mode.

q.p: Raised in Australia and signed to RSO Records, his 1977 debut album spun off two US chart-toppers including "I Just Want to Be Your Everything" — which late-1970s teen idol?
q.e: Andy Gibb (5 March 1958 - 10 March 1988) was an English singer.

q.p: Inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of the Police in 2003, this English guitarist also composed film scores and exhibited his photography — who is he?
q.e: Andy Summers (born 31 December 1942) is an English guitarist best known as a member of the rock band the Police.

q.p: Born in 2001, this Italian singer-songwriter finished second on the talent show Amici di Maria De Filippi in 2023 before going on to win the Sanremo Music Festival — who is she?
q.e: Angelina Mango (born 10 April 2001) is an Italian singer-songwriter.

q.p: A teenage rock star in her native Jakarta by 1989, this singer later moved to France and broke through internationally with the album Snow on the Sahara — who is she?
q.e: Anggun ((born 29 April 1974) is an Indonesian and French singer, songwriter, actress, and television personality.

q.p: This Belgian pop artist's 2018 single 'Tout oublier,' featuring her brother Roméo Elvis, broke a labelmate's record for weeks atop the Belgian charts — who is she?
q.e: Angèle (singer) (born 3 December 1995), known simply as Angle, is a Belgian singer and songwriter.

q.p: Released in January 1977, this Pink Floyd concept album explores the sociopolitical conditions of mid-1970s Britain, with cover art conceived by bassist Roger Waters — what is it?
q.e: Animals (Pink Floyd album) is the tenth studio album by the English rock band Pink Floyd, released on 21 January 1977, by Harvest Records and Columbia Records.

q.p: This 1960s pop singer and orange juice pitchwoman became a lightning rod in 1977 for spearheading a campaign against a local gay-rights ordinance in Florida — who is she?
q.e: Anita Bryant (March 25, 1940 - December 16, 2024) was an American singer and anti-gay-rights activist.

q.p: This Russian soprano was noticed globally after playing a lead role in a Mozart opera at the 2002 Salzburg Festival, later taking on heavier parts like Lady Macbeth — who is she?
q.e: Anna Netrebko (born 18 September 1971) is a Russian operatic soprano who has performed at the Salzburg Festival, Metropolitan Opera, Vienna State Opera, the Royal Opera and La Scala.

q.p: Recording primarily for Deutsche Grammophon, this German violinist began playing at age five and has earned four Grammy Awards plus a Grand Prix du Disque — who is she?
q.e: Anne-Sophie Mutter (born 29 June 1963) is a German violinist.

q.p: This German rock outfit, founded in Cologne in 2011, keeps most of its lyrics in German but occasionally covers songs in English — which band is this?
q.e: AnnenMayKantereit (occasionally shortened AMK) is a German rock band founded in Cologne in 2011.

q.p: Norwegian-born but raised in Sweden, 'Frida' was one of the lead singers of a pop group that has sold over 400 million records — which singer?
q.e: Anni-Frid Lyngstad (born 15 November 1945), also known simply as Frida, is a Norwegian-born Swedish singer who is best known as one of the founding members and lead singers of the pop band ABBA.

q.p: Half of Eurythmics and famous for a powerful androgynous look, this Scottish singer also became a political activist and philanthropist. Who is she?
q.e: Annie Lennox (born 25 December 1954) is a Scottish singer-songwriter, political activist and philanthropist.

q.p: Once a member of the alternative idol group You'll Melt More!, this Japanese performer later voiced Mem-cho in Oshi no Ko — who is she?
q.e: Ano (singer) (born September 4) is a Japanese singer, songwriter, actress, presenter, and model.

q.p: This actor originated a role in the original Broadway cast of a landmark 1990s rock musical, later playing a Star Trek officer named Paul Stamets — who is he?
q.e: Anthony Rapp (born October 26, 1971) is an American actor and singer who originated the role of Mark Cohen in the Broadway production of Rent.

q.p: Formed in New York City in 1981, this heavy metal band is considered part of thrash metal's Big Four, alongside Metallica, Megadeth, and Slayer — what band is it?
q.e: Anthrax (American band) is an American heavy metal band from New York City, formed in 1981 by rhythm guitarist Scott Ian and bassist Dan Lilker.

q.p: Co-written with Jack Antonoff and built on a 1980s-style LinnDrum beat, this Midnights lead single became one of the most acclaimed tracks of 2022 — can you name it?
q.e: Anti-Hero (song) is a song by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift and the lead single from her tenth studio album, Midnights (2022).

q.p: Known for symphonies emblematic of late Austro-German Romanticism, this Austrian composer and organist also wrote Masses, a Te Deum, and motets — who is he?
q.e: Anton Bruckner (4 September 1824 - 11 October 1896) was an Austrian composer and organist best known for his symphonies and sacred music, which includes Masses, Te Deum and motets.

q.p: A protégé of Christoph Willibald Gluck, this Italian composer wrote operas in three languages and helped shape late 18th-century operatic vocabulary — who was he?
q.e: Antonio Salieri (18 August 1750 - 7 May 1825) was an Italian composer and teacher of the classical period.

q.p: This Italian virtuoso violinist and impresario consolidated the solo concerto into a standard idiom and spawned a wave of imitators across Baroque Europe — who is he?
q.e: Antonio Vivaldi (4 March 1678 - 28 July 1741) was an Italian composer, virtuoso violinist and impresario of Baroque music.

q.p: Debuting in April 2011 with the EP Seven Springs, this South Korean girl group has since released nine Korean EPs and three Japanese studio albums — name the group?
q.e: Apink is a South Korean girl group formed in 2011, currently consists of five members: Chorong, Bomi, Eunji, Namjoo, and Hayoung.

q.p: Its cover shows a Celtic cross over five skulls, one for each band member, but this 1987 hard-rock debut got little attention until its follow-up singles — what album is it?
q.e: Appetite for Destruction is the debut studio album by American hard rock band Guns N' Roses, released on July 21, 1987, by Geffen Records.

q.p: This Danish-Norwegian eurodance group's 1997 single caused controversy and a lawsuit from a toy company over its double entendres about a certain plastic doll. Who are they?
q.e: Aqua (band) was a Danish-Norwegian eurodance band, best known for their 1997 single "Barbie Girl".

q.p: This Canadian indie rock outfit won a Juno for 'Neon Bible' in 2008 before conquering charts with 'The Suburbs' two years later — which band?
q.e: Arcade Fire is a Canadian indie rock band from Montreal, Quebec.

q.p: Formed in Sheffield in 2002, this band rode the early 'blog rock' era to a chart-topping debut, 'Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not' — who are they?
q.e: Arctic Monkeys are an English rock band formed in Sheffield in 2002. It won Best British Album at the 2007 Brit Awards and has been hailed as one of the greatest debut albums.

q.p: After splitting from his reggaeton duo partner De la Ghetto in 2007, this rapper launched a solo career and his own record label, becoming a key figure in Latin trap — who is he?
q.e: Arcángel (born December 23, 1985), better known by his stage name Arcngel, is an American rapper and singer.

q.p: Crowned the "Queen of Soul," this Detroit-raised singer began as a gospel voice in her minister father's church before her breakthrough on Atlantic Records — who is she?
q.e: Aretha Franklin (-; March 25, 1942 - August 16, 2018) was an American singer, songwriter and pianist.

q.p: Formed in Moscow in 1985 and dubbed the 'Russian Iron Maiden' for its NWOBHM-inspired sound, this band was the first Soviet act to break into mainstream success — which group?
q.e: Aria (band) is a Russian heavy metal band that was formed in 1985 in Moscow.

q.p: This Indian playback singer made his debut in 2007 as a child vocalist with the song 'Bum Bum Bole' from Taare Zameen Par — who is he?
q.e: Armaan Malik is an Indian playback singer, songwriter, voice actor, and actor.

q.p: This Filipino singer rose to fame in the Philippines during the 1980s before becoming, in 2007, the new lead singer of the American rock band Journey — who is he?
q.e: Arnel Pineda (born September 5, 1967) is a Filipino singer and songwriter.

q.p: This country artist's 2018 album Girl Going Nowhere followed her breakout single 'A Little Dive Bar in Dahlonega' — who is she?
q.e: Ashley McBryde (born July 29, 1983) is an American country music singer-songwriter.

q.p: Formed in London in 1981 from members of Yes, King Crimson, and Emerson, Lake & Palmer, which supergroup's self-titled debut topped Billboard's albums chart in 1982?
q.e: Asia (band) are an English rock supergroup formed in London in 1981.

q.p: This York-formed rock outfit debuted with 'Stand Up and Scream' in 2009 and saw vocalist Danny Worsnop briefly replaced by Denis Stoff — which band?
q.e: Asking Alexandria are an English rock band formed in York, North Yorkshire, consisting of guitarist Cameron Liddell, drummer James Cassells, vocalist Danny Worsnop, and bassist Sam Bettley.

q.p: This Argentine bandoneonist reinvented traditional tango as 'nuevo tango' by folding in jazz and classical influences, earning praise as tango's foremost composer — who is he?
q.e: Astor Piazzolla (Latin American; March 11, 1921 - July 4, 1992) was an Argentine tango composer, bandoneon player, and arranger.

q.p: This eight-member South Korean boy band, formed by KQ Entertainment, debuted in October 2018 with an EP called Treasure EP.1: All to Zero. What group is it?
q.e: Ateez (stylised in all caps) is a South Korean boy band formed by KQ Entertainment.

q.p: Recorded at what's now known as Abbey Road Studios, this Pink Floyd album's famous Hipgnosis-designed sleeve broke from tradition by showing only a cow in a field — which album?
q.e: Atom Heart Mother is the fifth studio album by the English rock band Pink Floyd.

q.p: This English girl group's single "Whole Again" became one of the best-selling singles of the 2000s in Britain, topping the chart in both the UK and Germany — which group?
q.e: Atomic Kitten were an English girl group formed in Liverpool in 1998, whose original lineup comprised Kerry Katona, Liz McClarnon, and Natasha Hamilton.

q.p: Abbreviated A7X, this California metal band is known for dramatic album-cover imagery and a lineup featuring guitarists Zacky Vengeance and Synyster Gates. Who are they?
q.e: Avenged Sevenfold (abbreviated as A7X) is an American heavy metal band from Huntington Beach, California, formed in 1999.

q.p: Originally the vocalist of a rock band that disbanded in 2020, this Japanese producer now writes and produces music for a duo he formed with vocalist Ikura — who is he?
q.e: Ayase (music producer) (born April 4, 1994) is a Japanese musician, singer, songwriter, and record producer.

q.p: Born Elif Akar in 1998, this German singer topped the domestic charts in 2023 with her second album, 'Schwarzes Herz'. Who is she, by stage name?
q.e: Ayliva (born Elif Akar, 4 April 1998 in Recklinghausen, Germany) is a German singer and musician.

q.p: Born from a Japanese idol group's sub-unit in 2010, this Tokyo trio fused heavy metal with kawaii idol pop, backed by session players called the 'Kami Band' — who are they?
q.e: Babymetal is a Japanese kawaii metal band formed in Tokyo in 2010. Babymetal (Japanese: ベビーメタル, Hepburn: Bebīmetaru), stylized in all caps, is a Japanese kawaii metal band formed in Tokyo in 2010.

q.p: Formed by a major Korean entertainment agency, this seven-member South Korean girl group's debut EP produced the hit single 'Sheesh.' Who are they?
q.e: Babymonster (stylized in all caps), also referred to as Baemon, is a South Korean girl group formed by YG Entertainment.

q.p: Formed in 2004, this Japanese power trio's chart-topping 'Christmas Song' earned a million certification from Japan's recording industry association — who are they?
q.e: Back Number (Bakku Namb) is a Japanese rock power trio formed in 2004.

q.p: This 1980 hard rock album was recorded after its band's original singer died of alcohol poisoning, marking the studio debut of his replacement, Brian Johnson — what is it?
q.e: Back in Black is the seventh studio album by Australian rock band AC/DC, released on 25 July 1980, by Albert Productions and Atlantic Records.

q.p: Formed in Orlando in 1993, this five-man vocal group hit superstardom with 1999's 'Millennium' and its worldwide smash 'I Want It That Way' — who are they?
q.e: Backstreet Boys (often abbreviated as BSB) are an American vocal group and pop boy band consisting of Nick Carter, Howie Dorough, AJ McLean, and cousins Brian Littrell and Kevin Richardson.

q.p: This 2014 pop track, co-written with Max Martin and Shellback, addresses betrayal by a close friend and got a 2015 remix featuring new verses from Kendrick Lamar — which single?
q.e: Bad Blood (Taylor Swift song) is a song by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift from her fifth studio album, 1989 (2014).

q.p: This 1970s English supergroup pulled members from Free, Mott the Hoople, and King Crimson, and scored three straight top-five albums on both sides of the Atlantic. Which band?
q.e: Bad Company were an English rock supergroup formed in London in 1973 by two former members of Free, singer Paul Rodgers and drummer Simon Kirke, former Mott the Hoople guitarist Mick Ralphs and former King Crimson bassist Boz Burrell.

q.p: Classified as an aerophone because air must be blown in to produce sound, this reed instrument stores that air in a bag rather than releasing it directly — what instrument is it?
q.e: Bagpipes is a woodwind instrument using enclosed reeds fed from a constant reservoir of air in the form of a bag.

q.p: Two of its three strings share the same pitch while the third rings a perfect fourth higher on this triangular-bodied Russian folk instrument — what is it?
q.e: Balalaika is a Russian stringed musical instrument with a characteristic triangular wooden, hollow body, fretted neck, and three strings.

q.p: Formed in London in 1980, this Irish-English pop trio holds a Guinness World Record for the most chart entries by any all-female group in history — name the group?
q.e: Bananarama are an Irish-English pop group formed in London in 1980. The group, originally a trio, consisted of friends Sara Dallin, Siobhan Fahey, and Keren Woodward.

q.p: Developed by African Americans from African antecedents, this stringed instrument stretches a thin membrane over a frame to form its resonator — name the instrument?
q.e: Banjo is a stringed instrument with a thin membrane stretched over a frame or cavity to form a resonator.

q.p: Inspired by an exhibit on kitsch culture featuring a famous fashion doll, this 1997 single by a Danish-Norwegian dance-pop group topped charts worldwide — name the song?
q.e: Barbie Girl is a song by Danish-Norwegian dance-pop group Aqua. It was released in April 1997 by Universal and MCA as the third single from the group's debut studio album, Aquarium.

q.p: Beginning her career in the early 1960s at nightclubs and Broadway, this performer has won Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony awards over six decades. Who is she?
q.e: Barbra Streisand (born April 24, 1942) is an American singer, actress, songwriter, and filmmaker.

q.p: Known for the singles 'Pinch Me' and 'One Week,' this Canadian rock group also composed the theme song for The Big Bang Theory — which band?
q.e: Barenaked Ladies (BNL) is a Canadian rock band formed in 1988 in Scarborough.

q.p: A founder of the Bee Gees famed for his high falsetto, this knighted songwriter has written or co-written sixteen Billboard Hot 100 number ones — who is he?
q.e: Barry Gibb (born 1 September 1946) is a British and American musician.

q.p: This Turkish rock singer, who won the TV competition Akademi Türkiye in 2004 and often donated his concert proceeds, died in 2007 following a car accident — who was he?
q.e: Barış Akarsu (June 29, 1979 - July 4, 2007) was a Turkish Anatolian rock singer and actor who rose to fame after winning the television series Akademi Trkiye (Academy Turkey) in July 2004.

q.p: Born Vasiliy Vakulenko, this Russian rapper, singer, and producer also works as a radio host — what is his stage name?
q.e: Basta (rapper) (born Vasiliy Mikhaylovich Vakulenko; April 20, 1980), also known by the stage name Noggano, is a Russian rapper, singer, producer, and radio host.

q.p: Named after a German art school's founding year before shortening it, this English band's 1979 debut single 'Bela Lugosi's Dead' helped launch gothic rock — which group?
q.e: Bauhaus (band) were an English rock band formed in Northampton in 1978.

q.p: This actress and singer won a Tony Award in 1966 before finding TV stardom as a fiery matriarch and later as a wisecracking Miami retiree. Who is she?
q.e: Bea Arthur (born Bernice Frankel; May 13, 1922 - April 25, 2009) was an American actress, comedian, and singer.

q.p: This New York hip-hop trio grew out of a hardcore punk band, scoring early local success with the 1983 comedy single "Cooky Puss." Which group is it?
q.e: Beastie Boys were an American hip-hop group formed in New York City in 1981.

q.p: Produced by Quincy Jones and boasting an unexpected guitar solo by Eddie Van Halen, this third single from 'Thriller' topped the Hot 100 in 1983 — which track is it?
q.e: Beat It is a song by American singer Michael Jackson from his sixth studio album, Thriller (1982).

q.p: A songwriter who co-wrote Eminem's "The Monster," she launched her solo career with the 2015 EP I Don't Wanna Grow Up. Who is she?
q.e: Bebe Rexha (born August 30, 1989) is an American singer and songwriter.

q.p: Developed by younger jazz musicians in the 1940s who wanted a faster, harmonically complex 'musician's music' rather than danceable swing — what style emerged?
q.e: Bebop is a style of jazz developed in the early to mid-1940s in the United States.

q.p: This English singer auditioned on The Voice UK with a John Legend cover, joined Jessie J's team, and topped the UK chart in 2014 alongside Oliver Heldens — who is she?
q.e: Becky Hill (born 14 February 1994) is an English singer.

q.p: This singer co-founded an all-female new wave band in 1978 and fronted its chart-topping 1981 debut album before launching a successful solo career. Who is she?
q.e: Belinda Carlisle (born August 17, 1958) is an American singer and songwriter.

q.p: This American musician fronts the indie rock band Death Cab for Cutie and is also a member of the indie pop supergroup The Postal Service — who is he?
q.e: Ben Gibbard (born August 11, 1976) is an American musician.

q.p: Identical twin brother of Joel, which Good Charlotte guitarist also coached alongside him on The Voice Australia?
q.e: Benji Madden (n Combs; born March 11, 1979) is an American musician and songwriter.

q.p: This Swedish musician, a member of the pop group ABBA, co-composed the musicals Chess and Mamma Mia! and served as executive producer on both Mamma Mia! films — who is he?
q.e: Benny Andersson (born 16 December 1946) is a Swedish musician, composer and producer best known as a member of the pop group ABBA and co-composer of the musicals Chess, Kristina frn Duvemla, and Mamma Mia!

q.p: This 1980s Arabesque music icon of Turkey broke sales records with her album 'Woman of Pains' and inspired a 2022 biographical film about her life — who is she?
q.e: Bergen (singer) (born Belgin Sarlmer; 15 July 1958 - 14 August 1989) was a Turkish singer.

q.p: Whose solo debut, Dangerously in Love (2003), became one of the century's best-selling albums after she'd first found fame fronting one of history's best-selling girl groups?
q.e: Beyoncé (bee-; ne Knowles; born September 4, 1981) is an American singer, songwriter, actress, and businesswoman.

q.p: After finishing runner-up on SBS's The Fan in 2018, this South Korean singer released the 2022 album Lowlife Princess: Noir and later starred in the film Hopeless — who is she?
q.e: Bibi (singer) is a South Korean singer, rapper, songwriter, and actress.

q.p: Classically trained at Mannes, this jazz pianist joined Miles Davis's sextet in 1958 and reshaped the music with impressionist harmony and "singing" melodic lines — who was he?
q.e: Bill Evans (August 16, 1929 - September 15, 1980) was an American jazz pianist and composer who worked primarily as the leader of his trio.

q.p: Born in 1989, this German singer-songwriter fronts the pop-rock band Tokio Hotel and records solo under the name Billy — who is he?
q.e: Bill Kaulitz (German; born 1 September 1989), also known as Billy for his solo project, is a German singer and songwriter.

q.p: Known for his deep bass-baritone voice in the Righteous Brothers, this singer also had a string of country chart hits in the 1980s — who is he?
q.e: Bill Medley (born September 19, 1940) is an American singer best known as one of the Righteous Brothers.

q.p: Hailed as one of punk's greatest singers and guitarists, this songwriter co-founded his famous band with Mike Dirnt in 1987 and also sings for Pinhead Gunpowder — who is he?
q.e: Billie Joe Armstrong (born February 17, 1972) is an American musician, songwriter and actor.

q.p: Having sold over 160 million records, this pianist earned a nickname from his 1973 signature song and once released a one-off album of classical compositions — who is he?
q.e: Billy Joel (born May 9, 1949) is an American singer, songwriter, and pianist.

q.p: This Tony-winning star of Kinky Boots made history in 2019 as the first openly gay Black man to win a lead-acting Emmy, for his role in Pose — who is he?
q.e: Billy Porter (born September 21, 1969) is an American singer, actor, writer, director and businessperson.

q.p: A top session keyboardist who backed the Beatles and the Rolling Stones in the 1960s, this musician later scored his own Grammy-winning solo hit with 'Outa-Space'. Who is he?
q.e: Billy Preston (September 2, 1946 - June 6, 2006) was an American keyboardist, singer, and songwriter whose work encompassed R&B, rock, soul, funk, and gospel.

q.p: With eight top-ten country hits and the line-dance smash 'Achy Breaky Heart,' this country singer-actor saw his debut 'Some Gave All' certified 9× multi-platinum — who is he?
q.e: Billy Ray Cyrus (born August 25, 1961) is an American singer, songwriter and actor.

q.p: This Japanese alternative idol girl group, founded in 2015 as a spiritual successor to an earlier group by the same manager, disbanded in June 2023 — name the group?
q.e: Bish (group) was a Japanese alternative idol girl group founded in 2015 by their manager Junnosuke Watanabe.

q.p: This Swedish musician, the oldest member of a legendary pop quartet, co-wrote musicals including Chess and Mamma Mia! and co-produced its film adaptations. Who is he?
q.e: Björn Ulvaeus (born 25 April 1945) is a Swedish musician, singer, songwriter, and producer best known as a member of the musical group ABBA.

q.p: This country star and TV personality broke through with the five-week chart-topper 'Austin' in 2001 and later covered Michael Bublé's 'Home' — who is he?
q.e: Blake Shelton (born June 18, 1976) is an American country singer, songwriter, and television personality.

q.p: Released as the second single from After Hours in late 2019, this synth-heavy, '80s-tinged track by a Canadian singer became a global smash and critical favorite — what is it?
q.e: Blinding Lights is a song by Canadian singer-songwriter the Weeknd, from his fourth studio album, After Hours (2020).

q.p: Formed in Poway, California in 1992, this band blends catchy pop melodies with fast punk and made its debut with the album Cheshire Cat — who are they?
q.e: Blink-182 is an American rock band formed in Poway, California, in 1992.

q.p: Born from New York's CBGB scene in 1974 around Debbie Harry and Chris Stein, this new wave act blended punk, disco, reggae and early hip hop — which band is it?
q.e: Blondie (band) is an American new wave band formed in New York City in 1974 by singer Debbie Harry and guitarist Chris Stein.

q.p: This 1991 Red Hot Chili Peppers album peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard 200 thanks to hits like 'Suck My Kiss' and 'Breaking the Girl' — which career-defining record?
q.e: Blood Sugar Sex Magik is the fifth studio album by American rock band Red Hot Chili Peppers, released on September 24, 1991, by Warner Bros.

q.p: Released in 1983 as a 12-inch single in a famously die-cut sleeve, this Eurodisco and synth-pop track by an English rock band became a dancefloor landmark. What song is it?
q.e: Blue Monday (New Order song) is a song by the English rock band New Order.

q.p: This London band started out wrapped in Madchester and shoegaze on their 1991 debut, then helped ignite Britpop with Parklife and the hit 'Girls & Boys' — who are they?
q.e: Blur (band) are an English rock band formed in London in 1988, consisting of singer Damon Albarn, guitarist Graham Coxon, bassist Alex James, and drummer Dave Rowntree.

q.p: This Irish rock frontman played Pink in a Pink Floyd film adaptation before becoming world-famous for organizing a charity single with a fellow musician in 1984 — who is he?
q.e: Bob Geldof (born 5 October 1951) is an Irish singer-songwriter, political activist, television producer and entrepreneur.

q.p: This Jamaican reggae legend, born 1945, became a Rastafarian icon whose music carried messages of democratic reform and pan-Africanism before his death in 1981. Who was he?
q.e: Bob Marley (6 February 1945 - 11 May 1981) was a Jamaican reggae singer, songwriter, and guitarist.

q.p: This Grateful Dead co-founder played mostly rhythm guitar, sang lead on many songs, and founded bands like RatDog and Kingfish after the group's 1995 breakup — who is he?
