q.e: Bob Weir (WEER; n Parber; October 16, 1947 - January 10, 2026) was an American musician and songwriter best known as a founding member of the Grateful Dead.

q.p: The only child of Whitney Houston, this reality TV personality appeared on a show about her parents and covered her mother's hit 'I'm Your Baby Tonight' — who was she?
q.e: Bobbi Kristina Brown (March 4, 1993 - July 26, 2015) was an American reality television personality and singer.

q.p: One of the first women in the US to write and produce her own material, this singer earned a Grammy for Best New Artist after her 1967 hit about Billie Joe -- who is she?
q.e: Bobbie Gentry (born Roberta Lee Streeter, July 27, 1942) is an American retired singer-songwriter.

q.p: This Aruban dancer, singer, and DJ was a member of the influential 1970s and '80s disco group Boney M — who is he?
q.e: Bobby Farrell (6 October 1949 - 30 December 2010) was an Aruban dancer, singer and DJ.

q.p: Built on one relentlessly repeated theme, this 1928 orchestral work was among Maurice Ravel's last completed pieces before illness ended his composing — which is it?
q.e: Boléro is a 1928 work for large orchestra by French composer Maurice Ravel.

q.p: Formed in Sayreville, New Jersey in 1983, this band broke through with 1986's Slippery When Wet and its trio of Top 10 hits. Which rock group is it?
q.e: Bon Jovi is an American rock band formed in Sayreville, New Jersey in 1983. In 1984, Bon Jovi released their self-titled debut album, and its single "Runaway" managed to reach the Top 40 of the Billboard Hot 100.

q.p: This Australian was AC/DC's second lead vocalist from 1974 until his death in 1980, ranked number one in Classic Rock's '100 Greatest Frontmen' — who was he?
q.e: Bon Scott (9 July 1946 - 19 February 1980) was an Australian singer who was the second lead vocalist and lyricist of the hard rock band AC/DC from 1974 until his death in 1980.

q.p: A roots-and-blues singer who collaborated with everyone from Warren Zevon to John Prine, she finally hit number one in 1989 with her tenth album, 'Nick of Time' — who is she?
q.e: Bonnie Raitt (born November 8, 1949) is an American singer-songwriter.

q.p: Released in January 2012 and reissued later that year as 'The Paradise Edition,' this Lana Del Rey album became one of the year's five best-selling records worldwide — which album?
q.e: Born to Die is the second studio album by American singer-songwriter, and record producer Lana Del Rey.

q.p: A former bandmate of Steve Miller who later launched a solo career, this singer-guitarist's 1976 album Silk Degrees produced the hits 'Lido Shuffle' and 'Lowdown' — who is he?
q.e: Boz Scaggs (born June 8, 1944) is an American singer, songwriter, and guitarist.

q.p: This American singer, frontman of a Long Beach ska band, died of a heroin overdose in a San Francisco hotel in 1996 while the group was on tour — who is he?
q.e: Bradley Nowell (February 22, 1968 - May 25, 1996) was an American musician and the lead singer of the band Sublime.

q.p: This American singer-songwriter has won eleven Grammy Awards across folk, alternative country, and Americana, and was named one of Time's Women of the Year in 2026. Who is she?
q.e: Brandi Carlile (born June 1, 1981) is an American singer-songwriter and producer.

q.p: This singer has recorded eight studio albums fronting Incubus and also collaborates with producer Brendan O'Brien under the name Sons of the Sea — who is he?
q.e: Brandon Boyd (born February 15, 1976) is an American musician, best known as the lead vocalist of the rock band Incubus, with whom he has recorded eight studio albums.

q.p: This American musician co-founded the Las Vegas rock band the Killers with Dave Keuning in 2001, serving as lead vocalist, and has also released two solo albums — who is he?
q.e: Brandon Flowers (born June 21, 1981) is an American musician.

q.p: The only constant member across his band's 19-year run, this singer disbanded the pop-rock outfit Panic! at the Disco in 2023 to focus on raising his child. Who is he?
q.e: Brendon Urie (born April 12, 1987) is an American singer, songwriter, and musician who is best known as the lead vocalist and frontman of Panic!

q.p: He led the band Geordie to a UK Top 10 hit before stepping in as AC/DC's third lead singer after Bon Scott's death — which English vocalist is it?
q.e: Brian Johnson (born 5 October 1947) is an English singer and songwriter.

q.p: He named the Rolling Stones and founded them in 1962, but drink and drug troubles eroded his studio role before his death at 27 in 1969 — which founding member was he?
q.e: Brian Jones (28 February 1942 - 3 July 1969) was an English musician and one of the founders of the Rolling Stones.

q.p: An animal-welfare activist and astrophysicist as well as a guitarist, he co-founded one of the world's biggest rock bands in 1970 alongside a singer and drummer — who is he?
q.e: Brian May (born 19 July 1947) is an English musician, animal welfare activist, and astrophysicist.

q.p: Which Irish pop star left his boy band in 2004, released a debut solo album called Irish Son, and later paired with Keith Duffy as boyzlife?
q.e: Brian McFadden (born 12 April 1980) is an Irish pop singer and television presenter.

q.p: This musician favors aggressive guitar work and non-standard tunings as the lyricist and lead singer of Placebo — who is he?
q.e: Brian Molko (born 10 December 1972) is a British-American musician who is the lead vocalist, guitarist, and lyricist of the band Placebo.

q.p: Shaped by George Gershwin and Phil Spector and famed for his falsetto and lush harmonies, which Beach Boys co-founder served as the band's songwriter and producer?
q.e: Brian Wilson (June 20, 1942 - June 11, 2025) was an American musician, singer, songwriter and record producer who co-founded the Beach Boys.

q.p: She played Teddy Duncan on Good Luck Charlie, then swapped Hollywood for MIT, Harvard, and co-founding the satellite startup Northwood Space — who is she?
q.e: Bridgit Mendler (born December 18, 1992) is an American entrepreneur and former actress and singer-songwriter.

q.p: Formed in Sheffield, England in 2004, this rock band's debut album leaned into a deathcore sound before their second album pivoted toward metalcore. Who are they?
q.e: Bring Me the Horizon are a British rock band formed in 2004 in Sheffield, England. The group currently consists of lead vocalist Oli Sykes, drummer Matt Nicholls, guitarist Lee Malia and bassist Matt Kean.

q.p: Amy Lee wrote this Evanescence debut single at 19, and the label insisted on male guest vocals from 12 Stones' Paul McCoy against her wishes — what song is it?
q.e: Bring Me to Life is the debut single by American rock band Evanescence from their debut studio album, Fallen (2003).

q.p: Born as a guitar-bright, defiantly British answer to American grunge and a cornerstone of the 'Cool Britannia' mood, which 1990s music movement echoed the Swinging Sixties?
q.e: Britpop was a British music and cultural movement that emerged in the 1990s.

q.p: After the Distillers disbanded in 2006, which Australian punk musician launched Spinnerette and later a solo career under a stage name?
q.e: Brody Dalle (born Bree Joanna Alice Robinson, 1 January 1979) is an Australian singer, songwriter, and musician.

q.p: All members of this 1983 London synth-pop trio were openly gay, and their biggest single reached number one in the Dutch, Italian, and Belgian charts — which band?
q.e: Bronski Beat were a synth-pop band formed in 1983 in London, England.

q.p: Released by a British rock band in 1985, this record became the first ever to sell over a million copies on CD and spent nine weeks atop the Billboard 200 - which record?
q.e: Brothers in Arms (album) is the fifth studio album by the British rock band Dire Straits, released on 17 May 1985, by Vertigo Records internationally and Warner Bros.

q.p: Which Grammy-winning pianist led his band the Noisemakers and also toured as a member of the Grateful Dead in the early 1990s?
q.e: Bruce Hornsby (born November 23, 1954) is an American singer-songwriter and pianist.

q.p: The most-played artist on Canadian radio in the 2010s, this singer broke through in 1983 with the album Cuts Like a Knife — who is he?
q.e: Bryan Adams (born November 5, 1959) is a Canadian singer-songwriter, musician, record producer, and photographer.

q.p: This English singer studied fine art and taught school before assembling a band in 1970 that hit international success with its 1972 self-titled debut — who is he?
q.e: Bryan Ferry (born 26 September 1945) is an English singer and musician.

q.p: Formed in Los Angeles in 1966 by a mix of Canadian and American musicians including Neil Young, which band helped pioneer folk rock alongside the Byrds?
q.e: Buffalo Springfield was a Canadian-American rock band formed in Los Angeles in 1966 by Canadians Neil Young, Bruce Palmer and Dewey Martin and Americans Stephen Stills and Richie Furay.

q.p: This singer-songwriter and Indigenous-rights activist co-wrote "Up Where We Belong," which won the Best Original Song Oscar for An Officer and a Gentleman — who is she?
q.e: Buffy Sainte-Marie (born Beverley Jean Santamaria; February 20, 1941) is an American singer-songwriter, musician, and social activist.

q.p: Formed in 1994 in Chiba, this Japanese alternative rock quartet has placed every release since its third single in the Oricon Weekly top ten — what band is it?
q.e: Bump of Chicken is a Japanese alternative rock group from Sakura, Chiba.

q.p: This folk singer turned actor won an Academy Award for playing Rufus Hannassey in a 1958 Western, after a radio career that made him a CBS star — who is he?
q.e: Burl Ives (June 14, 1909 - April 14, 1995) was an American singer and actor with a career that spanned more than six decades.

q.p: This American composer and pianist, a giant of orchestral pop and easy listening, wrote hundreds of songs often in partnership with lyricist Hal David — who is he?
q.e: Burt Bacharach (May 12, 1928 - February 8, 2023) was an American composer, songwriter, record producer, and pianist, widely regarded as one of the most important and influential figures of 20th-century popular music.

q.p: Fronted by Gavin Rossdale since forming in London in 1992, this rock band's debut album Sixteen Stone went six-times platinum — which band?
q.e: Bush (British band) are an English rock band formed in London in 1992.

q.p: Produced by Greg Kurstin, this Foo Fighters record is dedicated to both a late drummer and Dave Grohl's mother, who died the same year it was written — which album?
q.e: But Here We Are is the eleventh studio album by American rock band Foo Fighters, released on June 2, 2023.

q.p: Known offstage as Caroline Catherine Müller, this Dutch-German singer teamed up with Dieter Bohlen — one half of Modern Talking — for a string of 1980s hits. Who is she?
q.e: C. C. Catch (born 31 July 1964), known professionally as C.C.

q.p: Known for the mixtape Avida Dollars and its hit 'Llorando en la Limo,' this Spanish rapper got his start rhyming under the alias Crema — who is he?
q.e: C. Tangana (born July 16, 1990), known professionally as C. Tangana, is a Spanish rapper.

q.p: She rose to fame in Fifth Harmony before going solo, scoring a number-four hit 'Bad Things' with Machine Gun Kelly and a chart-topping Latin-flavored debut album — who is she?
q.e: Camila Cabello (Latin American; born March 3, 1997) is an American singer and songwriter.

q.p: Based on the melody of the 1784 French song 'Plaisir d'amour,' this song was originally written from a woman's perspective before becoming a famous romantic ballad — name the song?
q.e: Can't Help Falling in Love is a song written by Hugo Peretti, Luigi Creatore, and George David Weiss and published by Gladys Music, Inc.

q.p: Co-written by Bob Crewe and Bob Gaudio, this 1967 single gave Frankie Valli a gold record and a No. 2 spot on the Hot 100, remaining his top solo hit for years — which song?
o: Can't Take My Eyes Off You
q.e: Can't Take My Eyes Off You is a 1967 song written by Bob Crewe and Bob Gaudio, and first recorded and released as a single by Gaudio's Four Seasons bandmate Frankie Valli.

q.p: Formed in 1973, this Japanese idol trio of three young women debuted with the single 'Anata ni Muchū' — name the group?
q.e: Candies (group) (Kyandzu) was a Japanese idol trio formed in 1973, their first single being "Anata ni Much".

q.p: After playing Monterey and Woodstock in the late 1960s, this Los Angeles blues rock band built its name from a 1928 Tommy Johnson song about drinking Sterno — which band?
q.e: Canned Heat is an American blues rock band that was formed in Los Angeles in 1965.

q.p: Despite almost no radio or TV exposure, this death metal band formed in Buffalo in 1988 built a cult following and sold two million albums worldwide by 2015 — what's the band?
q.e: Cannibal Corpse is an American death metal band formed in Buffalo, New York, in 1988, now based in Tampa, Florida.

q.p: This English model-turned-actress played Laureline in Valerian and Margo Roth Spiegelman in Paper Towns after winning Model of the Year twice — who is she?
q.e: Cara Delevingne (born 12 August 1992) is an English model, actress, and musician.

q.p: The youngest of three musical brothers, this guitarist co-founded the Beach Boys and served as the band's de facto leader in the early-to-mid 1970s — who is he?
q.e: Carl Wilson (December 21, 1946 - February 6, 1998) was an American musician, singer, and songwriter who co-founded the Beach Boys.

q.p: This singer cofounded the indie pop duo Chairlift, known for the sleeper hit 'Bruises', before going solo and releasing the acclaimed avant-pop album Pang in 2019 — who is she?
q.e: Caroline Polachek (born June 20, 1985) is an American singer, producer, and songwriter.

q.p: After winning the fourth season of American Idol, this singer became the first-ever country artist to debut atop the Billboard Hot 100. Who is she?
q.e: Carrie Underwood (born March 10, 1983) is an American singer and songwriter.

q.p: This Mexican artist specializes in several subgenres of regional Mexican music and performs under a stage name rather than his birth name — who is he?
q.e: Carín León (born 26 July 1989), known professionally as Carn Len, is a Mexican singer-songwriter who specializes in regional Mexican music.

q.p: Discovered by producer Ryan Leslie and later signed by a hip hop mogul, this singer's 2006 debut single became her first Billboard Hot 100 entry. Who is she?
q.e: Cassie Ventura (ven-; born August 26, 1986) is an American singer, dancer, actress, and model.

q.p: Portrayed by Patti D'Arbanville in a 1989 film, this Canadian backup singer served over a year in prison for a fatal 1982 drug incident involving a famous actor — who is she?
q.e: Cathy Smith (April 25, 1947 - August 16, 2020), also known as Silverbag, was a Canadian backup singer, groupie, drug dealer, and legal secretary.

q.p: After her film career slowed in the 2010s, this Hong Kong actress and singer — known for The Promise and Running on Karma — shifted toward Chinese reality television — who is she?
q.e: Cecilia Cheung (born 24 May 1980) is a Hong Kong actress and singer.

q.p: Said to have sung in her heart to the Lord as musicians played at her own wedding, this Christian virgin martyr became the patron saint of music and musicians — who was she?
q.e: Cecilia of Rome was a Christian virgin martyr, who is venerated in Roman Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Anglican, and some Lutheran churches, such as the Church of Sweden.

q.p: Daughter of two legendary reggae musicians, which Jamaican singer toured with a sibling-led band that picked up three Grammy Awards?
q.e: Cedella Marley (born 23 August 1967) is a Jamaican singer.

q.p: Having led a post-hardcore group and later a band called Antemasque, this American singer is best known for fronting a prog-rock act he founded in 2001 — who is he?
q.e: Cedric Bixler-Zavala (born November 4, 1974) is an American musician.

q.p: Known as the 'Barefoot Diva' for performing without shoes, this Cape Verdean singer of morna won a Grammy in 2004 and even influenced Madonna — who was she?
q.e: Cesária Évora (Portuguese; 27 August 1941 - 17 December 2011) was a Cape Verdean singer known for singing morna, a genre of music from Cape Verde, in her native Cape Verdean Creole.

q.p: This Canadian musician, born under a different surname, is the lead singer, lead guitarist, and founding member of a hugely successful Canadian rock band — who is he?
q.e: Chad Kroeger (n Turton; born November 15, 1974) is a Canadian musician who is best known for being the lead singer, lead guitarist, primary songwriter, and founding member of the rock band Nickelback.

q.p: The longest-serving drummer of a Rock and Roll Hall of Fame band since joining in 1988, this musician also drums for the supergroup Chickenfoot — who is he?
q.e: Chad Smith (born October 25, 1961) is an American musician who is the drummer of the rock band the Red Hot Chili Peppers.

q.p: The youngest of eight children from rural Sinaloa, he's now called 'The King of Corrido' for his narcocorridos about crime and the cartels — which Mexican singer?
q.e: Chalino Sánchez (30 August 1960 - 16 May 1992) was a Mexican singer and composer.

q.p: Rising to fame in Girls Aloud, this English singer was part of the UK's best-selling girl group of the 21st century, which won a Brit Award for "The Promise" — who is she?
q.e: Cheryl (singer) (born 30 June 1983) is an English singer and television personality.

q.p: Frontman of Linkin Park, his band's debut Hybrid Theory (2000) earned Diamond status. He also fronted Grey Daze and Stone Temple Pilots. Who was he?
q.e: Chester Bennington (March 20, 1976 - July 20, 2017) was an American singer and songwriter who was the lead vocalist of the rock band Linkin Park.

q.p: He helped birth jazz fusion in Miles Davis's late-1960s band, later founded Return to Forever, and walked away with 29 Grammys — which pianist who wrote 'Spain' is this?
q.e: Chick Corea (June 12, 1941 - February 9, 2021) was an American jazz pianist, composer, bandleader, and occasional percussionist.

q.p: Originally formed in 1993 as Inearthed, which Finnish metal band became one of the country's best-selling acts with over 250,000 records sold at home?
q.e: Children of Bodom are a Finnish melodic death metal band from Espoo, Uusimaa.

q.p: Before headlining The CW's 'Black Lightning' as a teen superhero, this actress and singer got her start playing Uma in Disney's 'Descendants' franchise — who is she?
q.e: China Anne McClain (born August 25, 1998) is an American actress and singer.

q.p: Known for his dramatic tenor and distinctive screams, this alt-metal band's frontman also fronts the side projects Team Sleep and Crosses — who is he?
q.e: Chino Moreno (born June 20, 1973) is an American musician who is best known as the lead vocalist and primary lyricist of the alternative metal band Deftones.

q.p: Before her platinum 2021 solo single 'Have Mercy,' this singer rose to fame as half of a duo with her sister Halle and starred in 'Grown-ish' and 'Swarm' — who is she?
q.e: Chloe Bailey (born July 1, 1998), also known mononymously as Chle, is an American singer-songwriter, record producer, and actress.

q.p: In 2008 this South Korean idol debuted as a member of the boy band Shinee, going on to release a solo EP called 'Chase' in 2022 — who is he?
q.e: Choi Min-ho (born December 9, 1991), known mononymously as Minho, is a South Korean singer, songwriter, rapper and actor.

q.p: Known mononymously by her stage name, this South Korean singer-actress debuted in a short-lived Japanese duo before joining a hugely successful girl group in 2007 — who is she?
q.e: Choi Soo-young (born February 10, 1990), known mononymously as Sooyoung, is a South Korean singer, actress, and songwriter.

q.p: A former member of a South Korean-Japanese girl group formed on a reality survival show, this singer and actress launched her solo career in January 2022 — who is she?
q.e: Choi Ye-na is a South Korean singer and actress. Choi Ye-na (Korean: 최예나, born September 29, 1999), known mononymously as Yena, is a South Korean singer and actress.

q.p: With his 2005 debut single 'Run It!', this R&B singer became the first male artist since 1995 to top the Billboard Hot 100 with a debut — who is he?
q.e: Chris Brown (born May 5, 1989) is an American singer, songwriter, dancer and actor.

q.p: American musician (1964–2017), best known as lead vocalist of Soundgarden and Audioslave—founder of Temple of the Dog tribute band—regarded as one of grunge's greatest singers—who?
q.e: Chris Cornell (n Boyle; July 20, 1964 - May 18, 2017) was an American musician, best known as the lead vocalist, rhythm guitarist, and primary lyricist for the rock bands Soundgarden and Audioslave.

q.p: Singing countertenor, this American performer founded a pop group that's sold over 70 million records and remains one of the best-selling boy bands in history. Who is he?
q.e: Chris Kirkpatrick (born October 17, 1971) is an American singer, songwriter, dancer, music producer, podcaster, and actor.

q.p: Born in 1977, this English singer-pianist formed his record-shattering band with Jonny Buckland, Guy Berryman, and Will Champion at university — who is he?
q.e: Chris Martin (born 2 March 1977) is an English singer, songwriter and music producer.

q.p: Known for his deep, distinctive voice, this former Saturday Night Live cast member voices Cyril Figgis on Archer and narrates the PBS series WordGirl — who is he?
q.e: Chris Parnell (par-NELL; born February 5, 1967) is an American actor and comedian.

q.p: Discovered for his guitar skills by the band's producer, this San Antonio-raised musician joined a Tejano group and later married its lead singer — who is he?
q.e: Chris Pérez (born August 14, 1969) is an American guitarist best known for having been the lead guitarist of the Tejano music band Selena y Los Dinos.

q.p: Between 2011 and 2019, this musician also fronted a side project called the Brotherhood, before returning full-time to the rock band he and his brother founded in 1984 — who is he?
q.e: Chris Robinson (singer) (born December 20, 1966) is an American musician.

q.p: This singer-guitarist co-founded a rock band in Hereford, England, in 1978 and remains its only original member, serving as lead vocalist and chief songwriter. Who is she?
q.e: Chrissie Hynde (born September 7, 1951) is an American-British singer, songwriter, and musician.

q.p: This actor-musician played Lindsey McDonald on Angel and moonlights as the frontman of a country-rock band that released The House Rules in 2010 — who is he?
q.e: Christian Kane is an American actor and singer-songwriter.

q.p: Born in Sonora, this musician's debut album "Me Dejé Llevar" produced back-to-back number-one hits on Mexico's Monitor Latino chart — who is he?
q.e: Christian Nodal (born 11 January 1999) is a Mexican singer and songwriter.

q.p: She built a following posting covers on YouTube, then finished third on The Voice under Adam Levine, who promised to sign her to 222 Records — which singer?
q.e: Christina Grimmie (March 12, 1994 - June 10, 2016) was an American singer, songwriter, and internet personality.

q.p: Which English musician joined Fleetwood Mac as a session player in 1968, then stayed on as keyboardist and songwriter through the band's many lineup changes?
q.e: Christine McVie (ne Perfect; 12 July 1943 - 30 November 2022) was an English musician.

q.p: This Danish pop singer from Copenhagen was named New Thinker of the Year by Spotify and has released five studio albums beginning with 2012's Colours — who is he?
q.e: Christopher (singer) (Danish; born 31 January 1992) is a Danish singer from Copenhagen, signed to EMI Denmark.

q.p: This American actress played Ren Stevens on a Disney Channel sitcom while also voicing the title spy in an animated series — who is she?
q.e: Christy Carlson Romano (born March 20, 1984) is an American actress, podcaster, and singer.

q.p: He turned a Hank Ballard B-side into a worldwide dance craze in 1960, then added lyrics and a now-famous bar to the Champs' "Limbo Rock" — which singer?
q.e: Chubby Checker (born Ernest Evans; October 3, 1941) is an American rock and roll singer and dancer.

q.p: He refined rhythm and blues into rock and roll with songs like "Roll Over Beethoven" and "Johnny B. Goode," earning him a fitting "Father of Rock and Roll" nickname — who was he?
q.e: Chuck Berry (October 18, 1926 - March 18, 2017) was an American guitarist, singer, and songwriter who was one of the pioneers of rock and roll.

q.p: Known for anarcho-communist politics and the smash single 'Tubthumping,' which English band formed in Burnley in 1982?
q.e: Chumbawamba were an English band who formed in Burnley in 1982. In 2012, Chumbawamba announced they were splitting up after 30 years.

q.p: This American singer, a member of a pop vocal trio, is the daughter of two Mamas & the Papas band members and half-sister to two other performers — who is she?
q.e: Chynna Phillips (born February 12, 1968) is an American singer and actress.

q.p: Discovered by producer Jazze Pha in the early 2000s, this singer's debut album spawned hits like '1, 2 Step' featuring Missy Elliott. Who is she?
q.e: Ciara (see-AIR-; ne Harris; born October 25, 1985) is an American singer, songwriter, dancer and actress.

q.p: Formed in El Paso in 2008 by Greg Gonzalez, this dream pop band's androgynous vocals anchor a sleeper hit that took off years later through commercial licensing — what band is it?
q.e: Cigarettes After Sex is an American dream pop band formed in El Paso, Texas, in 2008 by Greg Gonzalez.

q.p: This jazz singer and 1976 Miss World titleholder from Jamaica became the mother of reggae musician Damian Marley — who is she?
q.e: Cindy Breakspeare (born October 24, 1954) is a Canadian-Jamaican jazz singer and beauty queen.

q.p: Born Wieck in Leipzig, this 19th-century piano virtuoso composed solo works, a concerto, and chamber music across six decades on the concert stage — who is she?
q.e: Clara Schumann (ne Wieck; 13 September 1819 - 20 May 1896) was a German virtuoso pianist, composer, and piano teacher.

q.p: Nicknamed Cloclo, this French pop singer co-wrote the lyrics to "Comme d'habitude" — the tune the English-speaking world later knew as "My Way" — who is it?
q.e: Claude François (French; 1 February 1939 - 11 March 1978), also known by the nickname Cloclo, was a French pop singer, composer, songwriter, record producer, drummer and dancer.

q.p: This American Idol season-two runner-up wrote a bestselling memoir called Learning to Sing and hosted his own televised Christmas special in 2004 — who is he?
q.e: Clay Aiken (n Grissom; born November 30, 1978) is an American singer, television personality, actor and political activist.

q.p: Compared in style to Led Zeppelin's John Bonham, this bassist joined Metallica in 1982 and profoundly shaped the band's sound before his death in 1986. Who is he?
q.e: Cliff Burton (February 10, 1962 - September 27, 1986) was an American musician who served as the bassist for the heavy metal band Metallica from 1982 until his death in 1986.

q.p: Inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2003 as AC/DC's bassist, he came out of a brief retirement to record Power Up in 2020 — who is he?
q.e: Cliff Williams (born 14 December 1949) is an English musician, best known as the bassist and backing vocalist of the Australian hard rock band AC/DC.

q.p: This American actor shot to stardom in the 1950s title role of the Western series Cheyenne, after first appearing in Cecil B. DeMille's The Ten Commandments — who is he?
q.e: Clint Walker (May 30, 1927 - May 21, 2018) was an American actor.

q.p: This American record executive led Columbia Records in the late 1960s, then founded both Arista Records and later J Records — who is he?
q.e: Clive Davis (April 4, 1932 - June 22, 2026) was an American record executive, A&R executive, record producer and lawyer.

q.p: Famous for her Americanized dance routines and 18 studio albums, this Chinese-American singer voiced the Mandarin Fa Mulan and sang "Reflection" — who was she?
q.e: Coco Lee (17 January 1975 - 5 July 2023) was a Chinese-American singer, songwriter, and actress.

q.p: The daughter of rapper and media executive Benzino, this American rapper and singer broke into the Hot 100's top 40 in 2021 with a Lil Durk remix of one of her songs — who is she?
q.e: Coi Leray (born May 11, 1997) is an American rapper and singer.

q.p: This Canadian country-folk artist debuted in 2017 with a self-titled album, followed a year later by 'Songs of the Plains' — who is he?
q.e: Colter Wall (born June 27, 1995) is a Canadian singer, songwriter, and musician.

q.p: Raised in Georgetown, Texas, this American singer-songwriter got his start uploading songs to YouTube as a teenager before signing with Republic Records in 2018 — who is he?
q.e: Conan Gray (born December 5, 1998) is an American singer, songwriter and former YouTuber.

q.p: He co-founded Stone Sour in Des Moines in 1992, then joined a masked metal band in 1997 to replace its original singer — which American vocalist is it?
q.e: Corey Taylor (born December 8, 1973) is an American musician, songwriter, author and actor.

q.p: Once a singer-songwriter, this English actor gained wide recognition portraying John Blackthorne in the 2024 historical drama series Shōgun — who is he?
q.e: Cosmo Jarvis (born 1989 or 1990) is an English actor and former singer-songwriter.

q.p: This American rock band earned two Grammy nominations in 1994 on the strength of their breakthrough album August and Everything After — which band?
q.e: Counting Crows is an American rock band from Berkeley, California.

q.p: This post-grunge rock band, formed in Tallahassee in 1994, released a second album that went diamond and helped it sell over 28 million records in the U.S. alone. What is it?
q.e: Creed (band) is an American rock band formed in Tallahassee, Florida, in 1994.

q.p: Having sold over 12 million records, this Mexican pop singer is the nephew of the actor who famously played Don Ramón in El Chavo del Ocho — who is he?
q.e: Cristian Castro (born 8 December 1974) is a Mexican pop singer.

q.p: This Melbourne-formed rock band, led by Neil Finn, topped the charts with 'Don't Dream It's Over' from their self-titled debut — which band?
q.e: Crowded House are an Australian/New Zealand rock band, formed in 1985 in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia.

q.p: Issued in the U.S. by Merge Records and in Canada by Dine Alone, this is the second studio album from Montreal-based artist Little Scream — which album?
q.e: Cult Following is the second studio album by American-born, Montreal-based indie rock artist Little Scream (Laurel Sprengelmeyer).

q.p: This 1981 London-formed pop band led by Boy George sold more than 50 million records with hits like 'Karma Chameleon' — which band?
q.e: Culture Club are an English pop band formed in London in 1981.

q.p: A sped-up 'Twin version' of this bubblegum K-pop hit about unrequited love went viral on TikTok, becoming a small label's breakout smash on the Billboard Hot 100 -- which track?
q.e: Cupid (Fifty Fifty song) is a song recorded by South Korean girl group Fifty Fifty.

q.p: Which of these was an official language of Union between Sweden and Norway?
q.e: Union between Sweden and Norway: Swedish. The Norwegian government was presided over by viceroys: Swedes until 1829, Norwegians until 1856.

q.p: Which of these was an official language of Denmark–Norway?
q.e: Denmark–Norway: Danish. The state also claimed sovereignty over three historical peoples: Frisians, Gutes and Wends.

q.p: Who is credited with discovering Mycenaean Greece?
q.e: Mycenaean Greece: Heinrich Schliemann. Mycenaean Greece (or the Mycenaean civilization) was the last phase of the Bronze Age in ancient Greece, spanning the period from approximately 1750 to 1050 BC.

q.p: Who is credited with discovering Anarchist communism?
q.e: Anarchist communism: Peter Kropotkin. Anarchist communism is a far-left political ideology and anarchist school of thought that advocates a form of communism.

q.p: Who is credited with discovering History of artificial intelligence?
q.e: History of artificial intelligence: John McCarthy. The history of artificial intelligence (AI) began in antiquity, with myths, stories, and rumors of artificial beings endowed with intelligence by master craftsmen.

q.p: Who is credited with discovering MeToo movement?
q.e: MeToo movement: Tarana Burke. The phrase "Me Too" was initially used in this context on social media around 2006, on Myspace, by sexual assault survivor and activist Tarana Burke.

q.p: Who is credited with discovering Yamnaya culture?
q.e: Yamnaya culture: Vasily Gorodtsov. It was discovered by Vasily Gorodtsov following his archaeological excavations near the Donets River in 1901–1903.

q.p: Who is credited with discovering Control of fire by early humans?
q.e: Control of fire by early humans: Homo erectus. The control of fire by early humans was a critical technology enabling the evolution of humans.

q.p: Of which country is Pataliputra the capital?
q.e: Pataliputra is the capital of Gupta Empire. The Gupta Empire was an Indian empire during the classical period of the Indian subcontinent which existed from the mid 3rd century to mid 6th century CE.

q.p: Of which country is Sanskrit an official language?
q.e: Sanskrit is an official language of Gupta Empire. The Gupta Empire was an Indian empire during the classical period of the Indian subcontinent which existed from the mid 3rd century to mid 6th century CE.

q.p: Which country uses the gold dinar as its official currency?
q.e: The gold dinar is the official currency of Abbasid Caliphate. The Abbasid Caliphate or Abbasid Empire was the third Islamic caliphate, ruled by the Abbasid dynasty.

q.p: Which country uses the yuan as its official currency?
q.e: The yuan is the official currency of Republic of China (1912–1949). It led the Nationalist government and ruled the ROC as a one-party state with Nanjing as the capital.

q.p: Which country uses the peseta as its official currency?
q.e: The peseta is the official currency of Francoist Spain. It has also been described as Catholic corporatism.

q.p: Which country uses the grivna as its official currency?
q.e: The grivna is the official currency of Novgorod Republic. For much of its history, Novgorod was the center of Russian art and culture.

q.p: Which country uses the Dutch guilder as its official currency?
q.e: The Dutch guilder is the official currency of United Kingdom of the Netherlands. The United Kingdom of the Netherlands is the unofficial but common historiographical name for the Kingdom of the Netherlands as it existed from 1815 to 1839.

q.p: Which country uses the Roman scudo as its official currency?
q.e: The Roman scudo is the official currency of Papal States. At their zenith, the Papal States covered most of the modern Italian regions of Lazio (which includes Rome), Marche, Umbria, Romagna, and portions of Emilia.

q.p: Which country uses the Austro-Hungarian krone as its official currency?
q.e: The Austro-Hungarian krone is the official currency of Kingdom of Hungary. The Kingdom of Hungary was a monarchy in Central Europe that existed for nearly a millennium, from 1000 to 1946.

q.p: Which country uses the Neapolitan piastra as its official currency?
q.e: The Neapolitan piastra is the official currency of Kingdom of Naples. It was established by the War of the Sicilian Vespers (1282–1302).

q.p: Which country uses the Genovino as its official currency?
q.e: The Genovino is the official currency of Republic of Genoa. The Republic of Genoa was a medieval and early modern maritime republic from the years 1099 to 1797 in Liguria on the northwestern Italian coast.

q.p: Which country uses the Spanish maravedí as its official currency?
q.e: The Spanish maravedí is the official currency of Kingdom of Castile. The Kingdom of Castile was a polity in the Iberian Peninsula during the Middle Ages.

q.p: Which country uses the dinar as its official currency?
q.e: The dinar is the official currency of Volga Bulgaria. Volga Bulgaria was a multi-ethnic state with large numbers of Bulgars, Finno-Ugrians, Varangians, and East Slavs.

q.p: Which country uses the Spanish real as its official currency?
q.e: The Spanish real is the official currency of Crown of Castile. In 1492, the voyage of Christopher Columbus and the discovery of the Americas were major events in the history of Castile.

q.p: Which country uses the pound Scots as its official currency?
q.e: The pound Scots is the official currency of Kingdom of Scotland. The Kingdom of Scotland was a sovereign state in northwest Europe, traditionally said to have been founded in 843.

q.p: Which country uses the Korean mun as its official currency?
q.e: The Korean mun is the official currency of Joseon. It was founded by Taejo of Joseon in 1392 and replaced by the Korean Empire in 1897.

q.p: Which country uses the assignat as its official currency?
q.e: The assignat is the official currency of French First Republic. The First Republic lasted until the declaration of the First Empire on 18 May 1804 under Napoléon Bonaparte, although the form of government changed several times.

q.p: Dubbed the "Missile Man of India" for his ballistic-missile work at DRDO and ISRO, this aerospace engineer went on to serve as president from 2002 to 2007 — who was he?
q.e: A. P. J. Abdul Kalam (k-LAHM; 15 October 1931 - 27 July 2015) was an Indian aerospace engineer and statesman who served as the president of India from 2002 to 2007.

q.p: Fill in the blank: “____ (born Henri Marie Joseph Grous; (5 August 1912 - 22 January 2007) was a French Catholic priest.”
q.e: Abbé Pierre (born Henri Marie Joseph Grous; (5 August 1912 - 22 January 2007) was a French Catholic priest.

q.p: The very first child born to Islam's earliest converts, this grandson of caliph Abu Bakr ran a rival caliphate from Mecca against the Umayyads until his death in 692 — who was he?
q.e: Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr (May 624 - October/November 692) was the leader of a caliphate based in Mecca in opposition to the Umayyads during the Second Fitna from 683 until his death in 692.

q.p: Trained as a pediatrician in Egypt, this Palestinian leader co-founded a major militant political movement in 1987 and led its council for a matter of weeks in 2004. Who is he?
q.e: Abdel Aziz al-Rantisi (23 October 1947 - 17 April 2004) was a Palestinian political leader and co-founder of Hamas, along with Sheikh Ahmed Yassin in 1987.

q.p: This Sudanese military officer took control of a transitional military council following the 2019 Sudanese Revolution and has led the country ever since — who is he?
q.e: Abdel Fattah al-Burhan (born 1960) is a Sudanese military officer who has been the leader of Sudan since 2019.

q.p: A retired military officer appointed Minister of Defense in 2012, he has served as Egypt's 6th president since 2014. Who is he?
q.e: Abdel Fattah el-Sisi (born 19 November 1954) is an Egyptian politician and retired military officer who has served as the 6th president of Egypt since 2014.

q.p: This Algerian politician has served as president since 2019, having previously held the post of prime minister for a few months in 2017 — who is he?
q.e: Abdelmadjid Tebboune (Berber languages:; born 17 November 1945) is an Algerian politician currently serving as President and Minister of National Defense of Algeria since 2019.

q.p: Chief of the Nigerien Presidential Guard since 2011, this officer overthrew the sitting president in a 2023 coup and was inaugurated president two years later — who is he?
q.e: Abdourahamane Tchiani (born 1960s) is a Nigerien military officer and politician who has served as president of Niger since 2025.

q.p: This former Minister of Water Resources succeeded Barham Salih as Iraq's head of state in 2022 — who is he?
q.e: Abdul Latif Rashid (born 10 August 1944), also known as Letif Reshid, is an Iraqi politician who served as the president of Iraq from 2022 to 2026.

q.p: This Ottoman sultan succeeded his brother in 1861 during a period of reform and resurgence following the Crimean War, but was overthrown in a government coup in 1876 — who was he?
q.e: Abdulaziz (8 February 1830 - 4 June 1876) was the sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 25 June 1861 to 30 May 1876, when he was overthrown in a government coup.

q.p: In the Book of Genesis, this favored shepherd son was slain by his jealous older brother, becoming the first murder victim in the Bible — who was he?
q.e: Abel (Biblical) is a biblical figure in the Book of Genesis within the Abrahamic religions.

q.p: After rising through Ethiopia's Information Network Security Agency, this former rebel fighter became prime minister in 2018 and later led the Prosperity Party — who is he?
q.e: Abiy Ahmed (born 15 August 1976) is an Ethiopian politician who is the current Prime Minister of Ethiopia since 2018 and the leader of the Prosperity Party since 2019.

q.p: Fill in the blank: “____ is the fifth and current caliph of the Islamic State.”
q.e: Abu Hafs al-Hashimi al-Qurashi is the fifth and current caliph of the Islamic State.

q.p: Raised alongside his companion Patroclus and tutored by the centaur Chiron, this son of a sea nymph was deemed the greatest Greek warrior of the Trojan War — who was he?
q.e: Achilles (-) or Achilleus (Ancient) was a hero of the Trojan War who was known as being the greatest of all the Greek warriors.

q.p: Before becoming his country's Minister of Justice in 2023, this lawyer and human rights activist spent six years serving as Poland's Ombudsman — who is he?
q.e: Adam Bodnar (born 6 January 1977) is a Polish lawyer, educator, human rights activist and politician who served as Minister of Justice from 2023 to 2025.

q.p: First elected to Congress from Illinois in 2010, this representative later became a vocal critic of his own party's attempts to overturn a presidential election result — who is he?
q.e: Adam Kinzinger (born February 27, 1978) is an American politician, political commentator, and former United States Air Force and Air National Guard officer.

q.p: This Islamic call to prayer, traditionally recited by a muezzin from a mosque's minaret, summons Muslims to each of the five daily obligatory prayers. What is it?
q.e: Adhan is the Islamic call to prayer, usually recited by a muezzin, traditionally from the minaret of a mosque, shortly before each of the five obligatory daily prayers.

q.p: Grandson of a 19th-century US vice president, this Illinois governor lost two presidential elections to Dwight Eisenhower before capping his career as UN ambassador — who is he?
q.e: Adlai Stevenson II (February 5, 1900 - July 14, 1965) was an American politician and diplomat who was the United States ambassador to the United Nations from 1961 until his death in 1965.

q.p: This French historian-turned-statesman arranged for Napoleon's remains to be brought home from Saint-Helena and later served as France's second elected president — who is he?
q.e: Adolphe Thiers (tee-AIR; 15 April 1797 - 3 September 1877) was a French statesman and historian who served as President of France from 1871 to 1873.

q.p: In Greek mythology, this king of Mycenae commanded the Achaean forces during the Trojan War and was killed by his wife Clytemnestra upon his return home. Who is he?
q.e: Agamemnon (Ancient) was a king of Mycenae who commanded the Achaeans during the Trojan War.

q.p: A former Indonesian army major turned Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Development, this Democratic Party leader is the son of former president SBY — who is he?
q.e: Agus Harimurti Yudhoyono (born 10 August 1978), commonly referred to as AHY, is an Indonesian politician and former army major who is currently serving as the leader of the Democratic Party.

q.p: Before rising to lead Indonesia's armed forces in 2023, this general served as Chief of Staff of the Army and commander of Kodam III/Siliwangi — who is he?
o: Prince Gustaf Adolf, Duke of Västerbotten
q.e: Agus Subiyanto (born 5 August 1967) is an Indonesian general who is currently serving as the 23rd and incumbent Commander of the Indonesian National Armed Forces.

q.p: Ruling from 1921 until his death in 1950, this sheikh was the tenth in a line of rulers over a Gulf sheikhdom that later became a modern nation — who was he?
q.e: Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah (1885 - 29 January 1950) was the tenth ruler of the Sheikhdom of Kuwait from 29 March 1921 until his death on 29 January 1950.

q.p: This messianic movement arose in British India in the late 19th century after its founder declared himself the promised Messiah and Mahdi — what movement is it?
q.e: Ahmadiyya is an Islamic messianic movement originating in British India in the late 19th century.

q.p: A nearly blind quadriplegic who relied on a wheelchair after a teenage sporting accident, this imam founded Hamas in 1987 and led it until his 2004 assassination — who was he?
q.e: Ahmed Yassin (June 1936/37 - 22 March 2004) was a Palestinian politician and imam who founded Hamas, an Islamist political and military organization.

q.p: This Shia cleric served as Iran's fourth president, led the Assembly of Experts, and famously was the one who chose Ali Khamenei as supreme leader — who was he?
q.e: Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani (n Bahramani; 25 August 1934 - 8 January 2017) was an Iranian Shia cleric and politician who was the fourth president of Iran from 1989 to 1997.

q.p: The son of veteran Uttar Pradesh politician Mulayam Singh, this Samajwadi Party president served as the state's youngest-ever Chief Minister from 2012 to 2017 — who is he?
q.e: Akhilesh Yadav (born 1 July 1973) is an Indian politician and national president of the Samajwadi Party, who served as the 20th Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh from 2012 to 2017.

q.p: This member of the Imperial House of Japan reigned as the 125th emperor from 1989 until his abdication in 2019, with his era named the Heisei era — who is he?
q.e: Akihito (born 23 December 1933) is a member of the Imperial House of Japan who reigned as the 125th emperor of Japan from 7 January 1989 until his abdication on 30 April 2019.

q.p: Fill in the blank: “____ are a Fatah-aligned coalition of Palestinian armed groups in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip.”
q.e: Al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades are a Fatah-aligned coalition of Palestinian armed groups in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip. The al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades have conducted various armed attacks on Israeli military and civilian targets since 2000.

q.p: Responsible for the 1998 US embassy bombings, the USS Cole attack, and the September 11 attacks, this pan-Islamist militant organization sought a global caliphate — name it?
q.e: Al-Qaeda is a pan-Islamist militant organization led by Sunni Islamist jihadists who self-identify as a vanguard spearheading a global Islamist revolution to unite the Muslim world under a supra-national Islamic caliphate.

q.p: Before he resigned a U.S. Senate seat from Minnesota in 2018, this Democrat spent three stints writing and performing on Saturday Night Live — who is he?
q.e: Al Franken (born May 21, 1951) is an American politician, comedian, screenwriter, and actor who served from 2009 until his resignation in 2018 as a United States senator from Minnesota.

q.p: This ancient Iranic nomadic people migrated to the North Caucasus, with some continuing into Europe and North Africa, and are regarded as part of the Sarmatians — name the people?
q.e: Alans were an ancient and medieval Iranic nomadic pastoral people who migrated to what is today the North Caucasus; some continued on to Europe and later North Africa.

q.p: Later profiled in the 2010 book A Company of Heroes, this Easy Company paratrooper served in both World War II and the Korean War, rising to Master Sergeant — who is he?
q.e: Albert Blithe (June 25, 1923 - December 17, 1967) was an American career soldier who served as a private first class with Easy Company, 2nd Battalion, 506th Parachute Infantry Regiment, in the 101st Airborne Division during World War II.

q.p: Nicknamed the 'Knight King' or 'Soldier King' for his role in World War I, this Belgian monarch succeeded his uncle Leopold II to the throne in 1909 — who was he?
q.e: Albert I of Belgium (8 April 1875 - 17 February 1934) was King of the Belgians from 23 December 1909 until his death in 1934.

q.p: An engineer and professor turned president of Peru from 1990 to 2000, this leader cracked down on the Shining Path while building a movement named after himself — who was he?
q.e: Alberto Fujimori (26 July 1938 - 11 September 2024) was a Peruvian politician, professor, and engineer who served as the president of Peru from 1990 to 2000.

q.p: This Italian statesman served five terms as prime minister and pursued a pro-Arab foreign policy before being kidnapped by the Red Brigades in March 1978 — who was he?
q.e: Aldo Moro (23 September 1916 - 9 May 1978) was an Italian statesman and prominent member of Christian Democracy (DC) and its centre-left wing.

q.p: Fill in the blank: “____ (born 16 February 1983) is a Galician publicist and political activist.”
q.e: Alejandra Silva (born 16 February 1983) is a Galician publicist and political activist.

q.p: This former Polish head of state, a onetime communist-era minister turned centre-left leader, helped broker a peaceful resolution to Ukraine's 2004 Orange Revolution — who is he?
q.e: Aleksander Kwaśniewski (born 15 November 1954) is a Polish politician and journalist who served as the 3rd president of Poland from 1995 to 2005.

q.p: A Hero of the Russian Federation since 2019 and a General of the Army, this FSB director sits close to Putin within his inner circle — who is he?
q.e: Alexander Bortnikov (born 15 November 1951) is a Russian intelligence officer who has served as the director of the Federal Security Service (FSB) since 2008.

q.p: Nicknamed 'the Blessed,' he took the Russian throne after his father's murder and steered the empire through the chaos of the Napoleonic Wars. Who was he?
q.e: Alexander I of Russia was Emperor of Russia (1801–1825).

q.p: A polar explorer turned admiral, he declared himself 'Supreme Ruler of Russia' in 1918 and led a White military dictatorship during the Civil War — who is it?
q.e: Alexander Kolchak was Russian admiral and White movement leader (1874–1920).

q.p: This Finnish politician served as prime minister from 2014 to 2015 before becoming president of Finland in 2024, after rising through EU-focused political roles. Who is he?
q.e: Alexander Stubb (born 1 April 1968) is a Finnish politician serving as the president of Finland since 2024.

q.p: This economics professor turned Green Party spokesman became Austria's head of state in 2017, having gained citizenship in 1958 after his family fled occupied Estonia — who is he?
q.e: Alexander Van der Bellen (born 18 January 1944), also referred to by the abbreviation VdB, is an Austrian politician serving as the president of Austria since 2017.

q.p: Born Princess Alix of Hesse, this last empress of Russia drew lasting controversy through her grip on her husband and her bond with the mystic Rasputin — who was she?
q.e: Alexandra Feodorovna (Alix of Hesse) was Empress of Russia from 1894 to 1917.

q.p: A member of the Democratic Socialists of America, this representative for New York's 14th district drew national attention by toppling Caucus chair Joe Crowley — who is she?
q.e: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (born October 13, 1989), also known as AOC, is an American politician and activist who has served since 2019 as the U.S.

q.p: Founder of the Anti-Corruption Foundation, which Russian opposition leader famously branded United Russia the 'party of crooks and thieves' and was named a prisoner of conscience?
q.e: Alexei Navalny (4 June 1976 - 16 February 2024) was a Russian opposition leader, anti-corruption activist and political prisoner.

q.p: Born with haemophilia treated by faith healer Grigori Rasputin, this last heir apparent to the Russian throne was exiled with his family to Siberia in 1917 — who was he?
q.e: Alexei Nikolaevich, Tsarevich of Russia was the last heir apparent to the Russian throne (1904–1918).

q.p: A moderate who often clashed with Lenin, this Bolshevik rose to lead the Soviet government from 1924 before later being tried and purged under Stalin — who is he?
q.e: Alexei Rykov (25 February 1881 - 15 March 1938) was a Russian Bolshevik revolutionary and a Soviet politician and statesman, most prominent as premier of Russia and the Soviet Union from 1924 to 1929 and 1924 to 1930 respectively.

q.p: Which military strongman served as Paraguay's president from 1954 until being overthrown in 1989, having suspended civil rights almost immediately after taking office?
q.e: Alfredo Stroessner (3 November 1912 - 16 August 2006) was a Paraguayan politician, army general, and military dictator who ruled as the 42nd president of Paraguay from 15 August 1954 until his overthrow in 1989.

q.p: Born in April 1967, this Turkish economist-turned-politician served in the 58th through 60th Turkish governments before founding his own party — who is he?
q.e: Ali Babacan (Turkish; born 4 April 1967) is a Turkish politician, economist, and engineer.

q.p: She has led the AfD's parliamentary group in the Bundestag since 2017 and now co-chairs the party with Tino Chrupalla — which German politician is it?
q.e: Alice Weidel (born 6 February 1979) is a German far-right politician who has been serving as co-chairwoman of the far-right, vlkisch nationalist Alternative for Germany (AfD) party alongside Tino Chrupalla since June 2022.

q.p: Founded by a religious reformer recognized by his followers as the Mahdi, which Berber Muslim empire ruled much of the Maghreb and Islamic Spain from 1121 to 1269?
q.e: Almohad Caliphate was a North African empire ruled by a Berber Muslim dynasty in the 12th and 13th centuries that lasted from 1121-1269.

q.p: This founder of Turkey's Nationalist Movement Party also ran training camps for the Grey Wolves from 1968 to 1978 — who is he?
q.e: Alparslan Türkeş (Turkish; 25 November 1917 - 4 April 1997) was a Turkish politician, who was the founder and president of the Nationalist Movement Party (MHP) and the Grey Wolves (lk Ocaklar).

q.p: It ran from 1765 to 1789, transformed thirteen British colonies into a sovereign nation, and reached a decisive military victory in 1781 — what was this political upheaval?
q.e: American Revolution (1765-1789) was a political movement in the Thirteen Colonies of Great Britain.

q.p: This economist-turned-statesman led Iran's government for more than a decade in the 1960s and 70s and also headed a ruling party's secretariat for a time — who is he?
q.e: Amir-Abbas Hoveyda (18 February 1919 - 7 April 1979) was an Iranian economist and politician who served as Prime Minister of Iran from 1965 to 1977 and Secretary-General of the Rastakhiz Party from 1975 to 1976.

q.p: The longest-serving Home Affairs Minister in Indian history, this politician also led the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party as its president from 2014 to 2020 — who is he?
q.e: Amit Shah (born 22 October 1964) is an Indian politician who has served as the 31st Minister of Home Affairs since 2019, the longest-serving holder of the office in Indian history.

q.p: Commandant of the Kraków-Płaszów camp, this Austrian SS officer earned the first-ever homicide conviction at a war crimes trial — who is it?
q.e: Amon Göth (11 December 1908 - 13 September 1946) was an Austrian SS functionary and war criminal.

q.p: First recorded in Sumerian texts around 2500 BC, this Northwest Semitic people built city-states like Mari and Ebla before founding the Old Babylonian Empire — who were they?
q.e: Amorites were an ancient Northwest Semitic-speaking Bronze Age people who emerged from western Mesopotamia.

q.p: Returning to Punjab from Dubai in 2022 to lead an anti-drug campaign, this Sikh preacher went on to win a seat in India's Parliament in 2024 — who is he?
q.e: Amritpal Singh (born 17 January 1993) is an Indian politician, Sikh preacher and pro-Khalistan separatist.

q.p: Recognized as monarch while still a boy living in Switzerland, this king of Siam returned home in 1945 only to die under mysterious circumstances the following year — who was he?
q.e: Ananda Mahidol (20 September 1925 - 9 June 1946) was the eighth king of Siam (later Thailand) from the Chakri dynasty, titled Rama VIII.

q.p: This political philosophy advocates for abolishing authority and hierarchy, and is described as the libertarian wing of the socialist movement. What ideology is this?
q.e: Anarchism is a political philosophy and movement that seeks to abolish all institutions that perpetuate authority, coercion, or hierarchy, primarily targeting the state and capitalism.

q.p: A Bolshevik who served from Lenin through Stalin and Khrushchev all the way to Brezhnev, this Soviet survivor inspired the saying "from Ilyich to Ilyich" — which statesman was he?
q.e: Anastas Mikoyan was Soviet statesman and revolutionary (1895–1978).

q.p: Having led Russia's 1990s privatization drive and later headed the Rusnano technology fund, which economist relocated to Israel in 2022?
q.e: Anatoly Chubais (born 16 June 1955) is a Russian-Israeli politician and economist who was responsible for privatization in Russia as an influential member of Boris Yeltsin's administration in the early 1990s.

q.p: This Russian chess grandmaster reigned as the 12th World Chess Champion from 1975 to 1985, later adding three more FIDE World Championship titles in the 1990s — who is he?
q.e: Anatoly Karpov (born May 23, 1951) is a Russian and former Soviet chess grandmaster, former World Chess Champion, and politician.

q.p: A co-author of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, this legal scholar became the first democratically elected mayor of Saint Petersburg. Who was he?
q.e: Anatoly Sobchak (10 August 1937 - 19 February 2000) was a Russian politician and legal scholar, a co-author of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, and the first democratically elected mayor of Saint Petersburg.

q.p: United around 3150 BC by a ruler called Menes or Narmer, this Nile-valley civilization is considered one of the world's cradles of civilization — name it?
q.e: Ancient Egypt was a cradle of civilization concentrated along the lower reaches of the Nile River in the northeastern corner of Africa.

q.p: Born in the colonial Carolinas and married to Rachel Donelson, this Army general turned seventh U.S. president lent his name to a whole democratic movement — who is he?
q.e: Andrew Jackson (March 15, 1767 - June 8, 1845) was the seventh president of the United States from 1829 to 1837.

q.p: Her name in Ancient Greek roughly means "man battler," fitting for the wife of Troy's greatest warrior, Hector — who is this mythological figure?
q.e: Andromache (Ancient) was the wife of Hector, daughter of Eetion, and sister to Podes.

q.p: Elected in a surprise 2015 upset over the incumbent, who served as Poland's president from 2015 to 2025 after earlier serving in both the national and European parliaments?
q.e: Andrzej Duda (born 16 May 1972) is a Polish lawyer and politician who served as the 6th president of Poland from 2015 to 2025.

q.p: Known by his initials AMLO, this Tabasco-born politician ran Mexico City before serving as the country's 65th president from 2018 to 2024 — who is he?
q.e: Andrés Manuel López Obrador (born 13 November 1953), also known by his initials AMLO, is a Mexican former politician, political scientist, and writer who served as the 65th president of Mexico from 2018 to 2024.

q.p: A Marxist feminist philosopher born in Birmingham, Alabama, this activist twice ran for U.S. Vice President on the Communist Party ticket in the 1980s. Who is she?
q.e: Angela Davis (born January 26, 1944) is an American Marxist and Marxist feminist political activist, philosopher, academic, author and social theorist.

q.p: She earned a doctorate in quantum chemistry in East Germany before politics, then became the first woman — and first East German — to lead her country as Chancellor. Who is she?
q.e: Angela Merkel (ne Kasner; born 17 July 1954) is a German stateswoman and retired politician who served as Chancellor of Germany from 2005 to 2021.

q.p: Rising through Japanese-organized security forces during the occupation, this general became Indonesia's second president, ruling for over three decades until 1998. Who is he?
q.e: Anil Ambani (born 4 June 1959) is an Indian businessman, chairman, and managing director of the Reliance Group.

q.p: Rooted in the Latin word for 'breath' or 'spirit,' this worldview holds that plants, rivers, and even rocks may possess souls or personhood — name it?
q.e: Animism (from) is the world-view or perception that all types of natural phenomena, including non-human organisms and often even landforms and inanimate objects, may possess distinct spiritual essences, souls, or personhood.

q.p: Once co-leader of Alliance 90/The Greens alongside Robert Habeck, she became Germany's foreign minister and then president of the UN General Assembly's 80th session — who is she?
q.e: Annalena Baerbock (born 15 December 1980) is a German diplomat and politician of the Alliance 90/The Greens party.

q.p: First elected in 2014 as the first female mayor in her city's history, this Socialist Party politician launched an urban-renewal program called 'Reinvent Paris' — who is she?
q.e: Anne Hidalgo (born 19 June 1959) is a Spanish-born French politician who served as the Mayor of Paris from 2014 to 2026 and is the first woman to hold the office.

q.p: Married to Henry VIII for barely six months in 1540 before the union was annulled, which German-born noblewoman became his fourth queen?
q.e: Anne of Cleves (28 June or 22 September 1515 - 16 July 1557) was Queen of England as the fourth wife of Henry VIII from 6 January to 12 July 1540.

q.p: Member for the Sydney seat of Grayndler since 1996 and Labor leader since 2019, this economics graduate became his nation's 31st prime minister in 2022. Who is he?
q.e: Anthony Albanese (born 2 March 1963) is an Australian politician who has served as the 31st prime minister of Australia since 2022.

q.p: She makes only a brief appearance in Aeschylus's Seven Against Thebes, yet this daughter of Oedipus became the protagonist of her own eponymous Sophocles tragedy — who is she?
o: Princess Madeleine, Duchess of Hälsingland and Gästrikland
Princess Beatrice of the United Kingdom
q.e: Antigone (ann-; Ancient) was a Theban princess and a character in several ancient Greek tragedies.

q.p: He founded the antisemitic precursor to the Nazi Party and mentored a young Adolf Hitler, only to be pushed out as chairman in a 1921 power struggle — who is he?
q.e: Anton Drexler (13 June 1884 - 24 February 1942) was a German far-right political agitator for the Vlkisch movement in the 1920s.

q.p: The fourth of Rome's 'Five Good Emperors,' this ruler married his predecessor's niece and was adopted as heir shortly before that predecessor's death — who was he?
q.e: Antoninus Pius (19 September 86 - 7 March 161) was Roman emperor from AD 138 to 161.

q.p: Known as the 'Grand Marshal of Ayacucho,' this Venezuelan general and close ally of Simón Bolívar served as Bolivia's president from 1825 to 1828 — who is he?
q.e: Antonio José de Sucre (Spanish; 3 February 1795 - 4 June 1830), known as the "Gran Mariscal de Ayacucho", was a Venezuelan general and politician who served as the president of Bolivia from 1825 to 1828.

q.p: Before becoming Italy's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, this politician served as President of the European Parliament from 2017 to 2019 — who is he?
q.e: Antonio Tajani (Italian; born 4 August 1953) is an Italian politician who has been serving as Deputy Prime Minister of Italy and Minister of Foreign Affairs since 22 October 2022.

q.p: A career diplomat who advocated for the 2003 invasion of Iraq, this man went on to serve as the 71st U.S. secretary of state from 2021 to 2025 — who is he?
q.e: Antony Blinken (born April 16, 1962) is an American lawyer and diplomat who served as the 71st United States secretary of state from 2021 to 2025.

q.p: Before becoming the ninth Secretary-General of the United Nations in 2017, this Portuguese Socialist led his country as prime minister from 1995 to 2002 — who is he?
q.e: António Guterres (born 30 April 1949) is a Portuguese and East Timorese politician and diplomat who, since 2017, has served as the ninth Secretary-General of the United Nations.

q.p: This Malaysian politician became his country's 10th prime minister in 2022 and promptly appointed himself finance minister as well — who is he?
q.e: Anwar Ibrahim (born 10 August 1947) is a Malaysian politician who has served as the 10th prime minister of Malaysia since 2022.

q.p: Symbolized by seashells, doves, and roses, this Greek goddess of love and beauty was worshipped chiefly on Cyprus and Cythera, and became Venus to the Romans — who is she?
q.e: Aphrodite is an ancient Greek goddess associated with love, lust, beauty, pleasure, passion, procreation, and as her syncretised Roman counterpart Venus, desire, sex, fertility, prosperity, and victory.

q.p: The twin brother of Artemis and son of Zeus, this Olympian god of prophecy, music, and archery presided over the famous oracle at Delphi — who is he?
q.e: Apollo is one of the Olympian deities in ancient Greek religion and mythology.

q.p: Lasting from about 800 BC until a Persian invasion in 480 BC, this era saw a massive population boom and the rise of the city-state, or polis — which historical period?
q.e: Archaic Greece was the period in Greek history lasting from c.

q.p: Son of Zeus and Hera, this Greek god embodies the raw brutality and bloodlust of war, standing in contrast to his sister's cooler, more strategic approach to battle — who is he?
q.e: Ares (Ancient) is the Greek god of war and courage.

q.p: Elected to Pakistan's National Assembly in 2013, this dentist-turned-politician later became the country's president, succeeding Mamnoon Hussain in 2018. Who is he?
q.e: Arif Alvi (born 29 July 1949) is a Pakistani politician and former dentist who served as the 13th president of Pakistan from September 2018 to March 2024.

q.p: The third son of Xerxes I, this Persian King of Kings ruled from 465 to 424 BC and appears in Greek sources under a nickname referring to an unusually long limb — who was he?
q.e: Artaxerxes I was the fifth King of Kings of the Achaemenid Empire of Persia, from August 465 to December 424 BC.

q.p: A Franco-German joint venture dedicated to culture, this public channel carries two audio tracks so it can serve viewers in both countries at once — what's it called?
q.e: Arte (Association relative la tlvision europenne, "Association relating to European television") is a European public service channel dedicated to culture.

q.p: This former bureaucrat turned anti-corruption activist won a Ramon Magsaysay Award in 2006, then became the 7th Chief Minister of Delhi — who is he?
q.e: Arvind Kejriwal (Hindi; born 16 August 1968) is an Indian politician, activist and former bureaucrat, who served as the 7th Chief Minister of Delhi.

q.p: Appointed U.S. attorney by Ronald Reagan in 1982, this Republican later served two terms as governor of Arkansas before running for the 2024 presidential nomination — who is he?
q.e: Asa Hutchinson (born December 3, 1950) is an American attorney, businessman, and politician who served as the 46th governor of Arkansas from 2015 to 2023.

q.p: This Indian politician has led the AIMIM party since 2008 and has been elected five times to the Lok Sabha from Hyderabad — who is he?
q.e: Asaduddin Owaisi (born 13 May 1969) is an Indian politician who is serving as the third and current president of the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) since 2008.

q.p: Genesis names this high-born Egyptian as Joseph's wife and the mother of his two sons — who is she?
o: Grand Duchess Tatiana Nikolaevna of Russia
q.e: Asenath (Koine) is a minor figure in the Book of Genesis.

q.p: The last president of Afghanistan before the Taliban takeover in 2021, he held a PhD in cultural anthropology from Columbia University and once taught at Johns Hopkins — who is he?
q.e: Ashraf Ghani (born 19 May 1949) is an Afghan former politician and economist who served as the 8th and last president of Afghanistan from 2014 until his government was overthrown by the Taliban in 2021.

q.p: Falling on the tenth of Muharram, this Islamic day of commemoration is marked by Sunni Muslims with voluntary fasting and recalls the parting of the Red Sea by Moses — what is it?
q.e: Ashura is a day of commemoration in Islam. It occurs annually on the tenth of Muharram, the first month of the Islamic calendar.

q.p: Married to Benazir Bhutto in 1987, this politician later served two separate terms as Pakistan's president, decades apart — who is he?
q.e: Asif Ali Zardari (born 26 July 1955) is a Pakistani politician who has served as the 14th president of Pakistan since 2024.

q.p: Known by the nickname Kráka, this woman of Norse legend is remembered in the sagas as one of Ragnar Lodbrok's wives — who is she?
q.e: Aslaug (Old), also called Aslg, Krka or Kraba, is a figure in Norse mythology who appears in Snorri's Edda, the Vlsunga saga and in the saga of Ragnar Lodbrok as one of his wives.

q.p: Born in Bamako and trained at Mali's Joint Military School, this officer chaired a junta that seized power in 2020 before becoming interim, then elected, head of state — who is he?
q.e: Assimi Goïta (born 1983) is a Malian military officer who has ruled Mali since 2021.

q.p: Blending cultural nationalism with political moderation, this poet and BJP co-founder served as India's PM from 1998 to 2004 after a brief two-week stint in 1996 — who is he?
q.e: Atal Bihari Vajpayee (25 December 1924 - 16 August 2018) was an Indian statesman and a poet who served as the prime minister of India, from 1998 to 2004, and previously for two weeks in 1996.

q.p: Rising through Chile's army to General Chief of Staff, this officer toppled an elected president in 1973 and ran a military dictatorship for 17 years — who was he?
q.e: Augusto Pinochet (25 November 1915 - 10 December 2006) was a Chilean army officer and military dictator who ruled Chile from 1973 to 1990.

q.p: Known as the 'Father of the Nation,' this Burmese independence leader was killed in 1947, months before seeing his country freed from British rule — who is he?
q.e: Aung San (13 February 1915 - 19 July 1947) was a Burmese politician, independence activist and revolutionary.

q.p: Known by the initials ÖVP and led since January 2025 by Christian Stocker, which Christian-democratic bloc holds 51 of 183 seats in Austria's National Council?
q.e: Austrian People's Party is a Christian-democratic and liberal-conservative political party in Austria.

q.p: Composed orally over centuries in an Old Iranian language before being written down in the Sasanian era, this is the foundational scripture corpus of Zoroastrianism — what is it?
q.e: Avesta is the text corpus of religious literature of Zoroastrianism.

q.p: With over 10 million daily visitors and Russia's most popular classifieds, this site is the biggest of its kind in the world — what is it?
q.e: Avito.ru is a Russian classified advertisements website with sections devoted to general goods for sale, jobs, real estate, personals, cars for sale, and services.

q.p: A trained surgeon by profession, this Egyptian-born militant became al-Qaeda's second-ever leader and is considered a chief orchestrator of the September 11 attacks — who is he?
q.e: Ayman al-Zawahiri (19 June 1951 - 31 July 2022) was an Egyptian-born pan-Islamist militant and physician who served as the second general emir of al-Qaeda from June 2011 until his death in July 2022.

q.p: An engineer and inventor, which Indonesian became the first vice president to take the presidency mid-term when he succeeded Suharto in 1998?
q.e: B. J. Habibie (25 June 1936 - 11 September 2019) was an Indonesian statesman, engineer, scientist and inventor who served as the third president of Indonesia from 1998 to 1999.

q.p: This German politician led the Hitler Youth from 1931 to 1940 and later served as Nazi governor of Vienna during World War II — who is he?
q.e: Baldur von Schirach (German; 9 May 1907 - 8 August 1974) was a German politician who was the leader (Reichsjugendfhrer) of the Hitler Youth from 1931 to 1940.

q.p: Founded in San Sebastián in 1919 and reestablished in Paris in 1937 amid the Spanish Civil War, this Spanish luxury fashion house closed in 1968 upon its founder's death — name it?
q.e: Balenciaga (b-) is a Spanish luxury fashion house headquartered in Paris.

q.p: A politician from Illinois who served as the 44th president of the United States from 2009 to 2017, he was the first African American to hold this office. Who is he?
q.e: Barack Obama (born August 4, 1961) is an American politician who served as the 44th president of the United States from 2009 to 2017.

q.p: This Polish politician led the United Left coalition into the 2015 parliamentary election and has headed the Polish Initiative party since 2016 — who is she?
q.e: Barbara Nowacka (born 10 May 1975) is a Polish politician who has served as Minister of National Education since December 2023.

q.p: Elected four times to Karnataka's legislature from Shiggaon, this engineer-turned-politician later served as the state's 17th chief minister — who is he?
q.e: Basavaraj Bommai (born 28 January 1960) is an Indian politician and engineer who is currently serving as the Lok Sabha MP of Haveri and previously served as the 17th Chief Minister of Karnataka from 18 July 2021 to 19 May 2023.

q.p: This short-lived Dutch state, the first of Napoleonic France's 'sister' client states, ended in 1806 when Louis Bonaparte took the Dutch throne — what was it known as?
q.e: Batavian Republic was the successor state to the Republic of the Seven United Netherlands.

q.p: Fought in southern Anatolia on 5 November 333 BC, this clash saw Alexander the Great rout Darius III, who fled leaving behind his family and treasury — which engagement was it?
q.e: Battle of Issus (also Issos) occurred in southern Anatolia, on 5 November 333 BC between the Hellenic League led by Alexander the Great and the Achaemenid (or Persian) Empire, led by Darius III.

q.p: In 751, an Abbasid-Tibetan force defeated Tang China's army for control of territory near the Syr Darya, ending Tang expansion into Central Asia — which clash?
q.e: Battle of Talas (pinyin: Dlus Zhny) was an armed confrontation between the Abbasid Caliphate along with the Tibetan Empire against the Tang dynasty and its allies in 751.

q.p: Crowned in 1951, he was the last Belgian king to be sovereign of the Congo, and in 2024 the Vatican opened a cause for his beatification — who was this monarch?
q.e: Baudouin of Belgium (7 September 1930 - 31 July 1993) was King of the Belgians from 17 July 1951 until his death in 1993.

q.p: He was the principal organizer of the 1963 March on Washington and a leader for civil rights, socialism, nonviolence, and gay rights — which activist is it?
q.e: Bayard Rustin (March 17, 1912 - August 24, 1987) was an American political activist and prominent leader in social movements for civil rights, socialism, nonviolence, and gay rights.

q.p: A former SAS trooper turned wilderness-TV host, in 2009 he became the Scout Association's youngest-ever Chief Scout at age 35 — who is this British adventurer?
q.e: Bear Grylls (born 7 June 1974) is a British adventurer, television presenter and former SAS trooper.

q.p: A federal prosecutor turned Delaware attorney general, this Democrat born in 1969 was the firstborn child of a man who'd become the 46th U.S. president — who was he?
q.e: Beau Biden (February 3, 1969 - May 30, 2015) was an American politician, lawyer, and Army National Guard officer who served as the 44th attorney general of Delaware from 2007 to 2015.

q.p: George Washington trusted this major general enough to hand him command of West Point — which he then schemed to surrender to the British in 1780. Who was the would-be turncoat?
q.e: Benedict Arnold was British military officer (1741–1801).

q.p: Known colloquially as PNoy, this 15th president of the Philippines was the son of an assassinated senator and the 11th president — who was he?
q.e: Benigno Aquino III (locally; February 8, 1960 - June 24, 2021), also known colloquially as PNoy, was the 15th president of the Philippines, serving from 2010 to 2016.

q.p: This Zapotec lawyer became the 26th president of Mexico in 1858, making him the first Indigenous president in the country's history. Who is he?
q.e: Benito Juárez (Latin American; 21 March 1806 - 18 July 1872) was a Mexican politician, military officer, and lawyer who served as the 26th president of Mexico from 1858 until his death in 1872.

q.p: According to rabbinic tradition, this son of Jacob and Rachel was one of only four ancient Israelites said to have died without sin — who is he?
q.e: Benjamin was the younger of the two sons of Jacob and Rachel, and Jacob's twelfth and youngest son overall in Jewish, Christian and Islamic tradition.

q.p: Which one below is best known as a professional footballer?
q.e: Frank Lampard is a professional footballer. Frank James Lampard (born 20 June 1978) is an English football manager and former midfielder who is the manager of Premier League club Coventry City.

q.p: Which of these four is a professional footballer?
q.e: Paul Pogba is a professional footballer. Paul Labile Pogba (born 15 March 1993) is a French professional footballer who plays as a central midfielder for Ligue 1 club Monaco.

q.p: Who among these is a professional footballer?
q.e: Kenny Dalglish is a professional footballer. Sir Kenneth Mathieson Dalglish (born 4 March 1951) is a Scottish former football player and manager.

q.p: Pick the professional footballer from these four.
q.e: Mauro Icardi is a professional footballer. Mauro Emanuel Icardi Rivero (born 19 February 1993) is an Argentine professional footballer who plays as a striker for and captains Süper Lig club Galatasaray.

q.p: Which of these is a professional footballer?
q.e: Billy Gilmour is a professional footballer. Gilmour signed for Italian side Napoli on a permanent deal on deadline day in August 2024, winning the Scudetto in his first season.

q.e: Tyson Fury: Tyson Luke Fury (born 12 August 1988) is a British professional boxer.
