q.e: Chenopodium album is a fast-growing annual plant in the flowering plant family Amaranthaceae.

q.p: Domesticated from the red junglefowl of Southeast Asia about 8,000 years ago, this social bird now numbers over 26.5 billion worldwide — what is it?
q.e: Chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus) is the domesticated form of the red junglefowl (Gallus gallus), originally native to Southeast Asia.

q.p: Its other name is varicella, it spreads through the air, and it tends to hit adults harder than children — which itchy, blister-forming disease is this?
q.e: Chickenpox is a highly contagious disease caused by varicella zoster virus (VZV), a member of the herpesvirus family.

q.p: Known as garbanzo, chana or Bengal gram, this protein-rich legume is mashed into hummus and fried into falafel, with its oldest remains found in Syria — what is it?
q.e: Chickpea (Cicer arietinum) is an annual legume of the family Fabaceae, subfamily Faboideae, cultivated for its edible seeds.

q.p: This woody perennial herb with bright blue flowers is cultivated for salad greens and a root that's roasted and ground as a coffee substitute. What plant is it?
q.e: Chicory (Cichorium intybus) is a somewhat woody, perennial herbaceous plant of the family Asteraceae, usually with bright blue flowers, rarely white or pink.

q.p: Along with the bonobo, which great ape of equatorial Africa's forests and savannas is humans' closest living relative, according to DNA and fossil evidence?
q.e: Chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes), also simply known as the chimp, is a medium-sized great ape species found in the forests and savannas of equatorial Africa.

q.p: Atomic number 17, this strongly oxidising yellow-green gas sits between fluorine and bromine on the periodic table — what element is it?
q.e: Chlorine is a chemical element; it has symbol Cl and atomic number 17.

q.p: A sweet-smelling, dense, colorless liquid with the formula CHCl3, this solvent doubled as an inhaled anesthetic from the 19th century into the early 20th. What is it?
q.e: Chloroform (often abbreviated as TCM), is an organochloride with the formula CHCl3 and a common solvent.

q.p: This plant-cell organelle uses chlorophyll pigments to capture sunlight and convert it into chemical energy, ultimately producing sugar via the Calvin cycle — what is it?
q.e: Chloroplast (-plahst) is a type of organelle known as a plastid that conducts photosynthesis mostly in plant and algal cells.

q.p: Often preceded by a gallbladder attack and typically caused by a gallstone lodging in the cystic duct, which condition can progress to complications like gallstone pancreatitis?
q.e: Cholecystitis is inflammation of the gallbladder. Often gallbladder attacks (biliary colic) precede acute cholecystitis.

q.p: The principal sterol of all animals, it concentrates in the brain and spinal cord and is essential to every cell membrane — yet too much in the blood spells trouble. What is it?
q.e: Cholesterol is the principal sterol of all animals, distributed in body tissues, especially the brain and spinal cord, and in animal fats and oils.

q.p: This class of jawed fish — including sharks and rays — has a skeleton made almost entirely of cartilage, setting it apart from its bony-skeletoned relatives. What class is this?
q.e: Chondrichthyes (from Ancient Greek (khndros) 'cartilage' and (ikhths) 'fish') is a class of jawed fish that contains the cartilaginous fish or chondrichthyans, which all have skeletons primarily composed of cartilage.

q.p: Defined by a hollow dorsal nerve cord, an endostyle, and a post-anal tail at some point in life, this phylum spans vertebrates, tunicates, and lancelets alike — which option fits?
q.e: Chordate is a bilaterian animal belonging to the phylum Chordata (kor-).

q.p: Originating in Northern China, this spitz-type dog breed is known for a dense double coat that forms a distinctive ruff around the neck — name the breed?
q.e: Chow Chow is a spitz-type of dog breed originally from Northern China.

q.p: Besides identifying the laws of elastic collision, this Dutch polymath studied Saturn's rings and improved the design of the telescope — who is he?
q.e: Christiaan Huygens (14 April 1629 - 8 July 1695) was a Dutch mathematician, physicist, engineer, astronomer, and inventor who is regarded as a key figure in the Scientific Revolution.

q.p: The first element in group 6, it lends its name to the shiny plating on car bumpers and, mixed into steel, makes it stainless. Which steely-grey metal is it?
q.e: Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.

q.p: Linked to repeated head trauma, this worsening neurodegenerative disease turns up in boxers and footballers — and even in soccer players, largely from heading the ball. What is it?
q.e: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) is a neurodegenerative disease linked to repeated trauma to the head. The encephalopathy symptoms can include behavioral problems, mood problems, and problems with thinking.

q.p: Grown for blue-flowered roadside roots that become a coffee substitute, or for bitter salad leaves like escarole and radicchio, which plant genus covers both chicory and endive?
q.e: Cichorium is a genus of plants in the tribe Cichorieae within the family Asteraceae.

q.p: A notorious household nuisance pest that feeds on sleeping humans, this insect has never been shown to actually transmit disease to people — what is it?
q.e: Cimex lectularius is a species of Cimicidae.

q.p: This roughly 24-hour internal biological cycle, generated within an organism but tuned by cues like daylight, is regulated by an internal biological clock — what is it called?
q.e: Circadian rhythm is a natural oscillation that repeats roughly every 24 hours.

q.p: This small, lean, mostly nocturnal mammal native to tropical Asia and Africa is often called a 'cat' in its common nickname, despite not actually being a cat at all — what is it?
q.e: Civet is a small, lean, mostly nocturnal mammal native to tropical Asia and Africa, especially the tropical forests.

q.p: This common name covers many species of bivalve mollusc that use a powerful foot to burrow into sand or mud, with two equal shells joined by adductor muscles — what creature is it?
q.e: Clam is a common name for several species of bivalve mollusc. In culinary usage, clams are commonly eaten marine bivalves, as in clam digging and the resulting soup, clam chowder.

q.p: After serving as dean of Harvard's Faculty of Arts and Sciences, this political scientist became the university's 30th president in July 2023 — who is she?
q.e: Claudine Gay (born August 4, 1970) is an American political scientist who is the Wilbur A. Cowett Professor of Government and of African and African-American Studies at Harvard University.

q.p: This anatomical term for the hollow between a woman's breasts was coined in its modern sense by a Hollywood censor reviewing the 1943 film starring Jane Russell — what is the term?
q.e: Cleavage (breasts) is the narrow depression or hollow between the breasts of a woman.

q.p: This tangor — a mandarin-orange cross — typically splits into seven to fourteen easy-to-peel segments — which fruit?
q.e: Clementine (Citrus clementina) is a tangor, a citrus fruit hybrid between a willowleaf mandarin orange (C. deliciosa) and a sweet orange (C. sinensis).

q.p: Once home to a bacterium behind a common cause of diarrhea before its 2016 reclassification, this genus of soil-dwelling bacteria also causes botulism — which genus?
q.e: Clostridium is a genus of anaerobic, Gram-positive bacteria.

q.p: Its Latin genus name literally means three-leaf, and this herbaceous legume, native to Europe, now grows worldwide in around 300 species — what plant is it?
q.e: Clover are plants of the genus Trifolium (from Latin tres 'three' and folium 'leaf').

q.p: Its glorious blue in glass and paint was long wrongly blamed on bismuth, and frustrated miners named its ore after a goblin. Which hard, gray element carries the symbol Co?
q.e: Cobalt is a chemical element; it has symbol Co and atomic number 27.

q.p: Mostly belonging to the genus Naja, these venomous snakes are known for rearing upward and flaring a distinctive hood when threatened — name this common snake type?
q.e: Cobra is the common name of various venomous snakes, most of which belong to the genus Naja.

q.p: Once a standard topical anesthetic prized for narrowing blood vessels, this tropane alkaloid is extracted from the leaves of South American coca plants — which substance is it?
q.e: Cocaine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant and tropane alkaloid, derived primarily from the leaves of two coca species native to South America.

q.p: Domed-backed little beetles that mostly hunt aphids, they wear aposematic spots to warn off predators and are named for 'lady' Mary — what's the scientific family?
q.e: Coccinellidae is a widespread family of small beetles.

q.p: A scale insect native to tropical and subtropical parts of the Americas that lives on prickly-pear cacti, this parasite is the source of the natural dye carmine — which insect?
q.e: Cochineal (-eel, US also, -eel; Dactylopius coccus) is a scale insect in the suborder Sternorrhyncha, from which the natural dye carmine is derived.

q.p: Whose larvae track down plant roots to eat by sensing both leaf-released volatiles and carbon dioxide, in a European scarab species also known as the Maybeetle?
q.e: Cockchafer (Melolontha melolontha), also colloquially known as the Maybug, Maybeetle, or doodlebug, is a species of scarab beetle belonging to the genus Melolontha.

q.p: Found naturally in the sap of the opium poppy and a prodrug of morphine, which opiate treats mild-to-moderate pain and is often paired with paracetamol?
q.e: Codeine is an opiate and prodrug of morphine mainly used to treat pain, coughing, and diarrhea.

q.p: Native to Africa, Arabia and India, this semi-succulent herb smells like oregano and is known by names like Spanish thyme and Mexican mint — which plant?
q.e: Coleus amboinicus is a species of semi-succulent perennial plant in the family Lamiaceae.

q.p: This digestive condition refers to swelling or inflammation of the large intestine, and can be acute and short-lived or a long-term, chronic issue — what is it called?
q.e: Colitis is swelling or inflammation of the large intestine (colon). It broadly fits into the category of digestive diseases.

q.p: Part of the same species as cabbage and broccoli, this loose-leafed member of the 'kale group' has been grown for its big, dark-green leaves since classical antiquity — what is it?
q.e: Collard (plant) is a group of loose-leafed cultivars of Brassica oleracea (the same species as many common vegetables, including cabbage and broccoli).

q.p: In mathematics, this term describes a selection of items from a set in which the order of choosing doesn't matter — unlike its counterpart, the permutation. Name the concept?
q.e: Combination is a selection of items from a set that has distinct members, such that the order of selection does not matter (unlike permutations).

q.p: Native to Asia but so invasive in Australian cities that it was dubbed 'Most Important Pest/Problem' in 2008, which urban-adapted bird species is this?
q.e: Common myna (Acridotheres tristis), sometimes spelled mynah, is a bird in the family Sturnidae, native to Asia.

q.p: Scholars still argue whether it merely transmits meaning or also creates it, but the simplest definition of this concept is the transmission of information — what is it?
q.e: Communication is commonly defined as the transmission of information.

q.p: With algorithms and data structures at its core and the theory of computation among its branches, which field studies computation, information, and automation?
q.e: Computer science is the study of computation, information, and automation. The theory of computation concerns abstract models of computation and general classes of problems that can be solved using them.

q.p: Known in the US as 'konk,' this sea snail's family includes so-called 'true' species identified by their long spires — what is it?
q.e: Conch is any of a number of different medium-to-large-sized sea snails.

q.p: This bird's name comes from the Quechua word 'kuntur,' and its California-dwelling relative was nearly wiped out by habitat loss — which giant vulture soars over the Andes?
q.e: Condor is the common name for two genera of New World vultures, each with one extant species.

q.p: This group of mostly evergreen, cone-bearing trees and shrubs reproduces via wind-pollination, with the seeds themselves also scattered by the wind — what plant group is it?
q.e: Conifer are a group of vascular plants and a subset of gymnosperms.

q.p: This highly poisonous member of the carrot family can grow to nearly 8 feet tall, with hollow, maroon-spotted stems and a famously unpleasant odor — what plant is it?
q.e: Conium maculatum (British English) or poison hemlock (in North America), is a highly poisonous flowering plant and a nitrophile weed species in the carrot family Apiaceae.

q.p: Known by a colorful nickname, this inflammation of the clear layer over the white of the eye turns it pink, may leave it stuck shut by morning, and spreads easily — what is it?
q.e: Conjunctivitis is inflammation of the conjunctiva, the thin and clear layer that covers the white surface of the eye and the inner eyelid.

q.p: This common bowel condition causes hard, dry stools passed fewer than three times a week, sometimes leading to hemorrhoids or fissures — what is it?
q.e: Constipation is a bowel dysfunction that makes bowel movements infrequent or hard to pass.

q.p: Entering service with Strategic Air Command in 1960, this four-engine, delta-wing supersonic bomber was the first in the world capable of Mach 2 — name the aircraft?
q.e: Convair B-58 Hustler is a supersonic strategic bomber, the first capable of Mach 2 flight. To achieve the high speeds desired, Convair chose a delta wing design used by contemporary interceptors such as the Convair F-102.

q.p: Lending its metal to sterling silver, cupronickel coins, and strain-gauge alloys, this element carries atomic number 29 and a name drawn from the Latin 'cuprum' — what is it?
q.e: Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum) and atomic number 29.

q.p: A genus of over 260 fungi, most of them parasites that bore into insects and other arthropods, this 'club-headed' organism has 1,500 years of use in Chinese medicine — what is it?
q.e: Cordyceps is a genus of ascomycete fungi (sac fungi) that includes over 260 species worldwide, many of which are parasitic.

q.p: This fungal plant disease disfigures maize with galls, yet in Mexican cuisine the infected kernels are prized as huitlacoche, a filling for quesadillas and soups — which disease?
q.e: Corn smut is a plant disease caused by the pathogenic fungus Mycosarcoma maydis, synonym Ustilago maydis.

q.p: This transparent dome covering the iris and pupil provides about two-thirds of the eye's total focusing power and can be reshaped via LASIK surgery — what is it?
q.e: Cornea is the transparent front part of the eye which covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber.

q.p: This group of related RNA viruses causes respiratory illnesses ranging from the mild common cold to deadly diseases like SARS, MERS, and COVID-19 — what's this virus family called?
q.e: Coronavirus are a group of related RNA viruses that cause diseases in mammals and birds.

q.p: Made up of subregions called the genu, rostrum, trunk, and splenium, this thick nerve tract lets the brain's two hemispheres communicate — what is it?
q.e: Corpus callosum (Latin for "tough body"), also callosal commissure, is a wide, thick nerve tract, consisting of a flat bundle of commissural fibers, beneath the cerebral cortex in the brain.

q.p: What's the statistical term for the extent to which two variables are linearly related — famously not the same thing as causation?
q.e: Correlation is a type of statistical relationship between two random variables or bivariate data.

q.p: Which genus of passerine birds, whose Latin name literally means 'raven,' includes about 46 species commonly known as crows, ravens, and rooks?
q.e: Corvus is a widely distributed genus of passerine birds ranging from medium-sized to large-sized in the family Corvidae.

q.p: Native to Europe and Western Asia, this birch-family shrub produces the round nuts sold commercially as hazelnuts — which species?
q.e: Corylus avellana is a species of flowering plant in the birch family Betulaceae.

q.p: Derived from Greek words meaning universe and study of, this scientific and philosophical field examines the nature of existence at the grandest scale — what is it called?
q.e: Cosmology (from Ancient Greek (cosmos) 'the universe, the world' and - (logia) 'study of') is the study of the nature of the universe, the cosmos.

q.p: Going by puma, mountain lion, catamount, and panther depending on the region, this big cat is the most widely distributed wild land mammal in the Western Hemisphere — what is it?
q.e: Cougar (Puma concolor), also called puma, mountain lion, catamount, and panther, is a large feline native to the Americas.

q.p: Which vanilla-scented, benzopyrone lactone compound acts as a plant's chemical defense against predators and, via its derivatives, gave rise to the anticoagulant warfarin?
q.e: Coumarin is an aromatic organic chemical compound with formula C9H6O2.

q.p: Tolerant of poor, sandy soil, this legume was domesticated in Africa millennia ago and is now grown far more in Nigeria and Niger than anywhere else on Earth — which crop?
q.e: Cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) is an annual herbaceous legume from the genus Vigna.

q.p: Belonging to the same genus as poliovirus and echovirus, these enteroviruses enter cells with help from a shared receptor and commonly cause aseptic meningitis — which pathogens?
q.e: Coxsackievirus are a few related enteroviruses that belong to the Picornaviridae family of nonenveloped, linear, positive-sense, single-stranded, RNA viruses, as well as its genus Enterovirus, which also includes poliovirus and echovirus.

q.p: Native to North America and smaller than its close relative the gray wolf, this canine fills a similar ecological niche to the golden jackal of Eurasia — which animal?
q.e: Coyote (Canis latrans) is a species of canine also known as the American jackal, prairie wolf, and brush wolf.

q.p: This trailing evergreen vine produces a tart berry that starts light green and turns bright red as it ripens on low, creeping stems. What fruit is it?
q.e: Cranberry are a group of evergreen dwarf shrubs or trailing vines in the subgenus Oxycoccus of the genus Vaccinium.

q.p: Which compound acts as a cellular buffer and, via its phosphorylated form, hands phosphate groups back to ADP to recharge ATP in muscle and brain?
q.e: Creatine (or) is an organic compound that, in vertebrates, facilitates recycling of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), primarily in muscle and brain tissue.

q.p: Affecting roughly 1 in 22,000 births and more common in girls, which genetic condition caused by a chromosome 5 deletion takes its French name from a feline-sounding cry?
q.e: Cri du chat syndrome is a rare genetic disorder due to a partial chromosome deletion on chromosome 5.

q.p: These echinoderms come in stalked "sea lily" and free-swimming "feather star" forms, with mouths on their upper surface ringed by feeding arms — what class of marine animal is it?
q.e: Crinoid are marine invertebrates that make up the class Crinoidea.

q.p: Together with birds, this order of predatory reptiles is one of only two survivors of the ancient Archosauria — and it lumps together alligators, caimans, and gharials. What is it?
q.e: Crocodilia is an order of semiaquatic, predatory reptiles that are known as crocodilians.

q.p: This breaded, deep-fried snack binds a thick sauce like béchamel with fillings such as meat, seafood, or cheese, and was originally a way to use up leftovers — what is it?
q.e: Croquette is a deep-fried roll originating in French cuisine and most extended in Spanish cuisine consisting of a thick binder combined with a filling, which is then breaded.

q.p: Usually viral and often worse at night, this childhood respiratory infection swells the windpipe to produce a barking, brassy cough and noisy breathing — what's the condition?
q.e: Croup (KROOP; from southeastern Scots, prob.

q.p: Mostly aquatic mandibulate arthropods, this group spans shrimp, crayfish, copepods, and barnacles — and modern science now files insects in alongside them — what are they?
q.e: Crustacean (from Latin word "crustacea" meaning: "those with shells" or "crusted ones") are mandibulate arthropods that are traditionally a part of the paraphyletic subphylum Crustacea.

q.p: This bird family, the sole one in its taxonomic order, includes roadrunners, koels, malkohas, and coucals across roughly 150 species. Name the family?
q.e: Cuckoo are birds in the family Cuculidae, the sole taxon in the order Cuculiformes.

q.p: A creeping vine of the gourd family that originated across Asia from India to Yunnan, this annual comes in slicing, pickling, and seedless types — what is it?
q.e: Cucumber (Cucumis sativus) is a widely-cultivated creeping vine plant in the family Cucurbitaceae that bears cylindrical to spherical fruits, used as culinary vegetables.

q.p: Bottle gourds, bitter melon, and the fibrous fruit that gives us loofah sponges are all members of which roughly 965-species plant family?
q.e: Cucurbitaceae (kew-), also called cucurbits or the gourd family, are a plant family consisting of about 965 species in 101 genera.

q.p: The third most-produced American fighter of the Second World War, trailing only the Mustang and the Thunderbolt, this plane first took flight in 1938 — which aircraft?
q.e: Curtiss P-40 Warhawk is an American single-engined, single-seat, all-metal fighter-bomber that first flew in 1938.

q.p: This bluish-purple discoloration of the skin, most visible on the lips, nail beds, and ear lobes, signals a drop in oxygen bound to hemoglobin in the blood — name the condition?
q.e: Cyanosis is the change of tissue color to a bluish-purple hue, as a result of decrease in the amount of oxygen bound to the hemoglobin in the red blood cells of the capillary bed.

q.p: This transdisciplinary field studies circular causal processes like feedback and recursion, where an action's outcome becomes the input for the next — what field is it?
q.e: Cybernetics is the transdisciplinary study of circular causal processes such as feedback and recursion, where the outcomes of actions return as inputs for subsequent actions.

q.p: Grown from tubers and known by the folk name 'sowbread,' this Primulaceae genus features flowers with distinctively upswept petals — which plant genus?
q.e: Cyclamen is a genus of 25 species of perennial flowering plants in the family Primulaceae.
